It is similar to 1.A.16.2.7, two proteins that are are 74% identical to each other). 3-D structures have been elucidated (PDB# 7E26 and 7E27). It is essential and druggable In vivo (Davies et al. 2023).

1.A.16.3.3.description: Hydrosulfide (hydrogen sulfide; HS-), Fnt3 (Hsc) channel. Also probably transports chloride, formate and nitrite. The 3-d crystal structure (2.2Å resolution in the closed state) is known (PDB# 3TE2) (Czyzewski and Wang, 2012). The Fnt3 gene is linked to the asrABC operon encoding the sulfite (SO32-) reductase that gives HS- as the product (Czyzewski and Wang 2012).

1.A.16.3.5.description: Formate channel of 283 aas and 6 TMSs, Fnt or FdhC. Its function has been veritifed (Helmstetter et al. 2019).

1.A.17.1.19.description: Increased sodium tolerance protein, Ist2, of 946 aas and 7 TMSs. Ist2 is an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident transmembrane protein that mediates associations between the plasma membrane (PM) and the cortical ER (cER) in baker's yeast (Kralt et al. 2015).

1.A.17.1.2.description: Anoctamin 1, isoform b (Gnathodiaphyseal dysplasia 1 protein homologue) (39% identical to Anoctamin 1a) (Planells-Cases and Jentsch, 2009). See also Xu et al. 2015.

1.A.17.1.20.description: Anoctamin 3, ANO3 or TMEM16C or KCNT1/Slack, of 981 aas and 9 putative TMSs. 1.A.17.1.21.name: Ano5 (GDD1, TMEM16E), of 913 aas and 10 TMSs, is an intracellular calcium-activated chloride channel in the endoplasmic reticulum.
1.A.17.1.21.description: Ano5 (GDD1, TMEM16E), of 913 aas and 10 TMSs, is an intracellular calcium-activated chloride channel in the endoplasmic reticulum. It positively modulates bone homeostasis via calcium signaling in GDD (Li et al. 2022), and is associated with bone fragility, limb girdle muscular dystrophy type 2L (LGMD2L), Miyoshi myopathy type 3 (MMD3), and gnathodiaphyseal dysplasia 1 (GDD1) in humans (Jin et…

1.A.17.1.22.name: Subdued, a calcium-activated chloride channel of 1075 aas.
1.A.17.1.22.description: Subdued, a calcium-activated chloride channel of 1075 aas. Functions in conjunction with the thermo-TRPs in thermal nociception. Subdued channels may amplify the nociceptive neuronal firing that is initiated by thermo-TRP channels in response to thermal stimuli (Jang et al. 2015). It may also act on phospholipids to transport or hydrolyze them (Le et al. 2019).

1.A.17.1.28.description: Anoctamin1, Ano1, TMEM16A of 979 aas and 10 TMSs. It is probably an anion (Cl-) cannel. Fertilization activates TMEM16A channels in X. laevis eggs and induces the earliest known event triggered by fertilization: the fast block to polyspermy (Wozniak et al. 2018).

1.A.17.1.3.name: TMEM16B (Anoctamin-2, ANO2) anion channel.
1.A.17.1.3.description: TMEM16B (Anoctamin-2, ANO2) anion channel. Exists in the membrane as a homodimer where the cytoplasmic N-terminus functions in dimerization (Tien et al. 2013). TMSs 5-6 may comprise parts of the pore-loop that controls Cl- conductance (Adomaviciene et al. 2013). TMEM16A and TMEM16B are differentially expressed during development in the olfactory epithelium of the mouse (Maurya and Menini 2014).

1.A.17.1.32.description: Anoctamin 1 of 1008 aas and 9 putative TMSs. Salinity and prolactin regulate anoctamin 1 in the model teleost, Fundulus heteroclitus (Breves et al. 2024).

1.A.17.1.33.description: Anoctamin-1 (Ano1) isoform X1 of 990 aas and 9 TMSs. It is a calcium-activated chloride channel (Konno et al. 2025).

1.A.17.1.5.description: Anoctamin-9 (Transmembrane protein 16J) (Tumor protein p53-inducible protein 5) (p53-induced gene 5 protein). It promotes pancreatic tumorigenesis (Jun et al. 2017).

1.A.17.1.9.description: Anoctamin, Anoh-1 of 822 aas. Functions in a sensory mode-specific manner. Present inamphid sensory neurons to detect external chemical and nociceptive cues (Wang et al. 2013).

The crystal structure of the N-terminal hydrophilic domain has been determined to 2.3 Å resolution (Hattori et al., 2007) (>50% identical to 9.A.19.1.1), while the C-terminal transmembrane domain has been determined at 2.2 Å resolution (Takeda et al. 2014). The structure reveals a homodimer with the channel at the interface of the two subunits. There is a plug helix…

1.A.26.1.3.name: The MgtE Mg2+ transporter.
1.A.26.1.3.description: The MgtE Mg2+ transporter. Its expression can compensate a TrpM7 deficiency in vertebrate B-cells (Sahni et al. 2012).

1.A.26.1.6.name: MgtE homologue of 469 AAs and 5 OR 6 TMSs.
1.A.26.1.6.description: MgtE homologue of 469 AAs and 5 OR 6 TMSs (Pohland and Schneider 2019).

1.A.26.1.7.name: Ferrous iron and cobalt importer, FicI, of 454 aas and 5 C-termnal TMSs.
1.A.26.1.7.description: Ferrous iron and cobalt importer, FicI, of 454 aas and 5 C-termnal TMSs. FicI may be a secondary, energy-dependent carrier for iron uptake by S. oneidensis under high Fe2+ concentrations, but it can also take up cobalt (Bennett et al. 2018).

1.A.26.2.1.name: Mg2+ transporter, SLC41A1 (10 TMSs; N- and C-termini inside).
1.A.26.2.1.description: Mg2+ transporter, SLC41A1 (10 TMSs; N- and C-termini inside) (Wabakken et al., 2003; Schmitz et al., 2007; Kolisek et al., 2008; Sponder et al. 2013). It has been reported to be a Na+:Mg2+ antiporter and therefore a Mg2+ efflux pump (Fleig et al. 2013). Regulated by Mg2+-dependent endosomal recycling through its N-terminal cytoplasmic domain (Mandt et al., 2011). Mutations result in a…

1.A.26.2.2.name: Mg2+ transporter, SLC41A2 (11 TMSs with the N-terminus out and the C-terminus in). (63% identical to SLC41A1) See also
1.A.26.2.2.description: Mg2+ transporter, SLC41A2 (11 TMSs with the N-terminus out and the C-terminus in) (Sahni et al. 2007). (63% identical to SLC41A1) See also (Wabakken et al., 2003; Schmitz et al., 2007)

1.A.26.2.3.name: Solute carrier protein (SLC) 41A3.
1.A.26.2.3.description: Solute carrier protein (SLC) 41A3. The gene is upregulated when mice are given a Mg2+ deficient diet (de Baaij et al. 2013). SLC41A3 knockout mice develop abnormal locomotor coordination. It is an established Mg2+ transporter involved in mitochondrial Mg2+ homeostasis (Schäffers et al. 2018).

1.A.26.2.4.name: MagT or MgtE of 503 aas and 12 TMSs in a 3 + 6 + 3 arrangement.
1.A.26.2.4.description: MagT or MgtE of 503 aas and 12 TMSs in a 3 + 6 + 3 arrangement. According to CDD, the domain order is: MgtE_N, a CBS pair (two repeats) and an MgtE domain.

1.A.28.1.1.name: Kidney vasopressin regulated urea transporter, UT-A2 (splice variant of UT-A1)
1.A.28.1.1.description: Kidney vasopressin regulated urea transporter, UT-A2 (splice variant of UT-A1)

1.A.28.1.2.description: Frog urinary bladder ADH-regulated urea transporter

1.A.28.1.3.name: Kidney urea transporter, UT-A1, of 414aas and 11 TMSs in a 5 + 5 + 1 TMS arrangement.
1.A.28.1.3.description: Kidney urea transporter, UT-A1, of 414aas and 11 TMSs in a 5 + 5 + 1 TMS arrangement. It mediates transepithelial urea transport in the inner medullary collecting duct for urinary concentration. Interacts with the C-terminus of Snapin (O95295) and SNARE-associated protein) (Mistry et al., 2007). Also transports formamide, acetamide, methylurea, methylformamide, ammonium carbamate, and acrylamide…

1.A.28.1.4.name: THe urea transporter channel protein of 337 aas and 11 TMSs in an apparent 6 + 5 TMS arrangement.
1.A.28.1.4.description: THe urea transporter channel protein of 337 aas and 11 TMSs in an apparent 6 + 5 TMS arrangement. The 3-d structure (2.3 Å resolution) is available (Levin et al., 2009). Urea binding and flux as well as dimethylurea (DMU) transport have been modeled (Zhang et al. 2017).

1.A.28.1.5.name: Urea transporter 1 or UT-B1 (Kidd Blood Group Antigen; Solute carrier family 14 member 1; Urea transporter of the erythrocyte).
1.A.28.1.5.description: Urea transporter 1 or UT-B1 (Kidd Blood Group Antigen; Solute carrier family 14 member 1; Urea transporter of the erythrocyte) (Bagnasco 2006). A phenylphthalazine compound, PU1424, is a potent UT-B inhibitor, inhibiting human and mouse UT-B-mediated urea transport with IC50 values of 0.02 and 0.69 mumol/L, respectively, and exerted 100% UT-B inhibition at high concentrations (Ran et al. 2016)…

1.A.28.1.6.name: Urea transporter 2, UT2, HUT2 or UTB (Solute carrier family 14 member 2) (Urea transporter, kidney).
1.A.28.1.6.description: Urea transporter 2, UT2, HUT2 or UTB (Solute carrier family 14 member 2) (Urea transporter, kidney). Knocking out both UT1 and UT2 increases urine output 3.5-fold and lowers urine osmolarity (Jiang et al. 2016). The double knockout also lowered blood pressure and promoted maturation of the male reproductive system. Thus, functional deficiency of all UTs causes a urea-selective urine-concentrating…

1.A.28.1.7.name: Putative urea transporter of 306 aas and 9 or 10 TMSs
1.A.28.1.7.description: Putative urea transporter of 306 aas and 9 or 10 TMSs

1.A.28.2.1.name: The dimeric urea transporter, Utp of 300 aas and 9 or probably 10 TMSs.
1.A.28.2.1.description: The dimeric urea transporter, Utp of 300 aas and 9 or probably 10 TMSs. Urea flux is saturable, could be inhibited by phloretin, and was not affected by pH (Raunser et al., 2009)

1.A.30.1.1.name: The flagellar motor (pmf-dependent) (MotA-MotB).
1.A.30.1.1.description: The flagellar motor (pmf-dependent) (MotA-MotB). TMSs 3 and 4 of MotA and the single TMS of MotB comprise the proton channel, which is inactive until the complex assembles into a motor. Hosking et al. 2006 identify a periplasmic segment of the MotB protein that acts as a plug to prevent premature proton flow. The plug is in the periplasm just C-terminal to the MotB TMS flanked by Pro52 and Pro65…
1.A.30.1.1.proteins: MotA and MotB of E. coli

1.A.30.1.2.name: The flagellar motor (smf-dependent) (PomAB; MotXY).
1.A.30.1.2.description: The flagellar motor (smf-dependent) (PomAB; MotXY) (Okabe et al., 2005). PomB interacts with the third TMS of PomA in the Na+-driven polar flagellum (Yakushi et al. 2004). Sodium-powered stators of the flagellar motor can generate torque in the presence of the sodium channel blocker, phenamil, with mutations near the peptidoglycan-binding region of PomB (Ishida et al. 2019). FliL associates with…
1.A.30.1.2.proteins: PomAB/MotXY of Vibrio alginolyticus; PomA (O06873); PomB (O06874); MotX (BAB63401); MotY (BAA12313)

1.A.30.1.5.proteins: The H+-driven flagellar motor complex of Shewanella oneidensis; MotA (Q8E9J0); MotB (Q8E9J1); MotX (Q8EAG6); MotY (D4ZJA6)

1.A.30.1.7.name: The motor complex of the bacterial flagellum, MotAB.
1.A.30.1.7.description: The motor complex of the bacterial flagellum, MotAB. MotA is 295 aas long with about 5 putative TMSs in a 2 + 1 + 2 TMS arrangement, possibly with a C-terminal additional TMS. MotB is 309 aas long with a single N-terminal TMS. They comprise the stator element of the flagellar motor complex and are required for rotation of the flagellar motor. Together they form the transmembrane proton channel…
1.A.30.1.7.proteins: MotAB of Salmonella enterica, subspecies Typhimurium

1.A.30.2.1.description: The TonB energy-transducing system. ExbB/D (the putative H+ channel) are listed here; TonB is listed under TC# 2.C.1.1.1. Deletion of the cytoplasmic loop gives rise to immediate growth arrest (Bulathsinghala et al. 2013). The rotational surveillance and energy transfer (ROSET) model of TonB action postulates a mechanism for the transfer of energy from the IM to the OM, triggering iron uptake and…
1.A.30.2.1.proteins: The TonB system of E. coli; ExbB (P0ABU7); ExbD (P0ABV2)

1.A.30.2.10.name: Putative biopolymer transport proteins ExbB/ExbD-like 3 (Sll1404/Sll1405).
1.A.30.2.10.description: Putative biopolymer transport proteins ExbB/ExbD-like 3 (Sll1404/Sll1405). Involved in the TonB-dependent energy-dependent transport of iron-siderophores via FhuA (Sll1406; TC# 1.B.14.2.9) using TonB (TC# 2.C.1.3.1) (Qiu et al. 2018). ExbB may protect ExbD from proteolytic degradation and functionally stabilizes TonB.
1.A.30.2.10.proteins: ExbBD of Synechocystis sp. (strain PCC 6803 / Kazusa)

1.A.30.2.11.name: ExbB/ExbD/ExbD' of 254 aas, 150 aas, and 147 aas, respectively, with 3, 1 and 1 TMSs, respectively.
1.A.30.2.11.description: ExbB/ExbD/ExbD' of 254 aas, 150 aas, and 147 aas, respectively, with 3, 1 and 1 TMSs, respectively. The genes encoding these three proteins are adjacent to each other. ExbD and TonB (TC# 2.C.1.3.1) interact directly (Qiu et al. 2018).

The channel is lined by TolR-Asp23, TolQ-Thr145 and TolQ-Thr178. 1.A.30.3.2.description: Motor for adventurous motility, AglR (a TolQ homologue)/AglS (a TolR homologue) (Nan et al. 2011). The mechanism by which the AglRS proteins energize adventurous gliding motility has been proposed (Jakobczak et al. 2015; Mignot and Nöllmann 2017).

1.A.30.3.3.description: Adventurous gliding motility proteins AglR, AglS and AglV. These three proteins presumably function in gliding motility but are homologues of MotA/ExbB, MotB/ExbD and MotB/ExbD, respectively.

1.A.33.1.5.description: Glucose regulated protein, GRP78 of 654 aas. GRP78, a member of the ER stress protein family. It can relocate to the surface of cancer cells, playing a role in promoting cell proliferation and metastasis. GRP78 consists of two major functional domains: the ATPase and protein/peptide-binding domains. The protein/peptide-binding domain of cell-surface GRP78 has served as a novel functional receptor…

1.A.33.2.1.description: MMAR_0617 MOMP (Hsp70 homologue) (van der Woude et al. 2013).

1.A.34.1.2.description: SpoIIQ homologue of one of the two components (SpoIIQ and SpoIIIAH) of the gap junction-like channel-forming complex of B. subtilis. Several SpoIIQ homologues in various E. coli strains were identified, but no homologue of the SpoIIAH component was found. Therefore, pore formation can not be inferred.

1.A.35.1.2.description: Divalent cation (Mg2+, Co2+ and Ni2+) transport system, CorA

1.A.35.2.1.name: Aluminum resistance protein AlR1p; Alr1; ALR1, LLR1; MNR1 AlR1p and AlR2p both catalyze uptake of Mg2+ and a variety of heavy metals.
1.A.35.2.1.description: Aluminum resistance protein AlR1p; Alr1; ALR1, LLR1; MNR1 (Mg2+ homeostasis transporter [Mg2+ regulated]) AlR1p and AlR2p (P43553; a close paralogue) both catalyze uptake of Mg2+ and a variety of heavy metals (da Costa et al., 2007). Truncation of Alr1 showed that the N-terminal 239 amino acids and the C-terminal 53 amino acids are not essential for magnesium uptake (Lee and Gardner 2006)…

1.A.35.2.2.name: Inner mitochondrial membrane manganese channel protein MnR2p or MRS2-11.
1.A.35.2.2.description: Inner mitochondrial membrane manganese channel protein MnR2p or MRS2-11. The regulatory domain of Mrs2 from the yeast inner mitochondrial membrane is similar to the E. coli regulatory domain of CorA with Met309 serving the same function as Met291 in CorA (Khan et al. 2013).

1.A.35.3.1.name: Divalent metal ion (Mg2+, Ca2+, Ni2+, etc.) transporter of 317 aas and 3 TMSs.
1.A.35.3.1.description: Divalent metal ion (Mg2+, Ca2+, Ni2+, etc.) transporter of 317 aas and 3 TMSs. The cryo-EM structure shows a pentameric channel with an asymmetric domain structure and featuring differential separations between the trans-segments, probably reflecting mechanical coupling of the cytoplasmic domain to the transmembrane domain and suggesting a gating mechanism (Cleverley et al. 2015).

1.A.35.3.2.name: Magnesium transport protein, CorA.
1.A.35.3.2.description: Magnesium transport protein, CorA. The structure at 2.7 Å resolution is known. The CorA monomer has a C-terminal membrane domain containing two transmembrane segments and a large N-terminal cytoplasmic soluble domain. In the membrane, CorA forms a homopentamer shaped like a funnel which binds fully hydrated Mg2+ in the periplasm (Maguire 2006). A ring of positive charges are external to the…

1.A.35.3.5.name: MIP family protein of 366 aas.
1.A.35.3.5.description: MIP family protein of 366 aas. Mg2+,Co2+ and the CorA-specific inhibitor (Co(III) hexamine chloride) bind in the loop at the same binding site. This site includes the glutamic acid residue from the conserved "MPEL" motif (Hu et al. 2009).

1.A.35.3.6.name: The CorA-homologous magnesium ion transporter of 831 aas, Mgt1.
1.A.35.3.6.description: The CorA-homologous magnesium ion transporter of 831 aas, Mgt1. Is critical for parasite development and virulence (Zhu et al. 2009).

1.A.35.3.7.name: Putative Mg2+ transporter of 322 aas and 2 or 3 TMSs.
1.A.35.3.7.description: Putative Mg2+ transporter of 322 aas and 2 or 3 TMSs.

1.A.35.3.8.description: Uncharacterized CorA homologue of 373 aas and 3 TMSs (Pohland and Schneider 2019).

It may transport Mg2+, Zn2+, Cd2+, Co2+, Cu2+ and Mn2+ as well as other di-valent and tri-valent metal cations. This suggestion is based on homology with other members of the MIT family.

1.A.35.4.2.description: The ZntB Zn2+/Cd2+ transporter. The 1.9Å structure of the N-terminal cytoplasmic domain of ZntB has been solved (Tan et al., 2009).

1.A.35.5.1.description: Mitochondrial inner membrane Mg2+ channel protein, Mrs2 (Schindl et al., 2007). Mutational analyses have been carried out, suggesting that internal Mg2+ affects intron splicing (Weghuber et al. 2006). MRS2 is involved in mitochondrial Mg2+ homeostasis (Schäffers et al. 2018). Hv1 most likely forms an internal water wire for selective proton transfer, and interactions between water molecules and S4 arginines may underlie coupling between voltage- and pH-gradient sensing (Ramsey et al. 2010).

Mutations in the first transmembrane segment at position 66 (Asp66), the presumed selectivity filter, led to a loss of proton-selective conduction (Chaves et al. 2016).

The presence of protein sequences corresponding to such channels were demonstrated in all four types of fungi (Zhao and Tombola 2021).

1.A.8.10.17.description: Aquaporin of 250 aas and 6 TMSs. It is a water channel required to facilitate the transport of water across membranes; it is involved in osmotolerance (Ghosh et al. 2006).

1.A.8.10.18.name: Aqp0a of 263 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.10.18.description: Aqp0a of 263 aas and 6 TMSs. Zebrafish optical development requires regulated water permeability by Aquaporin 0 (Safrina et al. 2024). Localization and expression of Aquaporin 0 (AQP0) in the Tissues of the Spiny Dogfish have been reported (Cutler et al. 2026).

1.A.8.10.2.name: Tonoplast intrinsic protein-a transports water, urea, glycerol and gases (CO2 and NH3)
1.A.8.10.2.description: Tonoplast intrinsic protein-a (transports water, urea, glycerol and gases (CO2 and NH3)

1.A.8.10.3.name: Tonoplast intrinsic protein 1.1 of 251 aas and probably 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.10.3.description: Tonoplast intrinsic protein 1.1 of 251 aas and probably 6 TMSs. TIPs control water trade among cytosolic and vacuolar compartments and can also transport glycerol, ammonia, urea, hydrogen peroxide, metals/metalloids, and several amino acids (Liu et al. 2003). Additionally, TIPs, which can be responsive to nitrogen availability and salt sensitivity, are engaged with different abiotic stress…

1.A.8.10.4.name: Vacuolar (tonoplast) NH3 channel, TIP2;3. [Tip2;2 of wheat is also an NH3/H2O channel].
1.A.8.10.4.description: Vacuolar (tonoplast) NH3 channel, TIP2;3 (Loque et al., 2005). [Tip2;2 of wheat is also an NH3/H2O channel (Bertl and Kaldenhoff, 2007)].

1.A.8.10.5.name: Endoplasmic reticulum Small and Basic Intrinsic Protein; water channel May play a role in gas and water exchange between the plant and its…
1.A.8.10.5.description: Endoplasmic reticulum Small and Basic Intrinsic Protein; (SIP1;1) water channel (present in all plant tissues except seeds) (Ishikawa et al., 2005) May play a role in gas and water exchange between the plant and its environment via stromata (turgor-driven epidermal valves) and the hydathode pore (Pillitteri et al., 2008).

1.A.8.10.6.name: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin, Tip1;3
1.A.8.10.6.description: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin, Tip1;3 (Soto et al. 2008)

1.A.8.10.7.name: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin.
1.A.8.10.7.description: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin. Tip5;1 (Soto et al. 2008) An aquaporin specifically targeted to pollen mitochondria; probably involved in nitrogen remobilization (Soto et al., 2010).

1.A.8.10.8.name: Aquaporin-B, AqpB of 294 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.10.8.description: Aquaporin-B, AqpB of 294 aas and 6 TMSs. Tyr216 in loop D is a key residue in gating, possibly involving phosphorylation. Mutation of Tyr216 to aspartate or glutamate initiated water permeability. The truncated, permanently open AqpB yielded cells with reduced capability to cope with hypotonic stress (von Bülow et al. 2015).

1.A.8.10.9.name: Aquaporin TIP1-2 (Gamma-tonoplast intrinsic protein 2) (Gamma-TIP2) (Tonoplast intrinsic protein 1-2) (AtTIP1;2)
1.A.8.10.9.description: Aquaporin TIP1-2 (Gamma-tonoplast intrinsic protein 2) (Gamma-TIP2) (Salt stress-induced tonoplast intrinsic protein) (Tonoplast intrinsic protein 1-2) (AtTIP1;2)

1.A.8.11.10.name: Pip2-4 of 291 aas with 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.11.10.description: Pip2-4 of 291 aas with 6 TMSs. In tobacco plants, overexpression of the NtPIP2;4 gene can enhance drought resistance (Luo et al. 2025).

1.A.8.11.11.name: PIP2-4 water channel of286 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.11.11.description: PIP2-4 water channel of286 aas and 6 TMSs. The PIP2;4 aquaporin water channel, primarily expressed in roots of rice, mediates both water and nonselective Na+ and K+ conductance (Tran et al. 2025).
1.A.8.11.11.proteins: PIP2.4 of Oryza sativa spbsp. japonica

1.A.8.11.2.name: The plasma membrane aquaporin, NtAQP1 (H2O and CO2 permeable; important for photosynthesis, stomatal opening and leaf growth)
1.A.8.11.2.description: The plasma membrane aquaporin, NtAQP1 (H2O and CO2 permeable; important for photosynthesis, stomatal opening and leaf growth) (Uehlein et al., 2003; Uehlein et al., 2008)

1.A.8.11.3.name: Plasma membrane aquaporin 1, PIP1, PIP1;2, PIP1b, of 286 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.11.3.description: Plasma membrane aquaporin 1, PIP1, PIP1;2, PIP1b, of 286 aas and 6 TMSs (Törnroth-Horsefield et al., 2006). Transports H2O, H2O2 (Dynowski et al., 2008), O2 and CO2 (Zwiazek et al. 2017). Forms active heterotetramers with PIP2;1 (1.A.8.11.4); down regulated under drought stress (Najafabadi et al., 2008); plays a role in salt tolerance (Li et al. 2018). Gated by H+, Ca2+, Mn2+ and Cd2+ (Verdoucq…

1.A.8.11.5.name: Probable aquaporin PIP2-6 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-6) (AtPIP2;6) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2e) (PIP2e).
1.A.8.11.5.description: Probable aquaporin PIP2-6 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-6) (AtPIP2;6) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2e) (PIP2e). In the radish (Raphaus sativus), there are 61 genes encoding aquaporins, and RsPIP2-6 is induced with high NaCl, and is involved in the salt stress response (Yi et al. 2022). The plasma membrane intrinsic protein OsPIP2;6 is involved in root-to-shoot arsenic translocation…

1.A.8.11.6.name: Aquaporin PIP2-8 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-8) (AtPIP2;8) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 3b) (PIP3b).
1.A.8.11.6.description: Aquaporin PIP2-8 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-8) (AtPIP2;8) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 3b) (PIP3b). This protein as well as 1.A.8.11.4 are possibly orthologous to spinach PIP1;2 for which the crystal structure is available (PDP# 4JC6) (Berny et al. 2016).

1.A.8.11.7.name: Aquaporin PIP2;5 (PIP2-5) of 285 aas.
1.A.8.11.7.description: Aquaporin PIP2;5 (PIP2-5) of 285 aas. Transports water and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) (Bienert et al. 2014;). PIP1;2 doesn't transport H2O2. TMS3 contains an LxxA motif that targets the protein to the plasma membrane from the ER. While PIP2s are in the plasma mebrane, PIP1s are retained in the ER; this motif only partly explains the difference (Chevalier and Chaumont 2015). PIP1;2 AND PIP2;5 form…

1.A.8.11.8.name: Aqp2 of 297 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.11.8.description: Aqp2 of 297 aas and 6 TMSs. Induced by both NH3 and CO2, and transports both gases. Aqp2 is found in the plasma membrane and may be involved in photoprotection. It may facilitate the efflux of NH3, preventing the uncoupling effect of high intracellular ammonia concentrations (Matsui et al. 2018).
1.A.8.11.8.proteins: Aqp2 of Phaeodactylum tricornutum, a marine photoautotrophic diatoms

1.A.8.11.9.name: Water channel, Aqp2-3 or Aqp2;3 or PIP2C of 285 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.11.9.description: Water channel, Aqp2-3 or Aqp2;3 or PIP2C of 285 aas and 6 TMSs. Ectopic expression of CrPIP2;3, a plasma membrane intrinsic protein gene from the halophyte, Canavalia rosea, enhanced drought and salt-alkali stress tolerance in Arabidopsis (Zheng et al. 2021). The Arabidopsis ortholog is presented here.

1.A.8.12.1.name: Nodulin-26 aquaporin and glycerol facilitator, NIP.
1.A.8.12.1.description: Nodulin-26 aquaporin and glycerol facilitator, NIP (de Paula Santos Martins et al. 2015). Transports NH3 5-fold better than water in Hg2+-sensitive fashion (Hwang et al., 2010).

1.A.8.12.10.name: Arsenite export pore, AqpS
1.A.8.12.10.description: Arsenite export pore, AqpS (Yang et al., 2005)

1.A.8.12.13.name: Rice NIP2.1 (NIP2-1; NIP2;1) of 295 aas and 6 or 7 TMSs.
1.A.8.12.13.description: Rice NIP2.1 (NIP2-1; NIP2;1) of 295 aas and 6 or 7 TMSs. It transports metaloids such as arsenous acid (arsenic) and silisic acid (silicon). The 3-D structure has been determined (Sharma et al. 2023). This protein is most similar to TC# 1.A.8.12.2 within TCDB.

1.A.8.12.2.name: The silicon (silicic acid) (undissociated form) transporter, Lsi1.
1.A.8.12.2.description: The silicon (silicic acid) (undissociated form) transporter, Lsi1 (Ma et al., 2007a, b; Mitani et al., 2008). The barley orthologue Lsi1 (also called NIP2-1) is also a silicon (silicic acid) uptake channel (Chiba et al., 2009). Rice Lsi1 also transports arsenite and pentavalent mono and dimethyl arsenite (Li et al., 2009). In addition to silicon (Si), selenite (Se) uptake is mediated by Lsi1…

1.A.8.12.3.name: The boric acid channel protein, NIP5;1 (expressed in the root elongation zone and root hairs in response to boron deficiency).
1.A.8.12.3.description: The boric acid channel protein, NIP5;1 (expressed in the root elongation zone and root hairs in response to boron deficiency) (Takano et al., 2006). Borate is an essential nutrient in plants. The ortholog in Brassica napus (XP_013652160.1) is 301 aas in length with 6 TMSs and is 90% identical to the A. thaliana protein. Synthesis of the B. napus protein is induced in roots and shoots by a borate…

1.A.8.12.4.name: The root-expressed MIP transporter of lactic acid, NIP2;1 (Nod26-like MIP-4; NLM4).
1.A.8.12.4.description: The root-expressed MIP transporter of lactic acid, NIP2;1 (Nod26-like MIP-4; NLM4) (induced by water logging and anoxic stress; shows minimal water and glycerol transport). It may play a role in adaptation to lactic fermentaion under anaerobic stress (Choi and Roberts, 2007). Lactic acid transport is induced by anoxic stress (Choi and Roberts, 2007).

1.A.8.12.5.name: The silicon (silicic acid) transporter, Nip2-2 (Nip2;2).
1.A.8.12.5.description: The silicon (silicic acid) transporter, Nip2-2 (Nip2;2) (Mitani et al., 2008). Also transports arsenite (Li et al., 2009).

1.A.8.12.6.name: Nip7;1 arsenite and borate channel
1.A.8.12.6.description: Nip7;1 arsenite and borate channel (Isayenkov and Maathuis, 2008; Li et al., 2011)

1.A.8.12.7.name: Aquaporin NIP1-2 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-2) (AtNIP1;2) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 2) (NodLikeMip2) (Protein NLM2).
1.A.8.12.7.description: Aquaporin NIP1-2 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-2) (AtNIP1;2) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 2) (NodLikeMip2) (Protein NLM2). Selectivity filters play roles in determining aluminum transport by AtNIP1;2 (Wang et al. 2021).

1.A.8.12.8.name: Aquaporin NIP1-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-1) (AtNIP1;1) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 1) (NodLikeMip1) (Protein NLM1).
1.A.8.12.8.description: Aquaporin NIP1-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-1) (AtNIP1;1) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 1) (NodLikeMip1) (Protein NLM1). NIP-like aquaporins transport water, but also arsenic, boric acid, sliicon, glycerol, urea, lactic acid and ammonia (Mitani-Ueno et al. 2011; Hwang et al. 2010). The grape ortholog appears to transport the same molecules including water and glycerol, but also…

1.A.8.12.9.name: Aquaporin NIP6-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 6-1) (AtNIP6;1).
1.A.8.12.9.description: Aquaporin NIP6-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 6-1) (AtNIP6;1). The grape ortholog is impermeable to water, but permeable to glycerol (Sabir et al. 2020).

1.A.8.13.1.name: MIP family homologue
1.A.8.13.1.proteins: Orf of Archaeoglobus fulgidus, AE000782 (ID# AF1426)

1.A.8.13.2.name: Hg2+-inhibitable aquaporin, AqpM (transports both water and glycerol as well as CO2).
1.A.8.13.2.description: Hg2+-inhibitable aquaporin, AqpM (transports both water and glycerol as well as CO2) (Kozono et al., 2003; Araya-Secchi et al., 2011). Its 3-d structure has been determined to 1.7 Å. In AqpM, isoleucine replaces a key histidine residue found in the lumen of water channels, which becomes a glycine residue in aquaglyceroporins. As a result of this and other side-chain substituents in the walls of…

1.A.8.13.3.name: Putative aquaporin, GlpF5, of 216 aas; probably transports water, glycerol and dihydroxyacetone.
1.A.8.13.3.description: Putative aquaporin, GlpF5, of 216 aas; probably transports water, glycerol and dihydroxyacetone (Bienert et al. 2013).

1.A.8.13.4.name: Aquaporin, Aqp, of 222 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.13.4.description: Aquaporin, Aqp, of 222 aas and 6 TMSs. It functions in hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) export from the cell, relieving oxidative stress (Tong et al. 2019). It is an H2O2-inducible bacterial "peroxiporin".
1.A.8.13.4.proteins: Aqp of Streptococcus oligofermentans or Streptococcus cristatus

1.A.8.13.5.name: Aquaporin, Aqp9, of 231 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.13.5.description: Aquaporin, Aqp9, of 231 aas and 6 TMSs. This protein co-localizes with the vacuolar proton pyrophosphatase to acidocalcisomes and the contractile vacuole complex (Montalvetti et al. 2004) which are involved in osmoregulation (Rohloff et al. 2004). Acidocalcisomes function as storage sites for cations and phosphorus, participate in PPi and poly P metabolism as well as volume regulation and are…

1.A.8.2.10.name: Aquaglyceroporin of 270 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.2.10.proteins: Aquaporin of Paramecium bursaria chlorella virus MT325

1.A.8.2.12.name: Aquaglyceroporin, AagP, of 298 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.2.12.description: Aquaglyceroporin, AagP, of 298 aas and 6 TMSs. This protein transports water, glycerol and H2O2. It catalyzes H2O2 efflux during glycerol uptake and contributes to virulence in mice (Zhu et al. 2023).

1.A.8.2.2.name: Mixed function glycerol facilitator/aquaporin, GlpF.
1.A.8.2.2.description: Mixed function glycerol facilitator/aquaporin, GlpF (Froger et al. 2001).

1.A.8.2.4.name: GlpF1; transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol as well as D,L-lactic acid.
1.A.8.2.4.description: GlpF1; transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol as well as D,L-lactic acid (Bienert et al. 2013).

1.A.8.2.5.name: GlpF2.
1.A.8.2.5.description: GlpF2. Transporter of water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol (Bienert et al. 2013).

1.A.8.2.6.name: GlpF3.
1.A.8.2.6.description: GlpF3. Transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol (Bienert et al. 2013).

1.A.8.2.7.name: GlpF4.
1.A.8.2.7.description: GlpF4. Transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol as well as D,L-lactic acid (Bienert et al. 2013).

1.A.8.2.8.name: Putative aquaporin, GlpF6.
1.A.8.2.8.description: Putative aquaporin, GlpF6. Probably transports water, glycerol and dihydroxyacetone (Bienert et al. 2013).

1.A.8.2.9.name: Glycerol facilitator, GlpF, of 248 aas and 6 TMSs
1.A.8.2.9.description: Glycerol facilitator, GlpF, of 248 aas and 6 TMSs
1.A.8.2.9.proteins: GlpF of Blattabacterium sp. subsp. Blattella germanica (strain Bge) (Blattella germanica symbiotic bacterium)

1.A.8.3.1.name: Aquaporin Z water channel (aqpZ gene expression is under sigma S control; induced at the onset of stationary phase).
1.A.8.3.1.description: Aquaporin Z water channel (aqpZ gene expression is under sigma S control; induced at the onset of stationary phase) (Mallo and Ashby, 2006). The high resolution 3-d structure is available (PDB 1RC2) revealing two re-entrant coil-helix domains from the selectivity filter (Savage et al. 2003). Coupled mutations enabled glycerol transport (Ping et al. 2018).

1.A.8.4.1.name: Intracellular endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized Aquaporin 11 (Aqp11, AqpX1) water channel.
1.A.8.4.1.description: Intracellular endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized Aquaporin 11 (Aqp11, AqpX1) water channel (important for the development of kidney proximal tubules; disruption produces neonatally fatal polycystic kidneys (Ishibashi 2006). Has a positively charged C-terminal amino acid cluster similar to the di-lysine motif (-KKXX) for ER retention (Nozaki et al., 2008)). In the horse, AQP3 and AQP11 are…

1.A.8.4.3.name: Aquaporin 10, Aqp10 of 259 aas and 6 TMSs
1.A.8.4.3.description: Aquaporin 10, Aqp10 of 259 aas and 6 TMSs
1.A.8.4.3.proteins: Aqp10 of Haemonchus contortus (Barber pole worm)

1.A.8.4.4.name: Aquaporin of 263 aas and 7 TMSs.
1.A.8.4.4.description: Aquaporin of 263 aas and 7 TMSs (Stavang et al. 2015).
1.A.8.4.4.proteins: Aquaporin of the salmon leach, Lepeophtheirus salmonis

1.A.8.4.5.name: Aquaporin of 256 aas with 6 TMSs in a 3 (N-terminus) + 3 TMS (C-terminus) arrangement.
1.A.8.4.5.description: Aquaporin of 256 aas with 6 TMSs in a 3 (N-terminus) + 3 TMS (C-terminus) arrangement (Zhou et al. 2018).

1.A.8.4.6.name: Aquaporin of 261 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.4.6.description: Aquaporin of 261 aas and 6 TMSs. Aquaporins may not play major roles in adapting to longterm survival in brackish water or they be regulated by non-transcriptional mechanisms like post-translational modifications (Misyura et al. 2020).
1.A.8.4.6.proteins: Aqp of Aedes aegypti (Yellowfever mosquito) (Culex aegypti)

1.A.8.5.1.name: FPS1 glycerol efflux facilitator.
1.A.8.5.1.description: FPS1 glycerol efflux facilitator. It is important for maintaining osmotic balance during mating-induced yeast cell fusion and for tolerating hypoosmotic shock; it also transports arsenite and antimonite). FPS1 is a homotetramer (Beese-Sims et al., 2011). It is important for osmo-adaptation by regulating intracellular glycerol levels during changes in external osmolarity. Upon high osmolarity…

1.A.8.5.2.name: Fps1 hyperactive orthologue of the S. cerevisiae Fps1 (1.A.8.5.1).
1.A.8.5.2.description: Fps1 hyperactive orthologue of the S. cerevisiae Fps1 (1.A.8.5.1) (Geijer et al., 2012).

1.A.8.6.1.name: Aqy1, aquaporin (mediates H2O efflux during sporulation) (spore maturation)
1.A.8.6.1.description: Aqy1, aquaporin (mediates H2O efflux during sporulation) (spore maturation) (Sidoux-Walter et al., 2004)

1.A.8.6.2.name: Aquaporin-2 Aqy2 (plays a role in reducing surface hydrophobicity promoting cell dispersion during starvation and reproduction)
1.A.8.6.2.description: Aquaporin-2 Aqy2 (plays a role in reducing surface hydrophobicity promoting cell dispersion during starvation and reproduction)

1.A.8.6.3.name: Aquaporin, Aqy1 (PIP2-7 7).
1.A.8.6.3.description: Aquaporin, Aqy1 (PIP2-7 7). The subangstron (0.88Å) structure is available (Kosinska Eriksson et al. 2013). the H-bond donor interactions of the NPA motif''s asparagine residues to passing water molecules are revealed. A polarized water-water H-bond configuration is observed within the channel. Four selectivity filter water positions are too closely spaced to be simultaneously occupied. Strongly…

1.A.8.6.4.name: Water and CO2 permeable aquaporin, AQP1, of an edible mycorhizal fungus (desert truffles).
1.A.8.6.4.description: Water and CO2 permeable aquaporin, AQP1, of an edible mycorhizal fungus (desert truffles) (Navarro-Ródenas et al. 2012).

1.A.8.7.1.name: Tobacco X-intrinsic protein (XIP1-1-β).
1.A.8.7.1.description: Tobacco X-intrinsic protein (XIP1-1-β). Transports glycerol, urea and boric acid, but not water (Bienert et al., 2011).

1.A.8.7.2.name: Potato X intrinsic protein, XIP1.
1.A.8.7.2.description: Potato X intrinsic protein, XIP1. Transports glycerol, urea and boric acid, but not water (Bienert et al., 2011).

1.A.8.7.3.name: Morning glory XIP-1-1-α.
1.A.8.7.3.description: Morning glory XIP-1-1-α. Transports glycerol, urea and boric acid, but not water (Bienert et al., 2011).

1.A.8.7.5.name: Aquaporin F (AqpF) of 321 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.7.5.description: Aquaporin F (AqpF) of 321 aas and 6 TMSs. It transports water and glycerol, but additionally transporters hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) for signaling purposes (Laothanachareon et al. 2023). It may be the only aquaporin capable of H2O2 transport and signalling.

1.A.8.8.1.name: Aquaporin 1 (CO2-, O2-, H202- and nitrous oxide-permeable, water-selective, and monovalent cation (Li+. Na+ and K+) permeable).
1.A.8.8.1.description: Aquaporin 1 (CO2-, O2-, H202- and nitrous oxide-permeable, water-selective, and monovalent cation (Li+. Na+ and K+) permeable) (Zwiazek et al. 2017; Varadaraj and Kumari 2020; Nourmohammadi et al. 2024). Aquaporin-1 tunes pain perception by interacting with Nav1.8 Na+ channels in dorsal root ganglion neurons (Zhang and Verkman, 2010). It is upregulated in skeletal muscle in muscular dystrophy (Au…

1.A.8.8.10.name: Water and urea transporting aquaporin (cockroach).
1.A.8.8.10.description: Water and urea transporting aquaporin (cockroach) (Herraiz et al., 2011).

1.A.8.8.11.name: Water channel, Aqp1; inhibited by HgCl2 and tetraethylammonium.
1.A.8.8.11.description: Water channel, Aqp1; inhibited by HgCl2 and tetraethylammonium. Plays a role in water homeostasis during blood feeding and humidity adaptation of A. gambiae, a major mosquito vector of human malaria in Africa (Liu et al., 2011).

1.A.8.8.12.name: Aquaporin, Aqp1 in the gall fly.
1.A.8.8.12.description: Aquaporin, Aqp1 in the gall fly. Transports water but not glycerol or urea. Promotes freeze-tolerance (Philip et al., 2011).

1.A.8.8.13.name: The Drosophila melanogaster integral protein, DRIP.
1.A.8.8.13.description: The Drosophila melanogaster integral protein, DRIP (Ishida et al., 2012).

1.A.8.8.15.name: Mercury-sensitive whitefly aquaporin-1 of the specialized filter chamber of the alimentary tract.
1.A.8.8.15.description: Mercury-sensitive whitefly aquaporin-1 of the specialized filter chamber of the alimentary tract (Mathew et al. 2011).

1.A.8.8.16.name: Aquaporin-1 or Aquaporin1, Aqp1, of 258 aas and 6 TMSs.
1.A.8.8.16.description: Aquaporin-1 or Aquaporin1, Aqp1, of 258 aas and 6 TMSs. Three Aqp1 isoforms are differentially regluated by the function of the vasotocin (AVTR) and isotocin (ITR) receptors (Martos-Sitcha et al. 2015). Aqp1aa, one of two isoforms in teleosts, may play a role in spermatogenesis in Cynoglossus semilaevis (Guo et al. 2017).
1.A.8.8.16.proteins: Aqp1 of Sparus aurata (Gilthead sea bream)

1.A.8.8.17.name: Aquaporin-3, Aqp-3 of 271 aas.
1.A.8.8.17.description: Aquaporin-3, Aqp-3 of 271 aas. Transports water, glycerol, hydrogen peroxide and urea (Geadkaew et al. 2015). AQP3 induces the production of chemokines such as CCL24 and CCL22 through regulating the amount of cellular H2O2 in M2 polarized alveolar macrophages, implying a role of AQP3 in asthma (Ikezoe et al. 2016).

1.A.8.8.18.name: Aqp-x2 water channel in the luminal epithelium of urinary bladder cells and lungs.
1.A.8.8.18.description: Aqp-x2 water channel in the luminal epithelium of urinary bladder cells and lungs. Responsive to Vasotocin (AVT) (Shibata et al. 2015).

1.A.8.8.19.name: Contractile vacuole aquaporin of 295 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp.
1.A.8.8.19.description: Contractile vacuole aquaporin of 295 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp. Shown to transport water, accounting for the high water permeability of the contractile vacuole (Nishihara et al. 2008).

1.A.8.8.20.name: Channel protein
1.A.8.8.20.proteins: Copper homeostasis protein (SmpX) of Synechococcus sp.

1.A.8.8.21.name: Aquaporin x5 of 273 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp-x5.
1.A.8.8.21.description: Aquaporin x5 of 273 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp-x5. The sequence reveals a mercurial-sensitive cysteine and a putative phosphorylation motif site for protein kinase A at Ser-257 (Kubota et al. 2006). A swelling assay using Xenopus oocytes revealed that AQP-x5 facilitated water permeability. Expression of AQP-x5 mRNA was restricted to the skin, brain, lungs and testes. Immunofluorescence and…

1.A.8.8.22.name: Aqp-1A of 258 aas and 6 TMSs, DRIP1.

1.A.8.8.9.description: Aquaporin 5 (x-ray structure at 2.0 Å resolution (PDB# 3D9S) is available) (Horsefield et al., 2008). 1.A.8.9.11.description: Aqp1 of 304 aas and 6 TMSs; the most abundant transmembrane protein in the tegument of Schistosoma mansoni. This protein is expressed in all developmental stages and seems to be essential in parasite survival since it plays a crucial role in osmoregulation, nutrient transport and drug uptake (Figueiredo et al. 2014).

The transmembrane beta-barrel is stable even in the absence of the alpha-helix. Removal of the helix…

1.B.13.1.7.description: Alginate export porin of 460 aas. May also export neutral lipids such as triacylglycerols, wax esters, and polyhydroxyalkanoates (Manilla-Pérez et al. 2010).

1.B.14.1.11.description: The outer membrane ferric-anguibactin receptor/transporter, FatA (Lopez and Crosa, 2007)

1.B.14.1.12.description: FecA ferric-citrate receptor (PA3901) (Marshall et al., 2009) (62% identical to the E. coli FecA).

Deletion of the…

1.B.14.1.20.name: The iron-citrate receptor/transporter, FecA.
1.B.14.1.20.description: The iron-citrate receptor/transporter, FecA. TonB mediates both signaling and transport by unfolding portions of the transporter (Mokdad et al. 2012). The ferric citrate regulator, FecR, is translocated across the bacterial inner membrane via a unique Twin-arginine transport dependent mechanism (Passmore et al. 2020).

1.B.14.1.21.name: Ferrioxamine receptor
1.B.14.1.21.proteins: Ferrioxamine receptor of Pseudovibrio sp. JE062

1.B.14.1.22.description: FepA ferri-enterobactin (also Colicins B and D) receptor for the 37 aas disulfide-containing K+ channel toxin, BgK (Braud et al., 2004). Functions by a "ball and chain" mechanism; The transport process involves expulsion of the N-terminal globular domain from the C-terminal beta-barrel (Ma et al. 2007). Conformational rearrangements occur in the N-terminus of FepA during FeEnt transport, but…

1.B.14.1.25.name: Nickel uptake receptor/channel of 724 aas.
1.B.14.1.25.description: Nickel uptake receptor/channel of 724 aas (Benoit et al. 2013).

1.B.14.1.26.name: Iron siderophore (ferripyoverdine) receptor and importer, FpvA of 808 aas.
1.B.14.1.26.description: Iron siderophore (ferripyoverdine) receptor and importer, FpvA of 808 aas (Ye et al. 2014). The crystal structure of FpvA has been solved at 3.6 Å resolution. It is folded in two domains: a transmembrane 22-stranded beta-barrel domain occluded by an N-terminal domain containing a mixed four-stranded beta-sheet (the plug). The beta-strands of the barrel are connected by long extracellular loops…

1.B.14.1.27.name: Iron(III) dicitrate transport protein, FecA1: iron dicitrate uptake receptor of 767 aas.
1.B.14.1.27.description: Iron(III) dicitrate transport protein, FecA1: iron dicitrate uptake receptor of 767 aas. Regulated by the ferric uptake regulator transcription factor, Fur (van Vliet et al. 2002) in response to iron availability (Danielli et al. 2009). Involved in iron deficiency anemia in children (Kato et al. 2017).

1.B.14.1.29.name: Iron-deficiency-induced (2x) iron siderophore uptake outer membrane receptor, FhuA, of 828 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.14.1.29.description: Iron-deficiency-induced (2x) iron siderophore uptake outer membrane receptor, FhuA, of 828 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS (Qiu et al. 2018).

1.B.14.1.3.name: Ferric enterobactin receptor, IroN The microbial metabolite, Enterobactin, impairs mitochondrial respiration and alleviates colitis in humans.
1.B.14.1.3.description: Ferric enterobactin (also ferricorynebactin) receptor, IroN The microbial metabolite, Enterobactin, impairs mitochondrial respiration and alleviates colitis in humans (Kushwaha et al. 2026).

1.B.14.1.31.name: Outer membrane porin, PiuA, of 753 aas.
1.B.14.1.31.description: Outer membrane porin, PiuA, of 753 aas. A deficiency of this iron transporter, PiuA in P. aeruginosa, caused 16-fold increases in cefiderocol resistance, suggesting that it contribute to the permeation of cefiderocol into the cell (Ito et al. 2018).

1.B.14.1.32.name: Catechol iron-siderophore uptake system, IrgA, an iron-regulated outer membrane virulence protein, of 652 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.14.1.32.description: Catechol iron-siderophore uptake system, IrgA, an iron-regulated outer membrane virulence protein, of 652 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS (Wyckoff et al. 2015). It is involved in the initial step of iron uptake by binding ferric vibriobactin, an iron chelatin siderophore that allows V. cholerae to extract iron from the environment and takes up linear enterobactin derivatives (Wyckoff et al. 2015).

1.B.14.1.33.name: Heme/hemin outer membrane TonB-related receptor of 708 aas, Tlr.
1.B.14.1.33.description: Heme/hemin outer membrane TonB-related receptor of 708 aas, Tlr (Slakeski et al. 2000).

1.B.14.1.34.description: TonB-dependent transporters (TBDTs) are outer membrane β-barrel proteins that mediate the proton motive force-dependent import of various nutrients to the periplasm. Hachmi et al. 2026 characterized a TBDT that imports copper in the whooping cough agent Bordetella pertussis, CrtABp (formerly BfrG), which is a prototype of a new subfamily of TBDTs. The data indicate that CrtABp is dedicated to the…

1.B.14.1.4.name: CirA Fe3+-catecholate receptor.
1.B.14.1.4.description: CirA Fe3+-catecholate receptor. Serves as the receptor for the TonB- and proton-dependent uptake of the E. coli bacteriocin, Microcin L (MccL) (Morin et al., 2011). CirA is also the translocator for colicin Ia (Jakes and Finkelstein, 2010). Plays roles in cefiderocol and ceftazidime resistance (Ito et al. 2018). Genotypic evolution of Klebsiella pneumoniae sequence type 512 during…

1.B.14.1.6.name: Ferripyoverdine/pyocin S3 receptor, FpvA
1.B.14.1.6.description: Ferripyoverdine/pyocin S3 receptor, FpvA (Adams et al., 2006; Nader et al., 2007; Schalk et al., 2009; Nader et al., 2011)

1.B.14.1.8.name: The Ferripyochelin receptor, FptA.
1.B.14.1.8.description: The Ferripyochelin receptor, FptA (Michel et al., 2007). In addition to Fe3+, FptA takes up Co2+, Ga3+, and Ni2+ at low rates (Braud et al., 2009). The high resolution 3-d structure of FptA (2.0 Å) bound to iron-pyochelin has been solved (Cobessi et al. 2005). The pyochelin molecule provides atetra-dentate coordination of iron. The structure is typical of the TonB-dependent receptor/transporter…

1.B.14.1.9.name: Ferric-catecholate siderophore (dihydroxybenzoylserine, dihydroxybenzoate) uptake receptor, Fiu or YbiL.
1.B.14.1.9.description: Ferric-catecholate siderophore (dihydroxybenzoylserine, dihydroxybenzoate) uptake receptor, Fiu or YbiL (Hantke, 1990; Curtis et al., 1988). Plays roles in cefiderocol and ceftazidime resistance (Ito et al. 2018). It can also transport catechol-substituted cephalosporins and is a receptor for microcins M, H47 and E492 (Patzer et al. 2003; Destoumieux-Garzón et al. 2006).

1.B.14.10.1.name: Heme/hemoglobin receptor, HmuR (also binds the Cu2+, Zn2+ and Fe2+ derivatives of protoporphyrin IX).
1.B.14.10.1.description: Heme/hemoglobin receptor, HmuR (also binds the Cu2+, Zn2+ and Fe2+ derivatives of protoporphyrin IX). Functions with the O.M. heme binding lipoprotein, HmuY (AAQ66587; Olczak et al., 2007).

1.B.14.10.5.description: Probable TonB-dependent long chain alkane receptor of 699 aas (Gregson et al. 2018).

1.B.14.12.1.description: The TonB-dependent maltooligosaccharide OM receptor/porin, MalA (Lohmiller et al., 2008).

1.B.14.2.17.description: The iron-catechol siderophore uptake/receptor, VctA, of 659 aas. Linear enterobactin derivatives are substrates, but it also transports the synthetic siderophore MECAM [1,3,5-N,N',N″-tris-(2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl)-triaminomethylbenzene] (Wyckoff et al. 2015).

1.B.14.2.3.description: HpuAB hemoglobin-haptoglobin receptor; porphyrin transporter (HpuA=lipoprotein; HpuB=OMR porin). Surface exposed loops in the gonococcal HpuB transporter are important for hemoglobin binding and utilization (Awate et al. 2023).

Forms a complex with and functions with SusD porin (TC# 8.A.46.1.1) as well as SusE and SusF porins (TC#s 1.B.38.1.1 and 1.2) as well as the SusG α-amylase (TC#8.A.9.1.3). 1.B.14.6.15.name: TonB-dependent collagenase (proteinase) of 1047 aas.
1.B.14.6.15.description: TonB-dependent collagenase (proteinase) of 1047 aas (Bhattacharya et al. 2017). 1.B.3.1.1.name: LamB (MalL) maltoporin (maltose–maltoheptose).
1.B.3.1.1.description: LamB (MalL) maltoporin (maltose–maltoheptose). Also catalyzes the uptake of antibiotics (Lin et al. 2014). LamB preferentially binds maltodextrins from the periplasmic side, and thus, sugar binding and uptake are asymmetric (Mulvihill et al. 2019). Expression of the lamB gene is regulated by EnvZ and OmpR in response to osmolarity and thereby influences antibiotic resistance (Gerken et al. 2024).

1.B.3.1.2.description: Oligosaccharide porin, ScrY (transports sucrose, raffinose and maltooligo-saccharides) (Kim et al. 2002). The 3-d structure known (PDB ID 1A0S). Sucrose translocation through the pore showed two main energy barriers within the constriction region of ScrY. Three asparate residues are key residues, opposing the passage of sucrose, all located within the L3 loop (Sun et al. 2016).

1.B.3.1.3.name: Porin with specificity for β-glucosides, BglH of 538 aas.
1.B.3.1.3.description: Porin with specificity for β-glucosides, BglH of 538 aas. High affinity binding was observed with the aromatic beta-D-glucosides arbutin and salicin as well as with gentibiose and cellobiose. Binding of maltooligosaccharides to BglH was much weaker, indicating that the binding site of BglH for carbohydrates is different from that of LamB (maltoporin) (Andersen et al. 1999).

1.B.76.1.1.description: Putative outer membrane porin, CopB of 422 aas. It has an N-terminal TMS, followed by a hydrophilic proline/alanine-rich domain and a C-terminal putative 10 β-strand domain. It confers copper resistance (Behlau et al. 2011).

1.B.76.1.2.name: Copper resistance protein, CopB of 251 aas.
1.B.76.1.2.description: Copper resistance protein, CopB of 251 aas. It has an N-terminal TMS followed by a putative beta barrel domain of 10 - 12 beta strands. This protein is 95% identical to the ortholog in Acinetobacter baumannii which is involved in copper efflux and virulence (Williams et al. 2020).

It is 50% identical to another fusion protein in Fluoribacter dumoffii of 827 aas (WP_010653677.1).

1.B.76.1.6.name: Copper resistance protein B, CopB of 332 aas and 12 putative β-strands.
1.B.76.1.6.description: Copper resistance protein B, CopB of 332 aas and 12 putative β-strands. May function with the copper uptake system, CopCD and the periplasmic CopA protein (TC# 9.B.62.6.1) (Wijekoon et al. 2015).

1.B.76.1.8.name: Blue multi-copper oxidase of 516 aas, CueO.
1.B.76.1.8.description: Blue multi-copper oxidase of 516 aas, CueO. CueO is involved in copper tolerance under aerobic conditions. It features the four typical copper atoms that act as electron transfer (T1) and dioxygen reduction (T2, T3; trinuclear) sites. In addition, it displays a methionine- and histidine-rich insert that includes a helix that blocks physical access to the T1 site (Cortes et al. 2015). It catalyzes…

1.C.1.3.2.description: Colicin B. Its structural stability and interactions have been studied (Ortega et al. 2001). It is 80% identical to colicin D, and colicin D has a well defined structure (PDB # 1V74; Gupta et al. 2023).

1.C.1.3.6.name: Colicin-like pore-forming domain protein, PmnH, of 462 aas and 2 C-terminal TMSs.

This protein has a dual-toxin architecture, having both an N-terminal colicin M-like domain, potentially interfering with peptidoglycan synthesis, and a colicin N-type domain, a pore-forming module distinct from the colicin Ia-type domain in Pseudomonas aeruginosa pyocin S5 (Ghequire et al. 2017). Enhanced killing…

1.C.1.4.1.name: Colicin E2 or E9.

The crystal structure of Colicin E3 with bound BtuB and with the N-terminal translocation (T) domain of E3 and E9 (DNAase) inserted into the OM OmpF porin has been solved…

1.E.14.1.16.name: Putative holin of 128 aas and 4 TMSs, CidA or YwbH.
1.E.14.1.16.description: Putative holin of 128 aas and 4 TMSs, CidA or YwbH. Functions in acetic acid promotion of biofilm formation (Chen et al. 2015). Increases the activity of extracellular murein hydrolases probably by mediating their export via hole formation. May be inhibited by LrgB/YwbG (2.A.122.1.5).

1.E.14.1.17.name: Putative holin (or anti-holin) of 146 aas and 4 TMSs, YsbA or LrgA.
1.E.14.1.17.description: Putative holin (or anti-holin) of 146 aas and 4 TMSs, YsbA or LrgA. YsbA is important for acetic acid induced biofilm formation (Chen et al. 2015) and for pyruvate utilization (van den Esker et al. 2016). van den Esker et al. 2016 proposed that YsbA is a pyruvate transporter. Thus, there is some question about the function of this protein and other members of this family.

1.E.14.1.2.name: Holin, CidA.
1.E.14.1.2.description: Holin, CidA (Bayles, 2003; Yang et al., 2005; Ranjit et al. 2011). Functions in biofilm formation in part by mediating release of cytoplasmic DNA during cell lysis to contribute to the biofilm matrix (Ranjit et al. 2011; Fischer et al. 2013). This protein contributes to cell lysis of dying cells (Patton et al. 2005). Calcium-chelating alizarin and other anthraquinones inhibit biofilm formation…

2.A.1.1.123.name: Sorbitol (D-Glucitol):H+ co-transporter, SOT1 (Km for sorbitol of 0.64 mM) of 509 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.123.description: Sorbitol (D-Glucitol):H+ co-transporter, SOT1 (Km for sorbitol of 0.64 mM) of 509 aas and 12 TMSs (Gao et al. 2003). SOT1 of P. cerasus is expressed throughout fruit development, but especially when growth and sorbitol accumulation rates are highest. In leaves, PcSOT1 expression is highest in young, expanding tissues, but substantially less in mature leaves (Gao et al. 2003).

2.A.1.1.124.name: The high affinity sugar:H+ symporter (sugar uptake) porter of 514 aas and 12 TMSs, STP10.
2.A.1.1.124.description: The high affinity sugar:H+ symporter (sugar uptake) porter of 514 aas and 12 TMSs, STP10. It transports glucose, galactose and mannose, and is therefore a hexose transporter (Rottmann et al. 2016). The 2.4 Å structure with glucose bound has been solved, explaining high affinity sugar recognition (Paulsen et al. 2019). The results suggest a proton donor/acceptor pair that links sugar transport to…

2.A.1.1.125.name: Glycerol:H+ symporter of 530 aas and 12 TMSs, GT1.
2.A.1.1.125.description: Glycerol:H+ symporter of 530 aas and 12 TMSs, GT1. It is essnetial for the glycerol repression of the alcohol oxidase 1 (AOX1 gene (Zhan et al. 2016), and plays a role in glycerol and methanol metabolism in Pichia pastoris (Li et al. 2017)..

2.A.1.1.126.name: Myo inositol uptake porter of 574 aas and 12 TMSs, Fst1.
2.A.1.1.126.description: Myo inositol uptake porter of 574 aas and 12 TMSs, Fst1. Also takes up the polyketide mycotoxin produced by Fusarium verticillioides during the colonization of maize kernels, Fumonisin B1 (FB1). The activity was demonstrated with the orthologue in Weissella verticillioides (Niu et al. 2016).

2.A.1.1.127.name: Hexose:proton symporter of 525 aas and 12 TMSs, Hxt5.
2.A.1.1.127.description: Hexose:proton symporter of 525 aas and 12 TMSs, Hxt5. Takes up D-glucose, D-fructose, D-xylose, D-mannose, D-galactose with decreasing affinity in this order (Rani et al. 2016).

2.A.1.1.128.name: Facilitative glucose-specific transporter (Km = 3 mM) of 486 aas and 12 TMSs, HT1; inhibited by cytochalasin B and localized to the midgut.
2.A.1.1.128.description: Facilitative (Na+-independent) glucose-specific transporter (Km = 3 mM) of 486 aas and 12 TMSs, HT1; inhibited by cytochalasin B and localized to the midgut (Price et al. 2007). The effect of sugar transporter 1 on the reproduction of Nilaparvata lugens (Hemiptera: Delphacidae) and trehalose metabolism have been described (Liu et al. 2025).

2.A.1.1.129.name: High-capacity facilitative transporter for trehalose, TRET1, required to induce anhydrobiosis.
2.A.1.1.129.description: High-capacity facilitative transporter for trehalose, TRET1, required to induce anhydrobiosis. Anhydrobiotic larvae can survive almost complete dehydration. Does not transport maltose, sucrose or lactose. Transports trehalose synthesized in the fat body and incorporates trehalose into other tissues that require a carbon source, thereby regulating trehalose levels in the hemolymph (Kikawada et al…

2.A.1.1.13.name: Fructose uniporter, GLUT5.
2.A.1.1.13.description: Fructose uniporter, GLUT5. The proteins from rat and cow have been crystalized and their structures have been determined in the open outward- and open inward-facing conformations, respectively. On the basis of comparisons of the inward-facing structures of GLUT5 and human GLUT1, a ubiquitous glucose transporter, a single point mutation proved to be enough to switch the substrate-binding…

2.A.1.1.130.name: Glucose transporter 1, GLUT1 or Slc2A1 of 491 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.130.description: Glucose transporter 1, GLUT1 or Slc2A1 of 491 aas and 12 TMSs. Expression occurs in the mesodermal region of Xenopus embryos, especially in the dorsal blastopore lip at the gastrula stage. It is an important player during gastrulation cell movement (Suzawa et al. 2007). This system is required for hepatocellular carcinoma proliferation and metastasis (Fang et al. 2021).
2.A.1.1.130.proteins: GLUT1 of Xenopus laevis (African clawed frog)

2.A.1.1.131.name: Myo-inositol-specific uptake transporter, ITR1 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.131.description: Myo-inositol-specific uptake transporter, ITR1 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs. The Km for myo-inositol is about 1 mM; glucose and other inositols are apparently not transported (Cushion et al. 2016).

2.A.1.1.133.name: Facilitative glucose transporter, GLUT2 of 503 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.133.description: Facilitative glucose transporter, GLUT2 of 503 aas and 12 TMSs. Evidence suggests that the blunt snout bream is able to regulate its ability to metabolize glucose by improving GLUT2, GK, and PK expression levels (Liang et al. 2018). The ortholog in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idellus) is exactly the same size and 98% identical throughout its length. It is found in the anterior and mid intestine…
2.A.1.1.133.proteins: GLUT2 of Megalobrama amblycephala (Chinese blunt snout bream) (Brema carp)

2.A.1.1.134.name: Sugar (mannose, fructose, glucose, galactose xylose) transporter of 521 aas and 12 TMSs, STP2.
2.A.1.1.134.description: Sugar (mannose, fructose, glucose, galactose xylose) transporter of 521 aas and 12 TMSs, STP2 (Liu et al. 2018).

2.A.1.1.135.name: Galactose-specific uptake porter of 515 aas and 12 TMSs, STP16.
2.A.1.1.135.description: Galactose-specific uptake porter of 515 aas and 12 TMSs, STP16 (Liu et al. 2018).

2.A.1.1.136.name: Monosaccharide uptake porter of 529 aas and 12 TMSs, STP7.
2.A.1.1.136.description: Monosaccharide uptake porter of 529 aas and 12 TMSs, STP7. Transports mannose, galactose, glucose and fructose, but not xylose (Liu et al. 2018).

2.A.1.1.137.name: Glycerol:H+ symporter,WaStl1, of 561 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.137.description: Glycerol:H+ symporter,WaStl1, of 561 aas and 12 TMSs. WaStl1 is a concentrative glycerol-H+ symporter with twice the affinity of S. cerevisiae. It is repressed by glucose and derepressed/induced by glycerol. This yeast, aerobically growing on glycerol, was found to produce ethanol, providing a redox escape to compensate the redox imbalance at the level of cyanide-resistant respiration (CRR) and…

2.A.1.1.138.name: Maltose permease, HPMAL2, of 582 aas and 12 TMSs in a 1 + 5 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.1.138.description: Maltose permease, HPMAL2, of 582 aas and 12 TMSs in a 1 + 5 + 6 TMS arrangement. Expression of both of the adjacent HPMAL1 and HPMAL2 genes is coordinately regulated, repressed by glucose, and induced by maltose (Viigand et al. 2005).

2.A.1.1.139.name: Glut3 or Slc2a3a of 541 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.139.description: Glut3 or Slc2a3a of 541 aas and 12 TMSs. Transcript analysis of zebrafish GLUT3 genes, slc2a3a and slc2a3b, have define overlapping as well as distinct expression domains in the central nervous system (Lechermeier et al. 2019).

2.A.1.1.14.name: Hexose:H+ symporter of 534 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.14.description: Hexose:H+ symporter of 534 aas and 12 TMSs. Substrate accumulation can be up to 1500-fold; one proton is symporter per hexose taken up. Helices I, V, VII and XI interact with the sugar during translocation and line the transport path through the membrane (Tanner 2000).

2.A.1.1.141.name: Lactose permease of 533 aas and 12 TMSs; 45% identical to 2.A.1.1.140.
2.A.1.1.141.description: Lactose permease of 533 aas and 12 TMSs; 45% identical to 2.A.1.1.140 (Havukainen et al. 2020).

2.A.1.1.142.name: MFS-type cellodextrin transporter, CdtG, of 538 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.142.description: MFS-type cellodextrin transporter, CdtG, of 538 aas and 12 TMSs (Havukainen et al. 2020).

2.A.1.1.146.name: MFS-type sugar/inositol transporter of 510 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.146.description: MFS-type sugar/inositol transporter of 510 aas and 12 TMSs. An orthologous system has been shown to be a highly specific L-arabinose transporter from Trichoderma reesei (Havukainen et al. 2021). Considering the high affinity for L-arabinose and low inhibition by D-glucose or D-xylose, Trire2_104072 could serve as a good candidate for improving the existing pentose-utilizing yeast strains…

2.A.1.1.147.name: MFS glucose transporter, Mfs1, of 550 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.147.description: MFS glucose transporter, Mfs1, of 550 aas and 12 TMSs. It is required for sugar transport, oxidative stress resistance, and pathogenicity of Colletotrichum gloeosporioides in Hevea brasiliensis (Liu et al. 2021). C. gloeosporioides is the causal agent of anthracnose in various plant species.

2.A.1.1.148.name: Glucose transporter 1, GLUT1, of 500 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.148.description: Glucose transporter 1, GLUT1, of 500 aas and 12 TMSs. EgGLUT1 Is crucial for the viability of Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto metacestode and may be a new therapeutic target (Amahong et al. 2021).

2.A.1.1.149.name: High affinity hexose transporter, HxtA of 531 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.149.description: High affinity hexose transporter, HxtA of 531 aas and 12 TMSs. HxtA is induced in vegetative hyphae upon starvation and in ascogenous hyphae during cleistothecium formation (Wei et al. 2004).

2.A.1.1.150.name: Hexose transporter-like protein, GCR1, of 541 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.150.description: Hexose transporter-like protein, GCR1, of 541 aas and 12 TMSs. Substrates include glucose, mannose and fructose. It functions in catabolite repression (as does Snf3p in S. cerevisiae (TC# 2.A.1.1.18)) of peroxisome biogenesis and of peroxisomal enzymes (Stasyk et al. 2004).

2.A.1.1.151.name: Facilitated trehalose transporter, Tret1-like, of 485 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.1.151.description: Facilitated trehalose transporter, Tret1-like, of 485 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Trehalose is the main blood sugar in insects and plays an important role in energy metabolism and stress resistance. Plutella xylostella (L.) is an agricultural pest worldwide. Tret1-like was cloned, knoched out and studied (Zhou et al. 2022). It was found that expression of the gene encoding…

2.A.1.1.152.name: INT7 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern.
2.A.1.1.152.description: INT7 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern. There are nine INT homologues in Populus trichocarpa, all presumed to transport inositor, and they are involved in stress responses (Zhang et al. 2023).
2.A.1.1.152.proteins: INT7 of Populus alba x Populus glandulosa

2.A.1.1.154.name: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 8 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.154.description: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 8 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs. Symbiotic cnidarians such as corals and anemones form highly productive and biodiverse coral reef ecosystems in nutrient-poor ocean environments, a phenomenon known as Darwin's paradox (Cui et al. 2023). Using the sea anemone Aiptasia, we show that during symbiosis, the increased availability of glucose and…

2.A.1.1.155.name: Sugar transporter ERD6-like 4 of 496 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.155.description: Sugar transporter ERD6-like 4 of 496 aas and 12 TMSs. Vacuolar sugar transporter EARLY RESPONSE TO DEHYDRATION 6-LIKE4 affects fructose signaling and plant growth (Khan et al. 2023).

2.A.1.1.158.name: Plastid glucose transporter 2, pGlcT2, of 493 aas and 12 TMSs. pGlcT2-GFP localized to the chloroplast envelope and is mainly produced in seedlings…
2.A.1.1.158.description: Plastid glucose transporter 2, pGlcT2, of 493 aas and 12 TMSs. pGlcT2-GFP localized to the chloroplast envelope and is mainly produced in seedlings and in the rosette centers of mature Arabidopsis plants. Therefore, pGlcT2 acts as a glucose importer that can limit cytosolic glucose availability in developing pGlcT2-overexpressing seedlings (Valifard et al. 2023). Possibly pGlcT2 contributes to a…

2.A.1.1.159.name: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 1a, Glut1 of 488 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.159.description: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 1a, Glut1 of 488 aas and 12 TMSs. Bisphenol S inhibits Glucose Transporter 1, leading to ATP excitotoxicity in the Zebrafish brain (Wang et al. 2024).

2.A.1.1.16.name: Low-affinity hexose (glucose, fructose, mannose, 2-deoxyglucose) uniporter.
2.A.1.1.16.description: Low-affinity hexose (glucose, fructose, mannose, 2-deoxyglucose) uniporter. The evolution of hexose transporters in kinetoplastid protozoans has been studied (Pereira and Silber 2012).

2.A.1.1.160.name: L-Arabinose high specificity and affinity uptake transporter of 514 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.1.160.description: L-Arabinose high specificity and affinity uptake transporter of 514 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. The system has low affinity for D-xylose and almost no affinity for D-glucose. It has use for bioengineering purposes (Havukainen et al. 2021). Due to its high affinity for L-arabinose and low inhibition by D-glucose or D-xylose, Trire2_104072 (AraE) could serve as a good candidate for…

2.A.1.1.161.name: MstH of 540 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.161.description: MstH of 540 aas and 12 TMSs. It is the major high-affinity glucose transporter with pleiotropic roles in carbon utilization regulation and citric acid production in Aspergillus niger (Bankaitis et al. 2025).

2.A.1.1.162.name: MFS traqnsporter of 527 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.162.description: MFS traqnsporter of 527 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.17.description: Glucose transporter of 884 aas and 12 TMSs with a 100 aa hydrophilic N-terminus and a 340 aas hydrophilic C-terminus.

2.A.1.1.18.name: Glucose/mannose/fructose transporter and high affinity sensor, Snf3p, (regulates glucose transport via other systems).
2.A.1.1.18.description: Glucose/mannose/fructose transporter and high affinity sensor, Snf3p, (regulates glucose transport via other systems). Residues involved in ligand preference are similar to those involved in transport (Dietvorst et al. 2010). Snf3p in Candida glabrata is essential for growth in low glucose media but not high glucose media, and plays a role in the induction of severall hexose transporters (Ng et…

2.A.1.1.19.name: Glucose transporter and low affinity sensor, Rgt2p (regulates glucose transport in conjunction with Snf3p).
2.A.1.1.19.description: Glucose transporter and low affinity sensor, Rgt2p (regulates glucose transport in conjunction with Snf3p). Rgt2 generates an intracellular signal in response to glucose that leads to inhibition of the Rgt1 transcriptional repressor and consequently to derepression of HXT genes encoding glucose transporters. They have unusually long C-terminal tails that bind to Mth1 and Std1, paralogous proteins…

2.A.1.1.2.name: Arabinose (xylose; galactose):H+ symporter, AraE (low affinity high capacity).
2.A.1.1.2.description: Arabinose (xylose; galactose):H+ symporter, AraE (low affinity high capacity) (Khlebnikov et al. 2001).

2.A.1.1.20.name: Myoinositol:H+ symporter, MIT
2.A.1.1.20.proteins: MIT of Leishmania donovani; most similar to ITRI of Saccharomyces cerevisiae

2.A.1.1.24.name: Hexose (Glucose and Fructose) transporter, PfHT1 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.24.description: Hexose (Glucose and Fructose) transporter, PfHT1 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs. This is the only hexose transporter, and it is found in the plasma membrane. It is an antimalarial drug target (Meier et al. 2018; Wunderlich 2022).

2.A.1.1.25.name: Myoinositol:H+ symporter, HMIT (also transport other inositols including scyllo-, muco- and chiro-, but not allo-inositol).
2.A.1.1.25.description: Myoinositol:H+ symporter, HMIT (also transport other inositols including scyllo-, muco- and chiro-, but not allo-inositol) (Aouameur et al., 2007). Expressed in the Golgi of the hippocampus and cortex. May also transport inositoltriphosphate (Di Daniel et al., 2009). Interacts directly with γ-secretase (9.B.47.1.1) to regulate its activity and the production of Abeta production, important in…

2.A.1.1.26.name: Major myoinositol:H+ symporter, IolT, of 473 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern.
2.A.1.1.26.description: Major myoinositol:H+ symporter, IolT, of 473 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern (Yoshida et al. 2002).

2.A.1.1.27.name: Minor, low affinity myoinositol:H+ symporter, IolF, of 438 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.27.description: Minor, low affinity myoinositol:H+ symporter, IolF, of 438 aas and 12 TMSs (Yoshida et al. 2002).

2.A.1.1.28.name: The erythrocyte/brain hexose facilitator, glucose transporter-1, Gtr1.
2.A.1.1.28.description: The erythrocyte/brain hexose facilitator, glucose transporter-1, Gtr1. SLC2a1 or Glut1. Transports D-glucose, dehydroascorbate, arsenite and the flavonone, quercetin, via one pathway and water via a distinct channel. Sugar transport has been suggested to function via a sliding mechanism involving several sugar binding sites (Cunningham et al., 2006). Glut1 is the receptor for human T-cell…

2.A.1.1.29.name: Glucosamine/glucose/fructose uniporter, Glut-2, Glut2 or ATG9A; it may also transport dehydroascorbate, and cotransports water against an osmotic…
2.A.1.1.29.description: Glucosamine/glucose/fructose uniporter, Glut-2, Glut2 or ATG9A; it may also transport dehydroascorbate (Mardones et al., 2011; Maulén et al., 2003), and cotransports water against an osmotic gradient (Naftalin, 2008). Mutations may give rise to the rare autosomal recessive Fanconi-Bickel syndrome (Batool et al. 2019). It mediates intestinal transport of quercetrin (Li et al. 2020) and can…

2.A.1.1.3.name: Xylose (xylopyranose):H+ symporter of 491 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.3.description: Xylose (xylopyranose):H+ symporter of 491 aas and 12 TMSs (Wambo et al. 2017). Also transports and binds D-glucose and 6-bromo-6-deoxy-D-glucose. The 3-d structure is known in three conformers, outward occluded, inward occluded and inward open (Sun et al. 2012: Quistgaard et al. 2013). Most of the sugar-binding residues are conserved with the human Glut-1, 2, 3 and 4 homologues. The coalescence…

2.A.1.1.30.name: Low affinity, constitutive, glucose (hexose; xylose) uniporter, Hxt4 (LGT1; Rag1).
2.A.1.1.30.description: Low affinity, constitutive, glucose (hexose; xylose) uniporter, Hxt4 (LGT1; Rag1) (also transports arsenic trioxide [As(OH)3] as do Hxtl, 3, 5, 7 and 9) (Liu et al., 2004). The Kluyveromyces lactis ortholog is 73% identical and is similarly regulated (Rolland et al. 2006). Key residues for efficient glucose transport by the hexose transporter CgHxt4 in the high sugar fermentation yeast Candida…

2.A.1.1.31.name: High affinity, glucose-repressible, glucose (hexose) uniporter (Hxt6/Hxt7).
2.A.1.1.31.description: High affinity, glucose-repressible, glucose (hexose) uniporter (Hxt6/Hxt7). Asn331 and hydrophobic residue side chains in TMS5 determine substrate affinity (Kasahara et al., 2011; Kasahara and Kasahara 2010). Also transports xylose (Wang et al. 2013). The F79S mutation in the hexose transporter HXT7 enhances xylose uptake, and five key aromatic hub residues (81W, 122F, 153Y, 208Y, and 492F) in…

2.A.1.1.34.name: The broad specificity sugar/sugar alcohol H+ symporter, AtPLT5 (expressed in roots, leaves and floral organs)
2.A.1.1.34.description: The broad specificity sugar/sugar alcohol (myo-inositol, glycerol, ribose, sorbitol, mannitol, xylitol, erythritol, etc) H+ symporter, AtPLT5 (transports a wide range of hexoses, pentoses, tetroses, sugar alcohols and a sugar acid, but not disaccharides) (Reinders et al., 2005) (expressed in roots, leaves and floral organs) (Klepek et al., 2004)

2.A.1.1.35.name: The major glucose (or 2-deoxyglucose) uptake transporter, GlcP
2.A.1.1.35.description: The major glucose (or 2-deoxyglucose) uptake transporter, GlcP (van Wezel et al., 2005)

2.A.1.1.36.name: The low affinity, glucose-inducible glucose transporter, MstE
2.A.1.1.36.description: The low affinity, glucose-inducible glucose transporter, MstE (Forment et al., 2006)

2.A.1.1.38.description: The glycerol:H+ symporter, Stl1p (Ferreira et al., 2005)

2.A.1.1.39.description: The high affinity glucose transporter, Hgt1 (Baruffini et al., 2006)

2.A.1.1.4.description: Glucose uniporter of 473 aas and 12 TMSs. Several GLUT isoforms, especially GLUT1 and GLUT3 in humans, are overexpressed in many tumors, and inhibitors have been identified (Kawatani and Osada 2025).

2.A.1.1.40.description: The xylose facilitator, Xylhp (Nobre et al., 1999)

2.A.1.1.41.description: The D-xylose:H+ symporter, XylT (Km=220 μM; inhibited competitively by 6-deoxyglucose (Ki=220 μM), but not by other sugars tested) (Chaillou et al., 1998)

2.A.1.1.42.name: The D-glucose:H+ symporter, GlcP (glucose uptake is inhibited by 2-deoxyglucose, mannose and galactose)
2.A.1.1.42.description: The D-glucose:H+ symporter, GlcP (glucose uptake is inhibited by 2-deoxyglucose, mannose and galactose) (Parche et al., 2006)

2.A.1.1.43.name: The monosaccharide (MST) (glucose > mannose > galactose > fructose):H+ symporter, MST1.
2.A.1.1.43.description: The monosaccharide (MST) (glucose > mannose > galactose > fructose):H+ symporter, MST1 (Schussler et al., 2006).

2.A.1.1.44.name: The hexose (glucose and fructose but not galactose) transporter (Glut11; SLC2A11)
2.A.1.1.44.description: The hexose (glucose and fructose but not galactose) transporter (Glut11; SLC2A11) (Scheepers et al., 2005)

2.A.1.1.45.name: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glucose transporter1, Vgt1 (important for seed germination and flowering)
2.A.1.1.45.description: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glucose transporter1, Vgt1 (important for seed germination and flowering) (Aluri and Büttner, 2007)

2.A.1.1.46.name: The blastocyst/testis glucose transporter, Glut8 (insulin stimulated in blastocysts).
2.A.1.1.46.description: The blastocyst/testis glucose transporter, Glut8 (Doege et al., 2000) (insulin stimulated in blastocysts) (Carayannopoulos et al., 2000).

2.A.1.1.47.name: The embryonic liver, kidney, and other tissue uric acid (urate) transporter, Glut9 (SLC2A9).
2.A.1.1.47.description: The embryonic liver, kidney, and other tissue uric acid (urate) transporter, Glut9 (SLC2A9) (Wright et al. 2010). Mutations in this transporter cause severe renal hyperuricemia. It transports hexoses as well as urate, the latter by an electrogenic uniport mechanism. It's transcription is regulated by a hepatocyte nuclear factor, HNF4α (Prestin et al. 2014).

2.A.1.1.48.name: The pentose/hexose transporter (sugar transport protein 2), STP2. (Expressed during pollen maturation and early stages of gametophyte development)
2.A.1.1.48.description: The pentose/hexose transporter (sugar transport protein 2), STP2. (Expressed during pollen maturation and early stages of gametophyte development) (Truernit et al., 1999)

2.A.1.1.49.name: The sink-specific, stress-regulated monosaccharide uptake porter, STP4.
2.A.1.1.49.description: The sink-specific, stress-regulated monosaccharide uptake porter, STP4. (Induced upon wounding or infection with bacteria or fungi; expressed in roots and flowers) (Truernit et al., 1996)

2.A.1.1.50.name: The glucose/fructose:H+ symporter, STP13 (sugar transport protein 13).
2.A.1.1.50.description: The glucose/fructose:H+ symporter, STP13 (sugar transport protein 13). Expressed in vascular tissues and induced during programmed cell death (Norholm et al., 2006). Used to combat bacterial infection by competing with them for sugars by phosphorylation of STP13 by the BAK1 receptor kinase (Yamada et al. 2016).

2.A.1.1.51.description: Glucose/xylose: H+ symporter, Gsx1 (Leandro et al., 2006)

2.A.1.1.52.description: The glucose transport protein, GTP1 (Skelly et al., 1994)

2.A.1.1.53.description: Myo-Inositol uptake porter, IolT1 (Km=0.2mM) (Krings et al., 2006). Can also transport D-glucose (Ikeda et al. 2011).

2.A.1.1.54.name: Myo-Inositol (Km=0.45mM) uptake porter, IolT2.
2.A.1.1.54.description: Myo-Inositol (Km=0.45mM) uptake porter, IolT2 (Krings et al., 2006). Can not transport D-glucose (Ikeda et al. 2011).

2.A.1.1.55.name: L-arabinose:proton symporter, AraE.
2.A.1.1.55.description: L-arabinose:proton symporter, AraE (Sa-Nogueira and Ramos, 1997). Also transports xylose, galactose and α-1,5 arabinobiose (Ferreira and Sá-Nogueira, 2010).
