2.A.1.1.57.name: High affinity (15 μM) glucose (monosaccharides including xylose):H+ symporter, MstA.
2.A.1.1.57.description: High affinity (15 μM) glucose (monosaccharides including xylose):H+ symporter, MstA (Jørgensen et al., 2007).

2.A.1.1.58.name: Low affinity glucose:H+ symporter, MstC.
2.A.1.1.58.description: Low affinity glucose:H+ symporter, MstC (Jørgensen et al., 2007).

2.A.1.1.59.name: The glucose transporter, GLUT10, was originally believed to be responsible for Type 2 diabetes.
2.A.1.1.59.description: The glucose transporter, GLUT10, was originally believed to be responsible for Type 2 diabetes. It is now believed to be responsible for arterial tortuosity, a rare autosomal recessive connective tissue disease (Callewaert et al., 2007). GLUT10 transports glucose and 2-deoxy glucose (Km=0.3 mM), and is inhibited by galactose and phloretin (Coucke et al., 2006).

2.A.1.1.6.name: Galactose, glucose uniporter, Gal2.
2.A.1.1.6.description: Galactose, glucose uniporter, Gal2. Also transports xylose (Wang et al. 2013). This transporter has been engineered by mutation (N376F) to transport xylose without being inhibited by glucose or transporting other hexoses (Farwick et al. 2014). The 3-d structure is known (Wang et al. 2015).

2.A.1.1.60.name: The major hexose transporter, Htr1
2.A.1.1.60.description: The major hexose transporter, Htr1 (mediates the active uptake of hexoses by sugar:H+ symport. Can transport glucose, 3-O-methylglucose, fructose, xylose, mannose, galactose, fucose, 2-deoxyglucose and arabinose. Confers sensitivity to galactose in seedlings. Km=20 uM for glucose) (Stadler et al., 2003; Boorer et al., 1994)

2.A.1.1.61.name: High affinity monosaccharide (Km = 25 µM) transporter, STP11 (expressed in pollen tubes).
2.A.1.1.61.description: High affinity monosaccharide (Km = 25 µM) transporter (takes up glucose, galactose, mannose, xylose and 3-O-methylglucose, but not fructose and ribose), STP11 (expressed in pollen tubes) (Schneidereit et al., 2005). This protein is also called Sugar Transport Protein (STP). Expression profiles of homologues in cabbage have been studied (Zhang et al. 2019).

2.A.1.1.62.name: High affinity (0.24mM) plasma membrane myoinositol-specific H+ symporter, INT4
2.A.1.1.62.description: High affinity (0.24mM) plasma membrane myoinositol-specific H+ symporter, INT4 (Schneider et al., 2006)

2.A.1.1.63.description: Low affinity inositol (myoinsoitol (Km = 1 mM), scylloinositol, d-chiroinositol and mucoinositol):H+ symporter (expressed in the anther tapetum, the vasculature, and the leaf mesophyll (Schneider et al., 2007)

2.A.1.1.64.name: The hexose sensor, Hxs1 (believed to be non-transporting)
2.A.1.1.64.description: The hexose sensor, Hxs1 (believed to be non-transporting) (Stasyk et al., 2008)

2.A.1.1.65.name: Glucose permease GlcP (most similar to 2.A.1.1.32)
2.A.1.1.65.description: Glucose permease GlcP (Pimentel-Schmitt et al., 2008) (most similar to 2.A.1.1.32)

2.A.1.1.66.name: The tonoplast H+:Inositol symporter 1, Int1 mediates efflux from the tonoplast to the cytoplasm (most similar to 2.A.1.1.63 and 2.A.1.1.62).
2.A.1.1.66.description: The tonoplast H+:Inositol symporter 1, Int1 (mediates efflux from the tonoplast to the cytoplasm (Schneider et al., 2008) (most similar to 2.A.1.1.63 and 2.A.1.1.62).

2.A.1.1.67.name: Glucose/xylose facilitator-1, GXF1 functions by sugar uniport; low affinity
2.A.1.1.67.description: Glucose/xylose facilitator-1, GXF1 (functions by sugar uniport; low affinity (Leandro et al., 2008)

2.A.1.1.69.name: Sugar & polyol transporter 1 (SPT1): broad specificity; takes up glucose.
2.A.1.1.69.description: Sugar & polyol transporter 1 (SPT1): broad specificity; takes up glucose (Schilling and Oesterhelt, 2007). Loss of the first 3 TMSs of the 12 TMSs does not prevent sugar uptake or sugar recognition but lowers substrate affinity & transport rate, and abolished H+ symport (Schilling and Oesterhelt, 2007).

2.A.1.1.71.name: Hexose (glucose) transporter, GT4 (D2) (almost identical to 2.A.1.1.16).
2.A.1.1.71.description: Hexose (glucose) transporter, GT4 (D2) (almost identical to 2.A.1.1.16). The L. infantum ortholog (A4I8N6) is 95% identical to this protein and is the dominant protein in the plasma membrane of this organims (Oliveira et al. 2020).
2.A.1.1.71.proteins: Hexose transporter, GT4 of Leishmania mexicana (B1PLM1)

2.A.1.1.72.name: The kidney basolateral urate efflux transporter (SLC2A9, URATv1 or GLUT9) (orthologue of 2.A.1.1.47).
2.A.1.1.72.description: The kidney basolateral urate efflux transporter (SLC2A9, URATv1 or GLUT9) (orthologue of 2.A.1.1.47) (Anzai et al., 2008). Human SLC2A9a and SLC2A9b isoforms mediate electrogenic transport of urate with different characteristics in the presence of hexoses (Witkowska et al., 2012). It transports hexoses, glucose and fructose, but not galactose, at a rate 50-fold slower than urate the latter by a…

2.A.1.1.73.name: Glycerol uptake permease (Glycerol:H+ symporter) Stl1. (Involved in salt stress relief) (similar to Stl1 of S. cerevisiae (2.A.1.1.38))
2.A.1.1.73.description: Glycerol uptake permease (Glycerol:H+ symporter) Stl1. (Involved in salt stress relief) (Kayingo et al. 2009) (similar to Stl1 of S. cerevisiae (2.A.1.1.38))

2.A.1.1.75.name: The fructose/xylose:H+ symporter, PMT1 (polyol monosaccharide transporter-1).
2.A.1.1.75.description: The fructose/xylose:H+ symporter, PMT1 (polyol monosaccharide transporter-1). Also transports other substrates at lower rates. PMT2 is largely of the same sequence and function. Both are present in pollen and young xylem cells (Klepek et al., 2005). A similar ortholog has been identifed in pollen grains of Petunia hybrida (Garrido et al. 2006).

2.A.1.1.76.name: Glucose transporter, GT1.
2.A.1.1.76.description: Glucose transporter, GT1. GT1, 2, and 3 are homologues. GT2 and GT3 transport ribose as well as glucose at different rates. GT3 transports ribose with 6-fold lower efficiency due to two threonines in GT3 that are alanines in GT2. They are in two loops between TMSs 3, 4, and 7, 8 (Naula et al., 2010). GT1 is expressed in the flagellar membrane and may be both a glucose transporter and sensor…

2.A.1.1.77.name: The D-glucose/D-ribose transporter, LmGT2 (Most similar to 1.A.1.1.18).
2.A.1.1.77.description: The D-glucose/D-ribose transporter, LmGT2 (Most similar to 1.A.1.1.18) (Naula et al., 2010).

2.A.1.1.78.name: The glucose transporter, LmGT3 (homologous to LmGT2 (1.A.1.1.75)).
2.A.1.1.78.description: The glucose transporter, LmGT3 (homologous to LmGT2 (1.A.1.1.75)). Two threonine residues located in the hydrophilic loops connecting TMSs 3 & 4 and 7 & 8 of GT3 prevent transport of D-ribose. Changing these two residues to alanine (as in GT2) allows transport of ribose. Thus, loops 3-4 and 7-8 partially determine substrate specificity (Naula et al., 2010).

2.A.1.1.80.name: Insulin-responsive facilitative glucose transporter in skeletal and cardiac muscle, adipose, and other tissues, Glut4 (GTR4; SLC2A4; 509aas).
2.A.1.1.80.description: Insulin-responsive facilitative glucose transporter in skeletal and cardiac muscle, adipose, and other tissues, Glut4 (GTR4; SLC2A4; 509aas). Defects in Glut4 cause noninsulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (NIDDM). Hyperinsulinemia leads to uncoupled insulin regulation of the GLUT4 glucose transporter and the FoxO1 transcription factor (Gonzalez et al., 2011). The first luminal loop confers insulin…

2.A.1.1.81.name: The glucose uptake porter, GluP.
2.A.1.1.81.description: The glucose uptake porter, GluP (Araki et al., 2011).

2.A.1.1.82.name: The cellobiose/cellotriose/cellotetraose/latose/cellodextrin transporter, Cdt-1 of 579 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.82.description: The cellobiose/cellotriose/cellotetraose/latose/cellodextrin transporter, Cdt-1 of 579 aas and 12 TMSs. It is a proton symporter with a Km of about 4 μM (Galazka et al., 2010).

2.A.1.1.83.name: The cellobiose/cellotriose/cellodextrin/lactose transporter, Cdt-2, of 525 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.83.description: The cellobiose/cellotriose/cellodextrin/lactose transporter, Cdt-2, of 525 aas and 12 TMSs. It functions by facilitated diffusion but with low efficiency and high affinity (Km = 3 μM). Mutations can increase its activity substantially (Lian et al. 2014). It appears to be capable of catalyzing efflux of 2'-fucosyllactose (2'FL), the most abundant oligosaccharide in human breast milk, following…

2.A.1.1.84.name: The heteromeric TMT1/TMT2 glucose/sucrose:H+ antiporter.
2.A.1.1.84.description: The heteromeric TMT1/TMT2 glucose/sucrose:H+ antiporter. Catalyzes glucose/sucrose antiport into vacuoles (Schulz et al., 2011).
2.A.1.1.84.proteins: The TMT1/2 sugar:H+ anti-porter of Arabidopsis thaliana. TMT1 (Q96290). TMT2 (Q8LPQ8).

2.A.1.1.86.name: The sea bream facilitative glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1).
2.A.1.1.86.description: The sea bream facilitative glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) (Balmaceda-Aguilera et al., 2012).

2.A.1.1.87.name: solute carrier family 2, member 12, Glut12 of 617 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.87.description: solute carrier family 2, member 12, Glut12 of 617 aas and 12 TMSs. In contrast to most mammalian members of this family, this protein has been reported to be a glucose:proton symporter (Wilson-O'Brien et al. 2010).

2.A.1.1.88.name: Solute carrier family 2 (facilitated glucose transporter), member 6, GLUT6 or SLC2A6, of 507 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.88.description: Solute carrier family 2 (facilitated glucose transporter), member 6, GLUT6 or SLC2A6, of 507 aas and 12 TMSs. Class III GLUTs (e.g., GLUT6, GLUT8, GLUT10, GLUT12) participate in redox balance, immunometabolism, intracellular trafficking, and proton-coupled substrate transport. They are also implicated in the pathophysiology of a wide range of common and serious diseases, including metabolic…

2.A.1.1.89.description: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 8 (Glucose transporter type 8) (GLUT-8) (Glucose transporter type X1)

2.A.1.1.91.description: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 3 (Glucose transporter type 3, brain) (GLUT-3 or GLUT3). It mediates the facilitative uptake of glucose, 2-deoxyglucose, galactose, mannose, xylose and fucose, and probably dehydroascorbate, but not fructose (Seatter et al. 1998, Deng et al. 2015). 2.A.1.1.99.name: Facilitated trehalose transporter Tret1-1 (DmTret1-1); transports trehalose with a Km of 11 mM.
2.A.1.1.99.description: Facilitated trehalose transporter Tret1-1 (DmTret1-1); transports trehalose with a Km of 11 mM (Kanamori et al. 2010). Tret1 orthologs of other insects examined have differing Km values (Apis mellifera, 9 mM; Anopheles gambiae, 46 mM, and Bombyx mori, 72 mM).

2.A.1.10.1.name: Nucleoside porter, NupG.
2.A.1.10.1.description: Nucleoside porter, NupG. Guanosine, inosine, cytidine and thymidine but not uridine, adenosine and xanthosine are transported (Patching et al. 2005). ADP-glucose is also a substrate of this system (Almagro et al. 2018Almagro et al. 2018).

2.A.1.10.2.name: Xanthosine porter, XapB.
2.A.1.10.2.description: Xanthosine porter, XapB. Xanthosine, inosine, adenosine, cytidine and thymidine but not guanosine and uridine are transported (Seeger et al. 1995). The Km for Xanthosine is 136 μM (Nørholm and Dandanell 2001). The transporter is encoded within an operon with xanthosine phosphorylase which is inactive in S. enterica but can be mutated to the active form (Hansen et al. 2006).

2.A.1.10.3.name: Putative low affinity ribonucleoside transporter, YegT, of 425 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.10.3.description: Putative low affinity ribonucleoside transporter, YegT, of 425 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.11.1.description: The oxalate:formate antiporter. Residues and TMSs involved in the translocation pathway and substrate binding have been identified (Fu and Maloney 1998; Fu et al. 2001; Ye and Maloney 2002; Wang et al. 2006). 2.A.1.11.11.name: PfMFSDT (PF3D7_0210300) is a drug exporter.
2.A.1.11.11.description: PfMFSDT (PF3D7_0210300) is a drug exporter (Maurya et al. 2024). It confers resistance to antifungal agents, ketoconazole and itraconazole. The nanomolar inhibitory effects of the drugs on the intra-erythrocytic growth of Plasmodium falciparum highlight their antimalarial properties. An assay to identify inhibitors of multiple validated and potential antimalarial drug targets has been developed…

2.A.1.11.3.description: Inner membrane protein BtsT or YhjX (probably a pyruvate:proton symporter that can also function as an exporter) (Vilhena et al. 2017). Regulated by Crp as well as the LytS-like histidine sensor kinase, BtsS or YehU, and the corresponding LytTR-like response regulator, BtsR or YehT (Kristoficova et al. 2017). Possibly induced by peptides as cells enter the stationary growth phase because they…
2.A.1.11.3.proteins: BtsT or YhjX of Escherichia coli

2.A.1.11.5.name: MFS-type transporter YcxA (ORF5) of 408 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.11.5.description: MFS-type transporter YcxA (ORF5) of 408 aas and 12 TMSs. Capable of exporting the peptide antibiotic, surfactin, synthsized by a non-ribosome mechanism in B. subtilis (Li et al. 2015).

2.A.1.12.1.name: The sialic acid porter, NanT, of 496 aas and 14 TMSs.
2.A.1.12.1.description: The sialic acid porter, NanT, of 496 aas and 14 TMSs. N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac) serves as a sole source of carbon and nitrogen for E. coli. It is a mucus-derived carbon source in the mammalian gut. NanT can also take up and allow efficient growth on the related sialic acids, N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc) and 3-keto-3-deoxy-d-glycero-d-galactonononic acid (KDN) (Hopkins et al. 2013)…

2.A.1.12.2.name: The lactate/pyruvate:H+ symporter of 616 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.12.2.description: The lactate/pyruvate:H+ symporter of 616 aas and 12 TMSs. Residues in the substrate translocation pathway have been reported (Soares-Silva et al., 2011). This systems and its orthologs in fungi have been reviewed (Guo et al. 2018).

2.A.1.12.3.name: Jen2 of 513 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.12.3.description: Jen2 of 513 aas and 12 TMSs. It is a dicarboxylic acid (succinate, malate, fumarate) uptake porter, and is subject to catabolite repression by glucose. It is induced during infection, being upregulated following the phagocytosis of C. albicans cells by neutrophils and macrophages. It may be important during early stages of virulence (Vieira et al. 2010). In the acid-tolerant yeast, Pichia…

2.A.1.12.4.name: Jen1 of 541 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.12.4.description: Jen1 of 541 aas and 12 TMSs. Zt is a monocarboxylate (lactate) uptake porter that is upregulated following the phagocytosis of Candida albicans cells by neutrophils and macrophages. It may be important for virulence (Soares-Silva et al. 2013; Vieira et al. 2010). It may be the only lactate uptake porter and is subject to glucose catabolite repression. However, growth on lactate affects biofilm…

2.A.1.13.1.name: The low affinity proton-linked monocarboxylate uptake/efflux porter. pH-gated succinate secretion regulates muscle remodeling in response to exercise.
2.A.1.13.1.description: The low affinity proton-linked monocarboxylate (lactate, pyruvate, mevalonate, branched chain oxo acids, β-hydroxybutyrate, γ-hydroxybutyrate, butyrate, acetoacetate, acetate and formate, succinate) uptake/efflux porter (Moschen et al. 2012; Reddy et al. 2020). pH-gated succinate secretion regulates muscle remodeling in response to exercise (Reddy et al. 2020). The structural basis of MCT1…

2.A.1.13.10.name: MCT8 (SLC16a2) homodimeric monocarboxylate thyroid hormone transporter 8 of 613 or 539 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.13.10.description: MCT8 (SLC16a2) homodimeric monocarboxylate thyroid hormone transporter 8 of 613 or 539 aas and 12 TMSs (Visser et al. 2009; Arjona et al., 2011). It is the X-linked mental retardation Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS) (a severe psychomotor retardation syndrome) protein (Schweizer and Köhrle 2012; Boccone et al. 2010; Johannes et al. 2016). Lack of MCT8 function produces serious neurological…

2.A.1.13.11.name: Solute carrier family 16, member 5 (monocarboxylic acid transporter 6) of 505 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.13.11.description: Solute carrier family 16, member 5 (monocarboxylic acid transporter 6) of 505 aas and 12 TMSs. Found on the luminal side of small intestinal epithelial cells (Kohyama et al. 2013). MCT6 mediates uptake of nateglinide, an oral hypoglycemic agent. The K(t) for nateglinide is 46 μM. Thus, MCT6 may play a role in the intestinal absorption of nateglinide, although other transporters are also likely to…

2.A.1.13.12.name: Solute carrier family 16, member 14 (monocarboxylic acid transporter 14), ATBo or MCT14.
2.A.1.13.12.description: Solute carrier family 16, member 14 (monocarboxylic acid transporter 14), ATBo or MCT14. Transports carnitine with low affinity (~ 1 mM) (Ingoglia et al. 2015). Its tissue localization in the mouse has been determined (Roshanbin et al. 2016).

2.A.1.13.13.name: solute carrier family 16, member 11 (monocarboxylic acid transporter 11)
2.A.1.13.13.description: solute carrier family 16, member 11 (monocarboxylic acid transporter 11)

2.A.1.13.14.name: Solute carrier family 16, member 12, SLC16A12, or monocarboxylic acid transporter 12; MCT12.
2.A.1.13.14.description: Solute carrier family 16, member 12, SLC16A12, or monocarboxylic acid transporter 12; MCT12. Facilitative monocarboxylate transporter that mediates creatine transport across the plasma membrane (Abplanalp et al. 2013; Takahashi et al. 2020). It is the cataract and glucosuria associated monocarboxylate transporter.

2.A.1.13.15.name: Monocarboxylate transporter 7 (MCT 7; mTORC1) (Monocarboxylate transporter 6) (MCT 6) of 523 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.13.15.description: Monocarboxylate transporter 7 (MCT 7; mTORC1) (Monocarboxylate transporter 6) (MCT 6) (Solute carrier family 16 member 6) of 523 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. SLC16a6, mTORC1, and autophagy regulate ketone body excretion in intestinal cells (Uebanso et al. 2023). Taurine is a substrate of this system (Higuchi 2024).

2.A.1.13.17.name: Monocarboxylate transporter 13 (MCT 13) (Solute carrier family SLC16 member 13).
2.A.1.13.17.description: Monocarboxylate transporter 13 (MCT 13) (Solute carrier family SLC16 member 13). Cephradine is a substrate of this system (Higuchi 2024), and uptake is stimulated by K+.

2.A.1.13.22.name: SLC16 Family protein of 771 aas and 12 TMSs, GEM-1.
2.A.1.13.22.description: SLC16 Family protein of 771 aas and 12 TMSs, GEM-1. GEM-1 acts in parallel to the GON-2 channel (TC# 1.A.4.5.10) to promote cation uptake within the developing gonad (Kemp et al. 2009).

2.A.1.13.23.name: Chicken MCT8 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.13.23.description: Chicken MCT8 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs. Transports pro-thyroid hormone, T4, with high affiinity, and T3 as well (Nele Bourgeois et al. 2016).

2.A.1.13.24.name: MCT10 (SLC16A10) of 400 aas and 11 TMSs.
2.A.1.13.24.description: MCT10 (SLC16A10) of 400 aas and 11 TMSs. Transports thyroid hormones, especially T3 (Nele Bourgeois et al. 2016).

2.A.1.13.25.name: Thyroid hormones (TH) transporter, MCT8 of 526 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.13.25.description: Thyroid hormones (TH) transporter, MCT8 of 526 aas and 12 TMSs (Zada et al. 2017). The mechanisms underlying MCT8-deficient brain development in various animal models including zebra fish and humans has been reviewed (Vancamp and Darras 2017).
2.A.1.13.25.proteins: TH transporter of Danio rerio (Zebrafish) (Brachydanio rerio)

2.A.1.13.26.name: Thyroid hormones (TH) transporter, MCT10 of 505 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.13.26.description: Thyroid hormones (TH) transporter, MCT10 of 505 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.13.27.name: MfsG of 447 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.13.27.description: MfsG of 447 aas and 12 TMSs. Exports fungicides such as glucosinolates and isothiocyanates. Exposure to glucosinolate-breakdown products induces expression of mfsG. MfsG functions in fungitoxic compound efflux (Vela-Corcía et al. 2019).
2.A.1.13.27.proteins: MfsG of Botryotinia fuckeliana (Noble rot fungus) (Botrytis cinerea)

2.A.1.13.3.name: The thyroid hormone transporter, MCT8.
2.A.1.13.3.description: The thyroid hormone transporter, MCT8 (transports L- and D-isomers of thyroxine (T4), 3,3',5-triiodothyronine (T3), 3,3'5'-triiodothyronine (rT3) and 3,3'-diiodothyronine [Km values = 2-5 μM; Leu, Phe, Trp and Tyr were not transported]) (Friesema et al., 2003). Loss of function mutations in MCT8 leads to Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome, severe X-linked psychomotor retardation and elevated serum T3…

2.A.1.13.4.name: The high affinity (17 μM) facilitated diffusion, riboflavin-regulated riboflavin uptake system, Mch5
2.A.1.13.4.description: The high affinity (17 μM) facilitated diffusion, riboflavin-regulated riboflavin uptake system, Mch5 (Reihl and Stolz, 2005)

2.A.1.13.5.name: Low affinity monocarboxylate transporter-2 (MCT2).
2.A.1.13.5.description: Low affinity monocarboxylate transporter-2 (MCT2). Transports γ-hydroxybutyrate (Wang and Morris, 2007). MCT2 requires the ancillary protein, embigin (Q6PCB8; 8.A.23.1.2) for plasma membrane localization (Ovens et al., 2010). It is present in neurons but not astrocytes where the low affinity MCT1 and MCT4 predominate (Hertz and Dienel 2013). Partially localizes to the peroxysomal membrane (Visser…

2.A.1.13.6.name: Plasma membrane proton-linked monocarboxylate transporter, MCT4 or MCT-4 (SLC16A3).
2.A.1.13.6.description: Plasma membrane proton-linked monocarboxylate transporter, MCT4 or MCT-4 (SLC16A3). It catalyzes the rapid low affinity plasma membrane transport of many monocarboxylates such as lactate, pyruvate, branched-chain oxo acids derived from leucine, valine and isoleucine, and the ketone bodies acetoacetate, beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetate. It is the main transporter that catalyzes lactate efflux from…

2.A.1.13.7.name: Monocarboxylate transporter-5 (MCT5 or SLC16A4; sometimes referred to as MCT4).
2.A.1.13.7.description: Monocarboxylate transporter-5 (MCT5 or SLC16A4; sometimes referred to as MCT4). Lactate transport via the MCT5 is non enzymatically stimulated by carbonic anhydrase II (Becker et al., 2010). MCTs require an ancillary 1TMS glycoprotein, either Embigin (Q6PCB8; TC# 8.A.23.1.2) or basigin (P35613; TC# 8.A.23.1.1) for plasma membrane localization (Ovens et al., 2010). Upregulated in some cancers and…

2.A.1.13.8.name: Monocarboxylate transporter, MCT10.
2.A.1.13.8.description: Monocarboxylate transporter, MCT10. Transports thyroid horomones as well as aromatic amino acids (Visser et al., 2010). Primary and secondary thyroid hormone transporters have been reviewed (Kinne et al., 2011). Deafness and loss of cochlear hair cells occurs in the absence of thyroid hormone transporters, Slc16a2 (Mct8) and Slc16a10 (Mct10) (Sharlin et al. 2018). Tissue-specific functions of…

2.A.1.13.9.name: Short chain monocarboxylate (lactate) transporter 3, MCT3.
2.A.1.13.9.description: Short chain monocarboxylate (lactate) transporter 3, MCT3. MCT1, 3 and 4 require the ancillary protein, basigin (P35613; 8.A.23.1.1) for plasma membrane localization (Ovens et al., 2010).

2.A.1.14.1.name: Glucarate porter, GudT, of 455 aas and 12 TMSs.

Hydrogen-stimulated carbon acquisition in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimuriumhas been described (Lamichhane-Khadka et al. 2011). Additionally, a link between gut community metabolism and pathogenesis: molecular hydrogen-stimulated glucarate catabolism aids Salmonella virulence (Lamichhane-Khadka et al. 2013).

2.A.1.14.15.description: Apical membrane renal proximal tubular voltage-driven but Na+-independent organic anion transporter, OATv1 (transports p-aminohippurate; probably transports organic anions but not cations and not inorganic phosphate. 2.A.1.14.19.description: Plasma membrane, high affinity vitamin H transporter 1 (H+:biotin symporter), Vht1 (Stolz, 2003)

2.A.1.14.2.description: Hexuronate (glucuronate; galacturonate) porter, ExuT (Nemoz et al. 1976). It also transports D-glucose (Kim et al. 2020).

2.A.1.14.22.description: The chloroplast thylakoid Na+:phosphate symporter, ANTR1 (512aas) (Pavón et al., 2008). Residues essential for function have been identified (Ruiz-Pavón et al., 2010).

2.A.1.14.23.description: Vesicular glutamate transporter #3 (VGLUT3) [Its absence in mice causes sensorineural deafness and seizures]. 70% identical to VGLUT2 (TC# 2.A.1.14.16) (Gras et al., 2002). 2.A.1.14.24.name: Intestinal mucosal sodium/phosphate symporter, SLC17A4.
2.A.1.14.24.description: Intestinal mucosal sodium/phosphate symporter, SLC17A4. Maintains phosphate homeostasis; mediates intestinal absorption, bone deposition and resorption and renal excretion.

2.A.1.14.25.description: The putative D-mannuronate porter, AlgT (Rodionov et al., 2010).

2.A.1.14.26.description: The plasma membrane Lethal (2)01810 glutamate uptake porter (Km=0.07μM) (Inhibited by aspartate) (Shim et al., 2011)

2.A.1.14.27.name: Voltage-driven Na+:phosphate cotransporter; solute carrier family 17, member 1.
2.A.1.14.27.description: Voltage-driven Na+:phosphate cotransporter; solute carrier family 17, member 1. Orthologous to 2.A.1.14.6. Transports other anions including urate; functions in urate cell elimination at the renal apical membrane (Prestin et al. 2014).

2.A.1.14.28.description: Solute carrier family 17 (sodium phosphate), member 3. Catalyzes voltage-driven Na+:phosphate cotransport, but also functions in cell elimination of urate at renal tubular cell apical membranes (Prestin et al. 2014).

2.A.1.14.29.description: Sodium-dependent phosphate transport protein 3 (Na(+)/PI cotransporter 3) (Sodium/phosphate cotransporter 3) (Solute carrier family 17 member 2)

2.A.1.14.3.description: Putative tartrate porter, TtuB or TUB3, of 449 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.14.30.description: Vesicular glutamate transporter 1, VGluT1 or PNP1 of 560 aas and 12 TMSs. Brain-specific Na+-dependent inorganic phosphate cotransporter; Solute carrier family 17 member 7). Several proteins must be retrieved to the synaptic vesicle before it can export neurotransmitters, and cargo retrieval is a collective cargo-driven process, dependent on VGluT1 (Pan et al. 2015). 2.A.1.14.31.name: Vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (VGluT2) (Differentiation-associated BNPI) (Solute carrier family 17 member 6, SLC17A6).
2.A.1.14.31.description: Vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (VGluT2) (Differentiation-associated BNPI) (Differentiation-associated Na+-dependent inorganic phosphate cotransporter) (Solute carrier family 17 member 6, SLC17A6). It has 582 aas with 12 probable TMSs. It is expressed in different nerve fibre populations that selectively contact pulmonary neuroepithelial bodies (Brouns et al. 2004). 2.A.1.14.32.name: Vesicular glutamate transporter 3 (VGluT3) (Solute carrier family 17 member 8).
2.A.1.14.32.description: Vesicular glutamate transporter 3 (VGluT3) (Solute carrier family 17 member 8). Loss in mice produces circadian-dependent hyperdopaminergia and amiliorates motor disfunction and dopa-mediated dyskinesias in a model of Parkinson's Disease (Divito et al. 2015). VGLUT3 is expressed selectively in the inner hair cells (IHCs) and transports the neurotransmitter glutamate into synaptic vesicles…

2.A.1.14.33.name: L-galactonate transporter, YjjL or DgoT of 460 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.14.33.description: L-galactonate transporter, YjjL or DgoT of 460 aas and 12 TMSs. The D-galactonate transporter DgoT has been solved at atomic resolution (Dmitrieva et al. 2024). Protonation of D46 and E133 precedes galactonate binding, and substrate binding induces closure of the extracellular gate, with the conserved R47 coupling substrate binding to transmembrane helix movement. After isomerization to an…
2.A.1.14.33.proteins: YjjL or DgoT of Escherichia coli

2.A.1.14.38.name: Transporter YIL166c of 542 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.14.38.description: Transporter YIL166c (Hellborg et al. 2008) of 542 aas and 12 TMSs. May transport inorganic sulfur-containing compounds such as sulfate, sulfite, thiosulfate and sulfonates.

2.A.1.14.4.name: Dipeptide (e.g., Gly-Leu), allantoate, ureidosuccinate, allantoin porter.
2.A.1.14.4.description: Dipeptide (e.g., Gly-Leu), allantoate, ureidosuccinate, allantoin porter (Cai et al., 2007).

2.A.1.14.40.name: Glucarate transporter, GudP.
2.A.1.14.40.description: Glucarate transporter, GudP. Encoded in an operon with GudD, a glucarate dehydratase (Moraes and Reithmeier 2012).

2.A.1.14.41.description: The Aldohexuronate (glucuronate, galacturonate) uptake porter (Valmeekam et al. 2001).

2.A.1.14.42.name: Vesicular glutamate transporter, EAT-4/VGLUT of 576 aas.
2.A.1.14.42.description: Vesicular glutamate transporter, EAT-4/VGLUT of 576 aas (Serrano-Saiz et al. 2013). EAT-4 is responsible for loading glutamate into synaptic vesicles, and thus in defining the glutamatergic phenotype of a neuron (Serrano-Saiz et al. 2013).

2.A.1.14.43.name: Uncharacterized but putative sulfonate (and other inorganic sulfur-containing compounds) uptake transporter of 537 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.14.43.description: Uncharacterized but putative sulfonate (and other inorganic sulfur-containing compounds) uptake transporter of 537 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.14.44.name: Vesicular Glutamate transporter, VGlut of 632 aas and 10 TMSs with the N- and C-termini in the cytoplasm.
2.A.1.14.44.description: Vesicular Glutamate transporter, VGlut of 632 aas and 10 TMSs with the N- and C-termini in the cytoplasm (Fei et al. 2007).

2.A.1.14.46.name: Vesicular glutamate transporter, VGLU-2, of 573 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.14.46.description: Vesicular glutamate transporter, VGLU-2, of 573 aas and 12 TMSs. In addition to being present in nerve cells, it may play a role in collagen trafficking in the skin. The C. elegans SLC17A6/7/8 family members probaly have diverse functions within and outside the nervous system (Serrano-Saiz et al. 2019).

2.A.1.14.48.name: MFS general substrate transporter of 451 aas and 12 TMSs, MFS-3-6.
2.A.1.14.48.description: MFS general substrate transporter of 451 aas and 12 TMSs, MFS-3-6. It facilitates the export of lactate from the cell under acidic conditions (Tian et al. 2022).

2.A.1.14.5.name: Phthalate porter, Pht1 of 451 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.14.5.description: Phthalate porter, Pht1 of 451 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.14.50.description: MFS carrier, a putative drug exporter of 450 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. It exports polymyxin B, CCCP and verapamil (Gao et al. 2023).

2.A.1.14.51.name: Vacuoloar glutamate transporter 1, VGLUT1 of 483 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.14.51.description: Vacuoloar glutamate transporter 1, VGLUT1 of 483 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Regulatory mechanisms of the six glutamate transporters (3 excitatory and 3 vesicular) in the response of the pacific oyster upon high-temperature stress have been studied (Zhang et al. 2024).
2.A.1.14.51.proteins: VGLUT1 of the pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas)

2.A.1.14.6.name: Na:Pi symporter, NPT1 or SLC17A1..
2.A.1.14.6.description: Na:Pi symporter, NPT1 or SLC17A1. (Renal chloride-dependent polyspecific anion exporter; transports organic acids such as p-aminohippurate, ureate, and acetylsalicylate (asprin)). Catalyzes ureate excretion. A mutant form shows increased risk of gout in humans.

2.A.1.15.10.description: The gentisate (2,5-dihydroxybenzoate) uptake porter, GenK (does not take up either benzoate or 3-hydoxybenzoate).

2.A.1.15.14.description: Probable uptake transporter for 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D), CadK (Kitagawa et al. 2002).

2.A.1.15.7.name: Aromatic compound (benzoate) uptake transporter of 450 aas.
2.A.1.15.7.description: Aromatic compound (benzoate) uptake transporter of 450 aas (Clark et al. 2002).

2.A.1.16.7.description: Ferri-siderophore transporter, MirB. Transports hydroxamate siderophores such as triacetylfusarinine C (TAFC) (Raymond-Bouchard et al. 2012).

2.A.1.16.9.name: Siderophore iron transporter 3, Str3 of 630 aas and 14 TMSs in a 6 + 7 + 1 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.16.9.description: Siderophore iron transporter 3, Str3 of 630 aas and 14 TMSs in a 6 + 7 + 1 TMS arrangement. It transports siderophore iron and so plays a role in iron homeostasis (Pelletier et al. 2003). It also transports heme, and the peroxiredoxin, Tpx1 (Q74887; 192 aas and 0 - 2 possible TMSs), is a binding partner of Str3 (Normant et al. 2020). 2.A.1.17.1.description: Cyanate transport system, CynT. Encoded with cyanate aminohydrolase, CynS, and carbonic anhydrase, CynX (Anderson et al. 1990; Moraes and Reithmeier 2012).

2.A.1.17.2.description: Glucose transporter, OEOE_0819. Does not transport fructose (Kim et al., 2011)

2.A.1.17.3.description: Inner membrane transport protein, NimT or YeaN of 393 aas and 12 TMSs. It exports 2-nitroimidazole from the cytoplasm, confering resistance to this anitbiotic, and transcription of this gene as well as NimO, within the same operon, is regulated by the repressor, NimR (YeaM) (Ogasawara et al. 2015).

2.A.1.18.1.description: D-Arabinitol:H+ symporter of 425 aas and 12 TMSs, DalT (Heuel et al. 1997; Heuel et al. 1998).

2.A.1.18.2.description: Ribitol:H+ symporter of 427 aas and 12 TMSs, RbtT (Heuel et al. 1997; Heuel et al. 1998).

2.A.1.19.10.description: The apical proximal tubular kidney/placenta organic anion transporter 4, Oat4 (Slc22a11) (transports estrone sulfate (Km = 1 µM), dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (Km = 60µM), many anionic drugs, diuretics, bile salts, urate and ochratoxin A). 2.A.1.19.11.description: The apical proximal tubular renal urate:anion exchanger, URAT1 (Slc22a12). 2.A.1.19.12.name: The high affinity L-carnitine transporter, CT2, present in the luminal membranes of epididymal epithelia and Sertoli cells of the testis.
2.A.1.19.12.description: The high affinity L-carnitine transporter, CT2, present in the luminal membranes of epididymal epithelia and Sertoli cells of the testis (Enomoto et al., 2002b). It also catalyzes uptake of the anticancer polyamine analogue, bleomycin-A5 (Aouida et al. 2010). Carnitine transport and metabolism have been reviewed (Nałęcz and Nałęcz 2017). 2.A.1.19.13.name: The organic cation transporter, Oct1 (transports L-carnitine; expressed in vascular tissues of various organs and at sites of lateral root formation).
2.A.1.19.13.description: The organic cation transporter, Oct1 (transports L-carnitine; expressed in vascular tissues of various organs and at sites of lateral root formation) (Lelandais-Briere et al, 2007). It also transports spermine and other polyamines and is induced by them (Sagor et al. 2016). It protects against the polyamine, cadaverine, which affects root length (Strohm et al. 2015).

2.A.1.19.14.description: Brush border glycosylated urate (Km= 1.2 mM) tranporter, RST. Orthologous to the human URAT1. 2.A.1.19.15.description: The liver multispecific organic anion transporter, NLT or OAT2. Transports salicylate, KM=90µM, acetylsalicylate, prostaglandin E2, dicarboxylate, p-aminohippurate, etc. (Sekine et al., 1998)

2.A.1.19.17.description: Kidney organic cation transporter-like 3 ORCTL-3 (OAT10; SLC22A13; Like-3) (Bahn et al., 2008) (transports nicotinate, p-aminohippurate and urate; KM=20-40 mμM) via exchange for lactate). 2.A.1.19.18.name: Oranic anion transporter, Oat7 (exchanges sulfate conjugates (steroids) and other anions for butyrate).
2.A.1.19.18.description: Oranic anion transporter, Oat7 (exchanges sulfate conjugates (steroids) and other anions for butyrate) (Shin et al., 2007). SLC22A9 and SLC29A2 are transporters mediating cellular uptake of 3,5,3'-Triiodothyroacetic acid (TRIAC), a T3-receptor agonist pharmacologically used in patients to mitigate T3 resistance. SLC22A9 encodes the organic anion transporter 7 (OAT7), a sodium-independent organic…

2.A.1.19.19.name: The rat kidney basolateral potential-driven symport carrier, Oct2 (transports tetraethylammonium and many other organic cations).
2.A.1.19.19.description: The rat kidney basolateral potential-driven symport carrier, Oct2 (transports tetraethylammonium and many other organic cations) (Sweet and Pritchard 1999). 2.A.1.19.2.name: The ergothionine/carnitine/hydroxyurea/organic zwitterion transporter, OCTN1 or SVOP (SLC22A4).
2.A.1.19.2.description: The ergothionine/carnitine/hydroxyurea/organic zwitterion transporter, OCTN1 or SVOP (SLC22A4). 2.A.1.19.20.description: Prostaglandin (PGE2, PGE2α, and PGD(2)) -specific organic anion transporter. Exhibits Na+ -independent and saturable transport. Shows narrow substrate selectivity and high affinity (Shiraya et al., 2010).

2.A.1.19.24.name: Solute carrier family 22 member 3 (Extraneuronal monoamine transporter) (EMT) (Organic cation transporter 3) of 556 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.19.24.description: Solute carrier family 22 member 3 (Extraneuronal monoamine transporter) (EMT) (Organic cation transporter 3) of 556 aas and 12 TMSs. Induction of astrocytic Slc22a3 (EMT) regulates sensory processing through histone serotonylation (Sardar et al. 2023).

2.A.1.19.25.name: Solute carrier family 22 member 7 (liver transporter) (hOAT2), transports cyclic nucleotodes and the anti-viral drug, acyclovir.

2.A.1.2.41.description: The tetracycline resistance determinant, TetA42 from a deep terrestrial subsurface bacterium (Brown et al., 2008).
2.A.1.2.41.proteins: TetA42 of Micrococcus sp. SMCC G8878 (B2YGG2)

2.A.1.2.42.name: The multidrug efflux pump, EmrD-3.
2.A.1.2.42.description: The multidrug efflux pump, EmrD-3 (exports ethidium, linezolid, tetraphenylphosphonium chloride, rifampin, erythromycin, minocycline, trimethoprim, chloramphenicol, and rhodamine) (Smith et al., 2009).

2.A.1.2.43.name: The multidrug efflux pump, Qdr3 (exports polyamines, quinidine, barban, cisplatin and bleomycin).
2.A.1.2.43.description: The multidrug efflux pump, Qdr3 (exports polyamines, quinidine, barban, cisplatin and bleomycin). The two halves of the protein each have an N-terminal. 150 residue hydrophilic region found in many fungi followed by a 200 residue, 6 TMS, transmembrane region. This suggests that an intragenic duplication event gave rise to 12 TMS proteins independently of most other MFS carriers, but this has not…

2.A.1.2.44.name: Diglucosyl-diacylglycerol exporter or flippase, LtaA (lipoteichoic acid protein A).
2.A.1.2.44.description: Diglucosyl-diacylglycerol exporter or flippase, LtaA (lipoteichoic acid protein A) (Gründling and Schneewind, 2007).

2.A.1.2.45.name: The fructose-specific uniporter, Ffz1 69% identical to Ffz2 (2.A.1.2.46) and 66% identical to (2.A.1.2.23).
2.A.1.2.45.description: The fructose-specific uniporter, Ffz1 (69% identical to Ffz2 (2.A.1.2.46) and 66% identical to (2.A.1.2.23) (Leandro et al., 2011).

2.A.1.2.46.name: The fructose/glucose uniporter, Ffz2 (64% identical to 2.A.1.2.23).
2.A.1.2.46.description: The fructose/glucose uniporter, Ffz2 (64% identical to 2.A.1.2.23). Both sugars are transported with similar affinities and efficiencies (Leandro et al., 2011).

2.A.1.2.47.name: The multidrug resistance efflux pump, HsMDR (YfmO2).
2.A.1.2.47.description: The multidrug resistance efflux pump, HsMDR (YfmO2). Exports drugs such as fluoroquinolones and chloramphenicol (Vardy et al., 2005).

2.A.1.2.49.name: Putative tetracycline resistance protein
2.A.1.2.49.proteins: Putative tet resistance pump of Pyrobaculum aerophilum (Q8ZUX8)

2.A.1.2.5.name: Multidrug (14- and 15-membered macrolides, lincosamides, streptogramins, tetracyclines, daunomycin, ethidium bromide, etc.):H+ antiporter, LmrP.
2.A.1.2.5.description: Multidrug (14- and 15-membered macrolides, lincosamides, streptogramins, tetracyclines, daunomycin, ethidium bromide, etc.):H+ antiporter, LmrP. Two proton translocation pathways have been proposed (Bapna et al., 2007), but Schaedler and van Veen, 2010 have provided evidence that a flexible cation binding site in LmrP is associated with variable proton coupling. Basic residues R260 and K357…

2.A.1.2.51.name: Chloramphenicol resistance pump, CraA (43% identical to MdfA of E. coli).
2.A.1.2.51.description: Chloramphenicol resistance pump, CraA (43% identical to MdfA of E. coli) (Roca et al., 2009). It is a broad specificity transporter exporting chloramphenicol, thiamphenicol, florfenicol, ethidium, dequalinium, chlorhexidine, benzalkonium, mitomycin C and TPP+. Glu-38 is essential for activity (Foong et al. 2019).

2.A.1.2.52.name: Puromycin resistance MDR protein, MdtM.
2.A.1.2.52.description: Puromycin resistance MDR protein, MdtM (Soo et al., 2011). Also catalyzes bile salt:H+ antiport, and binds cholate and deoxycholate to the protein with micromolar affinity. Functions as an MDR pump (Nishino and Yamaguchi 2001). Acts synergistically with AcrAB-TolC (Paul et al. 2014). The ortholog has been characterized in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi, and specific residues have been shown to…

2.A.1.2.53.name: MDR pump, SLC22A18 in lung cancer cells.
2.A.1.2.53.description: MDR pump, SLC22A18 in lung cancer cells (Lei et al., 2012). It has 424 aas and 12 TMSs. Allelic loss in the absence of mutations in the polyspecific transporter gene BWR1A on 11p15.5 in hepatoblastoma has been shown (Albrecht et al. 2004).

2.A.1.2.55.name: Peptide exporter (Ala-Gln and Ala-branched chain amino and dipeptides).
2.A.1.2.55.description: Peptide exporter (Ala-Gln and Ala-branched chain amino and dipeptides) (Hayashi et al., 2010). May also export arabinose (but not xylose) and function as an MDR pump (Koita and Rao 2012).

2.A.1.2.6.name: (Benomyl, cycloheximide, methotrexate, fluconazole, etc.):H+ antiporter, CaMDR1.
2.A.1.2.6.description: (Benomyl, cycloheximide, methotrexate, fluconazole, etc.):H+ antiporter, CaMDR1 (Basso et al., 2010; Cannon et al., 1998). MDR1 catalyzes efflux of commonly used azoles. The central cytoplasmic loop is critical for MDR function, but does not impart substrate specificity (Mandal et al., 2012). The structural basis for polyspecificity of MDR MFS transporters, based on studies with Mdr1, is the…

2.A.1.2.60.name: YajR of 454 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.60.description: YajR of 454 aas and 12 TMSs. The 3-D structure in the outward-facing conformation is available at 3.15Å resolution, and the cytoplasmic C-terminal YAM domain has been solved to 1.07Å resolution. This 65 aa YAM domain is thought to control the conformational states of the protein (Jiang et al. 2013; Jiang et al. 2014).

2.A.1.2.62.name: Putative MDR pump, YdhC or PunC.
2.A.1.2.62.description: Putative MDR pump, YdhC or PunC. It has been reporte to export arabinose but not xylose (Koita and Rao 2012). However, it also takes up adenosine, adenine, deoxyadenosine, and other purine nucleosides and nucleobases such as inosine and guanosine as sole nitrogen sources. It also takes up various sulfonamides such as sulfathiazole, sulfadiazine and sulfamethoxazole. Expression of the punC gene is…

2.A.1.2.68.name: Tetracycline resistance protein, class B (TetA(B)) (Metal-tetracycline/H+ antiporter).
2.A.1.2.68.description: Tetracycline resistance protein, class B (TetA(B)) (Metal-tetracycline/H+ antiporter). Mutants defective in either transport or tetracycline binding have been isolated (Wright and Tate 2015). Several amino acid substitutions (i.e., D190C, E192C and S201C) alter the specificity of the porter so that it prefers deoxycycline (3x) and minochcline (6x) over tetracycline (Sapunaric and Levy 2005).

2.A.1.2.7.name: Bicyclomycin, sulfathiazole, tetracycline, fosfomycin, acriflavin, etc.):H+ antiporter.
2.A.1.2.7.description: Bicyclomycin, sulfathiazole, tetracycline, fosfomycin, acriflavin, etc.):H+ antiporter (Nishino and Yamaguchi 2001). Also exports L-cysteine (Yamada et al., 2006).

2.A.1.2.73.name: Major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 10, MFSD10, a member of the SLC18 family.
2.A.1.2.73.description: Major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 10, MFSD10, a member of the SLC18 family. It is a tetracycline exporter-like protein. This protein is found in the inner nuclear membrane (Cheng et al. 2019) and is a disease protein in humans (Bagchi et al. 2020). Its gene shows increased expression with increased energy consumption (Bagchi et al. 2020). It may confers cellular resistance…

2.A.1.2.76.name: Major facilitator copper transporter 1, Mfc1.
2.A.1.2.76.description: Major facilitator copper transporter 1, Mfc1. Takes up copper in meiotic sporulating cells; present in the forespore membrane. Induced under copper limitation. Required for normal forespore development and spore copper-dependent amine oxidase activity (Beaudoin et al. 2011).

2.A.1.2.77.name: CefT confers phenylacetate resistance.
2.A.1.2.77.description: CefT confers phenylacetate resistance (Fernández-Aguado et al. 2012). It has been reported to be a hydrophilic beta-lactam transporter that is involved in the secretion of hydrophilic beta-lactams containing an α-aminoadipic acid side chain (isopenicillin N, penicillin N and deacetylcephalosporin C) (Cesareo et al. 2007; Ullán et al. 2002).

2.A.1.2.79.name: The host-nonselective polyketide perylenequinone toxin, cercosporin, exporter, Ctb4.
2.A.1.2.79.description: The host-nonselective polyketide perylenequinone toxin, cercosporin, exporter, Ctb4 (Choquer et al. 2007).

2.A.1.2.8.name: (Spermidine; fluoroquinolones, acriflavin, chloramphenicol, ethidium bromide, etc.):H+ antiporter.
2.A.1.2.8.description: (Spermidine; fluoroquinolones, acriflavin, chloramphenicol, ethidium bromide, etc.):H+ antiporter (Woolridge et al. 1997).

2.A.1.2.81.name: Uncharacterized MFS permease; encoded by a gene adjacent to one encoding a peroxiredoxin.
2.A.1.2.81.description: Uncharacterized MFS permease; encoded by a gene adjacent to one encoding a peroxiredoxin (an electron donor and antioxidant; Hanschmann et al. 2013).

2.A.1.2.83.name: MmrA MFS protein.
2.A.1.2.83.description: MmrA MFS protein. Homologous to drug exporter. RppA and MmrA are involved in amino acid uptake and efflux of antimicrobial agents including streptomycin, ethidium bromide and norfloxacin (Kimura et al. 2004).

2.A.1.2.84.name: Probable siderophore-specific exporter of 407 aas and 12 TMSs, MxcK.
2.A.1.2.84.description: Probable siderophore-specific exporter of 407 aas and 12 TMSs, MxcK.

2.A.1.2.85.name: Peroxysomal phenylacetate/phenoxyacetate transporter, PaaT (CefT) of 564 aas.
2.A.1.2.85.description: Peroxysomal phenylacetate/phenoxyacetate transporter, PaaT (CefT) of 564 aas (Fernández-Aguado et al. 2013).

2.A.1.2.86.name: Peroxisomal isopenicillin N importer, PenM.
2.A.1.2.86.description: Peroxisomal isopenicillin N importer, PenM (Evers et al. 2004; Fernández-Aguado et al. 2014).

2.A.1.2.87.name: Purine efflux porter of 392 aas, CepA.
2.A.1.2.87.description: Purine efflux porter of 392 aas, CepA. Exports purine analogues, 6-mercaptopurine and 6-mercaptoguanine, but not to 2-aminopurine and purine nucleoside analogues. May show increased resistance to the antibiotics nalidixic acid and ampicillin (Sim et al. 2014).

2.A.1.2.9.name: (Hydrophobic uncoupler e.g., CCCP, benzalkonium, SDS and other drugs):H+ antiporter, EmrD.
2.A.1.2.9.description: (Hydrophobic uncoupler e.g., CCCP, benzalkonium, SDS and other drugs):H+ antiporter, EmrD (Nishino and Yamaguchi 2001). The 3-d structure (3.5 Å resolution) has been determined (Yin et al., 2006). conformational dynamics studies have revealed details of the transport pathway and some motions of EmrD at an atomic level (Baker et al. 2012). Probably exports arabinose but not xylose (Koita and Rao…

2.A.1.2.92.name: The CefM protein of 482 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.92.description: The CefM protein of 482 aas and 12 TMSs. Probably involved in the translocation of penicillin N from the lumen of peroxisomes (or peroxisome-like microbodies) to the cytosol, where it is converted into cephalosporin C (Teijeira et al. 2009). A null mutant accumulates penicillin N, is unable to synthesize deacetoxy- and deacetyl-cephalosporin C as well as cephalosporin C, and shows impaired…

2.A.1.2.95.name: Blt of 422 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.95.description: Blt of 422 aas and 12 TMSs. Exports antibiotics such as fluoroquinolones and chloramphenicol (Vardy et al. 2005)

2.A.1.2.96.name: ZIF2 of 484 aas and 12 TMSs localises primarily at the tonoplast of root cortical cells and is a functional transporter able to mediate Zn efflux…
2.A.1.2.96.description: ZIF2 (Zinc-Induced Facilitator 2) of 484 aas and 12 TMSs localises primarily at the tonoplast of root cortical cells and is a functional transporter able to mediate Zn efflux from the cytoplasm (Remy et al. 2014). Activity is controlled by alternative RNA splicing.

2.A.1.2.97.name: Bcr/CflA family drug exporter, MSMEG_2991 of 428 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.97.description: Bcr/CflA family drug exporter, MSMEG_2991 of 428 aas and 12 TMSs. A pmf-dependent multidrug efflux pump that expels diverse groups of antibiotics including ciprofloxacin. May also be involved in biofilm enhancement (Bansal et al. 2016).

2.A.1.2.98.name: Uncharacterized MFS transporter of 427 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.98.description: Uncharacterized MFS transporter of 427 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.2.99.name: Putative siderophore exporter, SbnD of 418 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.99.description: Putative siderophore exporter, SbnD of 418 aas and 12 TMSs (Marklevitz and Harris 2016).

2.A.1.20.1.name: Sugar efflux transporter A, SetA.
2.A.1.20.1.description: Sugar efflux transporter A, SetA. Exports lactose, glucose, aromatic glucosides and galactosides, cellobiose, maltose, α-methylglucoside and isopropyl β-thiogalactosides (IPTG); amino-glycosides, streptomycin and kanamycin are weakly expelled (Liu et al. 1999). Regulated by SgrR (a transcriptional regulator of sgrS) and SgrS (a small RNA that represses trascription of setA). These two regulatory…

2.A.1.20.2.name: Sugar efflux system, SetB, for lactose and glucose, but not IPTG or galactose.
2.A.1.20.2.description: Sugar efflux system, SetB, for lactose and glucose, but not IPTG or galactose (Liu et al. 1999). Overexpression of the gene for SetB allows export of Lacto-N-triose (LNT II) and lacto-N-tetraose (LNT), human milk oligosaccharides (Sugita and Koketsu 2022).

2.A.1.20.3.name: Arabinose (but not xylose) exporter, SetC.
2.A.1.20.3.description: Arabinose (but not xylose) exporter, SetC (Koita and Rao 2012).

2.A.1.20.4.name: Efflux system for arabinose and IPTG (>>lactose), SotA
2.A.1.20.4.description: Efflux system for arabinose and IPTG (>>lactose), SotA

2.A.1.21.1.name: The macrolide (erythromycin; oleandomycin; azithromycin; telithromycin) efflux pump, MefA, of 405 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.21.1.description: The macrolide (erythromycin; oleandomycin; azithromycin; telithromycin) efflux pump, MefA, of 405 aas and 12 TMSs (Cantón et al. 2005; Bley et al. 2011). Iannelli et al. 2018 suggested that MefA can function with an ATPase, MsrD (TC# 3.A.1.121.6), and therefore function as an ABC drug exporter. However, the data presented seem inconsistent with this suggestion. The two genes encoding these two…

2.A.1.21.12.name: Multidrug-efflux transporter, Rv1258c/MT1297, of 419 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.21.12.description: Multidrug-efflux transporter, Rv1258c/MT1297, of 419 aas and 12 TMSs. Both Rv1634 and Rv1258c are believed to play major roles in drug resistance by altering the protein pump that is required to remove the active drugs from the bacterial cell (Panja et al. 2019). Thymol exhibits inhibitory activity against Mycobacterium smegmatis and shows promising interaction with a combination of isoniazid…

2.A.1.21.2.name: The multidrug (erythromycin, tetracycline, puromycin, bleomycin) resistance protein, Cmr
2.A.1.21.2.description: The multidrug (erythromycin, tetracycline, puromycin, bleomycin) resistance protein, Cmr

2.A.1.21.22.name: Macrolide efflux pump, MefE (Mef; MefA) of 405 aas.
2.A.1.21.22.description: Macrolide efflux pump, MefE (Mef; MefA) of 405 aas. Induced by erythromycin and the antimicrobial peptide, LL-37 (Zähner et al. 2010). May act in conjunction with Mel (Q93QE4), an ABC-type ATPase that is encoded in the same operon with the mefA gene (Ambrose et al. 2005).

2.A.1.21.6.name: The tetracycline resistance efflux pump, TetA(P) (21% identity (e-07) with 2.A.1.21.5 and 22% identity (2xe-7) with 2.A.1.2.10).
2.A.1.21.6.description: The tetracycline resistance efflux pump, TetA(P) (Bannam et al., 2004) (21% identity (e-07) with 2.A.1.21.5 and 22% identity (2xe-7) with 2.A.1.2.10). It may be the link between DHA1 and DHA3.

2.A.1.21.7.name: The Staphyloferrin A (siderophore) exporter, NWMN-2081.
2.A.1.21.7.description: The Staphyloferrin A (siderophore) exporter, NWMN-2081 (Beasley et al. 2009). Independently suggested to be a macrolide exporter (Marklevitz and Harris 2016).

2.A.1.21.8.name: The putative macrolide exporter, TIGR00900 (most similar to 2.A.1.21.1).
2.A.1.21.8.description: The putative macrolide exporter, TIGR00900 (most similar to 2.A.1.21.1).

2.A.1.22.name: The Vesicular Neurotransmitter Transporter (VNT) Family (Related to the SP Family (TC #2.1.1))

2.A.1.22.1.name: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein neurotransmitter (e.g., dopamine) transporter, SV2A or SLC22B1.
2.A.1.22.1.description: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein neurotransmitter (e.g., dopamine) transporter, SV2A or SLC22B1. This protein localizes to neurotransmitter-containing vesicles and has a nucleotide binding site (Yao and Bajjalieh 2009). The SV2 family is comprised of three paralogues: SV2A, SV2B, and SV2C. They are present in secretory vesicles, including synaptic vesicles, and are critical to neurotransmission…

2.A.1.24.name: The Vacuolar Basic Amino Acid Transporter (VBAAT) Family

2.A.1.24.2.name: Vacuolar amino acid (Arg, Lys, His) transporter, Atg22 (Autophagy-related protein-22).
2.A.1.24.2.description: Vacuolar amino acid (Arg, Lys, His) transporter, Atg22 (Autophagy-related protein-22) (Sugimoto et al. 2011).

2.A.1.24.5.name: MFS permease
2.A.1.24.5.proteins: MFS permease of Micrococcus luteus (Micrococcus lysodeikticus)

2.A.1.25.1.name: The endoplasmic reticular/Golgi acetyl-CoA:CoA antiporter 1, ACATN/ACATN1 (SLC33A1).
2.A.1.25.1.description: The endoplasmic reticular/Golgi acetyl-CoA:CoA antiporter 1, ACATN/ACATN1 (SLC33A1). Allows acetylation of sialic acid residues in gangliosides and lysine residues in membrane proteins. It is associated with neurodegenerative disorders such as sporadic amyotrophic laterial sclerosis (ALS) and Spastic Paraplegia 42, and it is essential for motor neuron viability (Hirabayashi et al. 2013). Abnormal…

2.A.1.25.2.name: Cell wall degradation product as well as penicillin derivative uptake porter, AmpG.
2.A.1.25.2.description: Cell wall degradation product (peptides and glycopeptides including N-acetylglucosaminyl β-1,4-anhydro-N-acetyl-muramyl-tri or tetra-peptide) as well as penicillin derivative uptake porter, AmpG (Cheng and Park 2002). The AmpG permease is also required for AmpC beta-lactamase induction (Chahboune et al. 2005; Park and Uehara 2008). AmpG mediates a dynamic relationship between serine…

2.A.1.25.3.name: The AmpG peptidoglycan degradation product uptake porter is part of the peptidoglycan recycling pathway.
2.A.1.25.3.description: The AmpG peptidoglycan degradation product uptake porter is part of the peptidoglycan recycling pathway (Garcia and Dillard, 2008). It also plays a role in peptidoglycan remodeling, recycling, and toxic fragment release as well as pathogenesis (Schaub and Dillard 2019).

2.A.1.25.4.name: Putative peptide/acetyl-CoA transporter of 560 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.25.4.description: Putative peptide/acetyl-CoA transporter of 560 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.25.4.proteins: Uncharacterized protein of Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Baker's yeast)

2.A.1.25.5.name: Transporter of meuropeptides, N-acetylglucosamine anhydrous N-acetylmuramyl peptides, AmpG.
2.A.1.25.5.description: Transporter of meuropeptides, N-acetylglucosamine anhydrous N-acetylmuramyl peptides, AmpG (Kong et al. 2010). Necessary for induction of ampC, β-lactamase, and ampicillin resistance (Zhang et al. 2010). Amino acyl residues essential for proper mRNA production and for catalytic activity have been identified (Li et al. 2016).

2.A.1.25.6.name: Uptake transporter, AmpG, of 433 aas and 12 TMSs, specific for muropeptides, fragments of the peptidoglycan cell walls of bacteria.
2.A.1.25.6.description: Uptake transporter, AmpG, of 433 aas and 12 TMSs, specific for muropeptides, fragments of the peptidoglycan cell walls of bacteria (Ruscitto et al. 2017).

2.A.1.25.7.name: Putative acetyl-CoA:CoA antiporter, ACT or AT1, of 590 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs in a 6 or 7 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.25.7.description: Putative acetyl-CoA:CoA antiporter, ACT or AT1, of 590 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs in a 6 or 7 + 6 TMS arrangement (Wunderlich 2022).

2.A.1.26.1.name: 41.4 KDa Protein, YcaD.
2.A.1.26.1.description: 41.4 KDa Protein, YcaD. It may export ectoine and hydroxyectoine (Czech et al. 2022).

2.A.1.26.2.name: MFS porter, YfkF; possible drug exporter
2.A.1.26.2.description: MFS porter, YfkF; possible drug exporter

2.A.1.26.3.name: Multidrug resistance efflux porter, BC3310 of 396 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.26.3.description: Multidrug resistance efflux porter, BC3310 of 396 aas and 12 TMSs. Exports ethidium bromide, sodium dodecyl sulfate and silver nitrate. D105 in TMS4 is essential for activity (Kroeger et al. 2015).

2.A.1.27.1.name: The phenylpropionate porter, HcaT (YfhS).
2.A.1.27.1.description: The phenylpropionate porter, HcaT (YfhS) (Díaz et al. 1998).

2.A.1.27.3.name: Putative metabolite transporter of 393 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.27.3.description: Putative metabolite transporter of 393 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.28.name: The Feline Leukemia Virus Subgroup C Receptor (FLVCR)/Heme Importer Family

2.A.1.28.1.name: Cell surface receptor (C-receptor) for anemia-inducing feline leukemia virus subgroup C (FLCVR, Slc49A1 or Mfsd7d) of 555 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.28.1.description: Cell surface receptor (C-receptor) for anemia-inducing feline leukemia virus subgroup C (FLCVR, Slc49A1 or Mfsd7d) of 555 aas and 12 TMSs. It may function in choline transport (Kenny et al. 2023) or haem export in haemopoietic cells (Latunde-Dada et al., 2006; Khan and Quigley, 2011) and may cause Diamond-Blackfan anemia when defective (Keel et al., 2008). Mutations of FLVCR1 in posterior column…

2.A.1.28.4.name: The Fowler syndrome-associated protein, feline leukemia virus subgroup C receptor-related protein 2, FLVCR2, or SLC49A2, is probably a heme importer.
2.A.1.28.4.description: The Fowler syndrome-associated protein, feline leukemia virus subgroup C receptor-related protein 2, FLVCR2, or SLC49A2, is probably a heme importer (Duffy et al., 2010). Mutations of SLC49A2 are observed in Fowler syndrome, a rare proliferative vascular disorder of the brain (Khan and Quigley 2018). A rocker-switch mechanism of choline transmembrane transport in FLVCR2 occurs involving dynamic…

2.A.1.28.8.name: MFSD7, FLVCR2 or SLC49A3 of 560 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.28.8.description: MFSD7, FLVCR2 or SLC49A3 of 560 aas and 12 TMSs. It is the feline leukemia virus subgroup C receptor-2 (FLVCR2), a member of the SLC49 family of four paralogous genes in humans (Khan and Quigley 2018). It is a cell surface heme transporter, essential for erythropoiesis and systemic iron homeostasis. Mutations of SLC49A2, encoding FLVCR1, are noted in patients with Fowler syndrome (Khan and…

2.A.1.3.1.name: The main boron exporter in yeast, Atr1 (Aminotriazole, 4-nitroquinoline-N-oxide, etc.):H+ antiporter.
2.A.1.3.1.description: The main boron exporter in yeast, Atr1 (Kaya et al. 2009) (Aminotriazole, 4-nitroquinoline-N-oxide, etc.):H+ antiporter. Also exports L-cysteine (Yamada et al., 2006).

2.A.1.3.13.name: Unconjugated bile acid uptake transporter
2.A.1.3.13.proteins: BaiG of Eubacterium sp. strain VPI 12708

2.A.1.3.14.name: Methylviologen (paraquat):H+ antiporter, SmvA (also exports ethidium bromide, acriflavin, malachite green, pyronine B and benzyl viologen).
2.A.1.3.14.description: Methylviologen (paraquat):H+ antiporter, SmvA (also exports ethidium bromide, acriflavin, malachite green, pyronine B and benzyl viologen) (Villagra et al. 2008).

2.A.1.3.16.name: The Me2+·tetracycline:2H+ antiporter (Me2+ = Co2+, Mg2+, Mn2+) (also probably a Na+ or K+:2H+ antiporter).
2.A.1.3.16.description: The Me2+·tetracycline:2H+ antiporter (Me2+ = Co2+, Mg2+, Mn2+) (also probably a Na+ or K+:2H+ antiporter) (Wang et al. 2000).

Both Rv1634 and Rv1258c are believed to play a major role in drug resistance by altering the protein pump that is required to remove the active drug compounds from the bacterial cell (Panja et al. 2019). Ciprofloxacin and norfloxacin are substrates, to which M. tuberculosis strains have become resistant. The expulsion of the drugs…

2.A.1.3.60.description: MDR efflux pump, SdrM. Exports norfloxacin, acriflavin and ethidium bromide (Yamada et al. 2006). Multidrug-resistance in S. aureus is inhibited by the endocannabinoid, anandamide (Sionov et al. 2022).

2.A.1.3.61.name: MDR efflux pump, MdeA.
2.A.1.3.61.description: MDR efflux pump, MdeA. Exports quaternary ammonium compounds and antibiotics (Huang et al. 2004). Also exports hoechst 33342, doxorubicin, daunorubicin, tetraphenyl phosphonium, ethidium bromide and rhodamine 6G (Yamada et al. 2006). Multidrug-resistance in S. aureus is inhibited by the endocannabinoid, anandamide (Sionov et al. 2022).

2.A.1.3.62.description: MDR efflux pump, AedC (Hassan et al. 2011). Shown to export chloramphenicol and tetracycline.

2.A.1.3.63.description: Iron homeostasis protein, AedD; may function in siderophore export (Hassan et al. 2011).

2.A.1.3.65.name: ThMFS1 of 563 aas and 14 TMSs.
2.A.1.3.65.description: ThMFS1 of 563 aas and 14 TMSs. Catalyzes export of fungicides causing tolerance. It exports trichodermin, but it is not the only exporter of this secondary metabolite (Liu et al. 2012). Trichothecenes are the sesquiterpenes secreted by Trichoderma spp. residing in the rhizosphere. These compounds have been reported to act as plant growth promoters and bio-control agents (Chaudhary et al. 2016).

2.A.1.3.66.name: MFS permease of 413 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.3.66.description: MFS permease of 413 aas and 12 TMSs. Encoded within the SoxR regulon; possibly a drug exporter (Naseer et al. 2014).

2.A.1.3.68.name: The PfMFS transporter (551 aas; 14 putative TMSs) is involved in the acid resistance and intracellular pH homeostasis of Penicillium funiculosum.
2.A.1.3.68.description: The PfMFS transporter (551 aas; 14 putative TMSs) is involved in the acid resistance and intracellular pH homeostasis of Penicillium funiculosum (Xu et al. 2014). This protein (AIJ02309) was not in UniProt when enterred into TCDB, and its closest orthologue, PmMFS of Penicillium marneffei, is therefore presented here. These two proteins are 82% identical.

2.A.1.3.69.name: Drug resistance pump, YMR279c of 540 aas.
2.A.1.3.69.description: Drug resistance pump, YMR279c of 540 aas. When overexpressed, confers boron resistance, but is not induced by boron (Bozdag et al. 2011).

2.A.1.3.81.description: multidrug (tetracycline, kanamycin, rhodamin 6G, ampicillin, acriflavine, ethidium bromide, and tetraphenylphosphonium chloride) resistance exporter, MdeA, of 453 aas and 14 TMSs (Kim et al. 2013).

2.A.1.3.82.name: Multidrug resistance transporter protein of 519 aas and 14 TMSs.
2.A.1.3.82.description: Multidrug resistance transporter protein of 519 aas and 14 TMSs. It exports 2-thiocyanatopyridine derivatives (Nunvar et al. 2019).

2.A.1.3.84.description: Trichothecene efflux pump, Tri12, of 590 aas and 14 TMSs (Lee et al. 2002). It may function as a phospholipid flippase, and five flippases (FgDnfA, B, C1, C2 and D have been identified (Yun et al. 2020). 2.A.1.32.1.description: Putative aromatic compound/drug exporter. Enhances expression of the sigma X gene that functions to modify the cell envelope (Turner and Helmann, 2000). yitG is reported to be a mutator gene that inhibits transition base substitutions (Sasaki and Kurusu, 2004).

2.A.1.32.2.name: Bacillibactin exporter, YmfE (199aas; 6TMSs) resembles the 2nd half of YitG of B. subtilis (2.A.1.32.1).
