2.A.1.32.3.description: Putative copper/multidrug efflux protein, YfmO. The yfmPO operon is autoregulated by the MerR homologue, YfmP (a repressor). The copZA operon encodes CopA, a copper ATPase (TC# 3.A.3.5.18) which is induced by a copper dependent mechanism. Since a yfmP null mutant had poor copZA induction but elevated levels of the YfmO efflux pump, YfmO could catalyze copper efflux and be responsible for reduced…

2.A.1.33.1.name: MFS homologue, YqgE.
2.A.1.33.1.description: MFS homologue, YqgE. It is cotranscribed with ftsI, encoding the peptidoglycan transpeptidase that crosslinks peptidoglycan strands, releasing free D-alanine. Possibly YqgE is a D-alanine uptake porter. Its expression causes a decrease in the amount of sigma W synthesis, the sigma factor for genes involved in detoxification and antimicrobial synthesis (Turner and Helmann 2000).

2.A.1.35.1.name: The fosmidomycin resistance (Fsr) protein (confers fosmidomycin, trimethoprim and carbonylcyanide m-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP) resistance).
2.A.1.35.1.description: The fosmidomycin resistance (Fsr) protein (confers fosmidomycin, trimethoprim and carbonylcyanide m-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP) resistance) (Fujisaki et al. 1996).

2.A.1.35.2.name: The cationic microbial peptide resistance (RosA) protein
2.A.1.35.2.description: The cationic microbial peptide resistance (RosA) protein

2.A.1.35.3.name: MFS transporter of 388 aas and 12 TMSs
2.A.1.35.3.description: MFS transporter of 388 aas and 12 TMSs

2.A.1.36.1.name: The acriflavin-sensitivity protein, YnfM (increases sensitivity to acriflavin specifically).
2.A.1.36.1.description: The acriflavin-sensitivity protein, YnfM (increases sensitivity to acriflavin specifically). Also exports arabinose but not xylose (Koita and Rao 2012).

2.A.1.36.2.name: Hypothetical MFS carrier of 411 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.36.2.description: Hypothetical MFS carrier of 411 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.36.4.name: MdrA.
2.A.1.36.4.description: MdrA. Putative MDR transporter that may export cationic and hydrophobic compounds, Sco4007. Regulated by a TetR-like repressor that binds drugs (Hayashi et al. 2013).

2.A.1.36.6.name: Succinate/dicarboxylate transporter, YnfM, of 416 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.36.6.description: Succinate/dicarboxylate transporter, YnfM, of 416 aas and 12 TMSs. It exports succinate under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions (Fukui et al. 2019).

2.A.1.36.7.name: Copper (Cu) importer of 417 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement, CuiT or YnfM, or STM1486.
2.A.1.36.7.description: Copper (Cu) importer of 417 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement, CuiT or YnfM, or STM1486. It is required for metal homeostasis (Zhao et al. 2026). Comparative genomics revealed that cuiT is evolutionarily conserved across Enterobacteriaceae. CuiT mediates rapid Cu import, supporting larger intracellular Cu pools (Zhao et al. 2026).

2.A.1.38.1.name: The enterobactin (siderophore) exporter, EntS or YbdA.
2.A.1.38.1.description: The enterobactin (siderophore) exporter, EntS or YbdA (Bleuel et al., 2005). May also export arabinose but not xylose (Koita and Rao 2012).

2.A.1.38.2.name: The putative siderophore exporter (DUF 894; Pfam 05977), VabS
2.A.1.38.2.description: The putative siderophore exporter (DUF 894; Pfam 05977), VabS

2.A.1.38.3.name: Enterobactin exporter, EntS (probably orthologous to 2.A.1.38.1).
2.A.1.38.3.description: Enterobactin exporter, EntS (Crouch et al., 2008) (probably orthologous to 2.A.1.38.1).

2.A.1.4.1.name: Sugar-P:Pi antiporter (transports many sugar-phosphates - both 1- and 6-P esters)
2.A.1.4.1.description: Sugar-P:Pi antiporter (transports many sugar-phosphates - both 1- and 6-P esters)

2.A.1.4.10.name: 2-phosphonoacetate/2-phosponopropionate uptake porter of 428 aas, PhnB.
2.A.1.4.10.description: 2-phosphonoacetate/2-phosponopropionate uptake porter of 428 aas, PhnB. The PhnA protein is a hydrolase, and PhnC is a positive transcriptional regulator. Induction occurs with either of the two substrates (Kulakova et al. 2001).

2.A.1.4.11.name: Glycerol-3-phosphate:inorganic phosphate antiporter, GlpT.
2.A.1.4.11.description: Glycerol-3-phosphate:inorganic phosphate antiporter, GlpT (Frohlich and Audia 2013).

2.A.1.4.2.name: P-glycerate:Pi antiporter, Pgt.
2.A.1.4.2.description: P-glycerate:Pi antiporter, Pgt. Takes up phosphoenolpyruvate, 2-phosphoglycerate, and 3-phosphoglycerate as sole sources of carbon and energy for rapid growth (Saier et al. 1975). Not present in E. coli K12, but is present in many intracellular pathogenic strains of E. coli (Tang and Saier, unpublished observations).

2.A.1.4.3.name: Glycerol-P:Pi antiporter.
2.A.1.4.3.description: Glycerol-P:Pi antiporter (may function by a 'rocker switch' mechanism; Law et al., 2007). The 3-d structure is known (3.3Å resolution) (Huang et al., 2003; Lemieux et al., 2005; Lemieux, 2007).

2.A.1.4.4.name: Hexose-P:Pi antiporter regulatory protein; senses external glucose-6-P and transports it with high affinity and low efficiency
2.A.1.4.4.description: Hexose-P:Pi antiporter regulatory protein; senses external glucose-6-P and transports it with high affinity and low efficiency

2.A.1.4.5.name: Microsomal (ER/Golgi) glucose-6-P:Pi antiporter glycogen storage disease protein (4 isoforms present in humans).
2.A.1.4.5.description: Microsomal (ER/Golgi) glucose-6-P:Pi antiporter (glycogen storage disease protein (GSD1b and 1c; Gierke''s disease protein) (SLC37A2 in mice, SLC37a4 associated with white adipose tissue obesity and expressed at high levels in macrophage) (4 isoforms present in humans (Chen et al., 2008)). SLC37A1 and A2 can not substitute for A4. 91 mutations have been observed in human patients (Chou and…

2.A.1.4.6.name: Glucose-6-P:Pi antiporter, Hpt (may also transport other organophosphates including C3 organophosphates).
2.A.1.4.6.description: Glucose-6-P:Pi antiporter, Hpt (may also transport other organophosphates including C3 organophosphates).
2.A.1.4.6.proteins: Hpt of Chlamydia pneumoniae (spQ9Z7N9 & gi9979188) & pirA72050

2.A.1.4.7.name: Putative glycerol-3-phosphate (G-3-P) transporter, G3PP (most similar to TC# 2.A.1.4.6, 22% identity).
2.A.1.4.7.description: Putative glycerol-3-phosphate (G-3-P) transporter, G3PP (most similar to TC# 2.A.1.4.6, 22% identity). Has been shown to catalyze glucose 6-P:Pi antiport across the endoplasmic reticular membrane(Pan et al. 2011).

2.A.1.4.8.name: solute carrier family 37 (putative glycerol-3-phosphate transporter), member 2.
2.A.1.4.8.description: solute carrier family 37 (putative glycerol-3-phosphate transporter), member 2. Has been shown to catalyze glucose 6-P:Pi antiport across the endoplasmic reticular membrane (Pan et al. 2011). N-glycosylation is critical for the function of bovine PepT2 (Wang et al. 2020).

2.A.1.40.name: The Major Facilitator Superfamily Domain-containing Protein (MFS-DP) Family

2.A.1.40.2.name: Major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 5, MFSD5 or SLC61A1, of 450 aas and 13 TMSs in a 5 + 2 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.40.2.description: Major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 5, MFSD5 or SLC61A1, of 450 aas and 13 TMSs in a 5 + 2 + 6 TMS arrangement. It mediates high-affinity (550 nM Km) intracellular uptake of the rare oligo-element molybdenum. It is probably a molybdate (the oxianion molybdate)/anion uptake porter (Tejada-Jiménez et al. 2011). In mammals, it is expressed in the brain and may play a role in…
2.A.1.40.2.proteins: Molybdate uptake porter of Homo sapiens

2.A.1.42.1.name: The lysophospholipid (LPL) transporter, LplT.
2.A.1.42.1.description: The lysophospholipid (LPL) transporter, LplT (Harvat et al., 2005). Substrates include lyso-PE, lyso-cardiolipin, diacylcardiolipin, fully-deacylated cardiolipin and lyso-phosphatidylglycerol, but not lysophosphatidylcholine, lysophosphatidic acid or phosphatidic acid (Lin et al. 2016). Reacylation by acyltransferase/acyl-acyl carrier protein synthetase then occurs on the inner leaflet of the…

2.A.1.42.2.name: The lysophospholipid transporter-2-acyl glycerophosphoethanolamine acyl transferase/acyl ACP synthetase (LplT-Pls-ACS) fusion protein.
2.A.1.42.2.description: The lysophospholipid transporter-2-acyl glycerophosphoethanolamine acyl transferase/acyl ACP synthetase (LplT-Pls-ACS) fusion protein (Harvat et al., 2005).
2.A.1.42.2.proteins: The fused LplT-PlsC-ACS of Bradyrhizobium japonicum (BAC47589)

2.A.1.43.2.name: The magnetosome permease fused to a C-terminal YedZ-like domain, MamZ.
2.A.1.43.2.description: The magnetosome permease fused to a C-terminal YedZ-like domain, MamZ (von Rozycki et al., 2004). This protein has 649 aas and 18 TMSs with a C-terminal YedZ domain and is therefore in the YedZ superfamily as well as the MFS. The two MFS proteins in the magnetosome membrane, MamZ and MamH (44% identical to MamZ), appear to overlap in function as deletion of their two genes have additive effects…

2.A.1.44.1.name: The L-amino acid transporter-3, LAT3 (Prostate cancer up-regulated gene product).
2.A.1.44.1.description: The L-amino acid transporter-3, LAT3 (transports neutral amino acids such as L-leucine, L-isoleucine, L-valine, and L-phenylalanine by a Na+-independent, electroneutral, facilitated diffusion process; it also transports amino acid alcohols and thyroid hormones such as 3,3'-T2) (Prostate cancer up-regulated gene product) (Krause and Hinz 2019).

2.A.1.44.2.name: L-amino acid transporter-4 (LAT4) has the same specificity and is 57% identity to LAT3.
2.A.1.44.2.description: L-amino acid transporter-4 (LAT4) has the same specificity and is 57% identity to LAT3. Na+, Cl- and pH independent; not trans-stimulated; it has been reported to have two kinetic components, a low affinity component sensitive to NEM, and a high affinity component insensitive to NEM. It is found in the basolateral membrane of epithelial cells in the distal tubule and collecting duct of the kidney…

2.A.1.46.6.name: UPF0226 protein YfcJ.
2.A.1.46.6.description: UPF0226 protein YfcJ. Catalyzes export of arabinose but not xylose (Koita and Rao 2012).

2.A.1.46.7.name: UPF0226 protein, YhhS.
2.A.1.46.7.description: UPF0226 protein, YhhS. Exports arabinose but not xylose (Koita and Rao 2012). Also may export the herbicide, glyphosate (Staub et al. 2012).

2.A.1.48.name: The Vacuolar Basic Amino Acid Transporter (V-BAAT) Family

2.A.1.48.1.name: The vacuolar basic amino acid (histidine, lysine and arginine) transporter, Vba1 (most similar to family 2.A.1.3; DHA2; 13-14 putative TMSs)
2.A.1.48.1.description: The vacuolar basic amino acid (histidine, lysine and arginine) transporter, Vba1 (catalyzes uptake into the vacuoles (equivalent to efflux from the cytoplasm)) (most similar to family 2.A.1.3; DHA2; 13-14 putative TMSs) (Shimazu et al., 2005)

2.A.1.48.2.name: The vacuolar basic amino acid (Arg, Lys, His) transporter, Vba2
2.A.1.48.2.description: The vacuolar basic amino acid (Arg, Lys, His) transporter, Vba2 (Shimazu et al., 2005)

2.A.1.48.3.name: Vacuolar G0 arrest protein, Fnx1; involved in amino acid (e.g., his, lys, ile, asn, etc) uptake into the vacuole.
2.A.1.48.3.description: Vacuolar G0 arrest protein, Fnx1; involved in amino acid (e.g., his, lys, ile, asn, etc) uptake into the vacuole (Chardwiriyapreecha et al., 2008).

2.A.1.48.4.name: Vacuolar amino acid uptake system, Fnx2
2.A.1.48.4.description: Vacuolar amino acid uptake system, Fnx2 (Chardiwiriyapreecha et al., 2008)

2.A.1.49.1.name: The spinster protein, spin1 or spns1 gene product.
2.A.1.49.1.description: The spinster protein, spin1 or spns1 gene product (involved in synaptic growth regulation; interacts with Bcl-2/Bcl-xL, affecting programmed cell death) (Nakano et al., 2001; Sanyal and Ramaswami, 2002; Yanagisawa et al., 2003). Probably transports sphingosine-1-phosphate (Fukuhara et al. 2012), but polymorphisms in spns1 are associated with alterred triglyceride levels (Västermark et al. 2012).

2.A.1.49.10.name: MFS multidrug exporter of 429 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.49.10.description: MFS multidrug exporter of 429 aas and 12 TMSs. Exports capreomycin and ethidium bromide, and deletion mutants grow faster than wild type cells (Zhang et al. 2015).

2.A.1.49.12.name: Spinster 3, SPNS3 (SLC63A3), of 512 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.49.12.description: Spinster 3, SPNS3 (SLC63A3), of 512 aas and 12 TMSs. The evolutionary conservation, predicted structure and neuronal expression have been characterized (Perland et al. 2017). It probably exports sphigosine-1- phosphate.

2.A.1.49.2.name: The spinster homologue, Spin1 or Spns1 (SLC63A1) of 528 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.49.2.description: The spinster homologue, Spin1 or Spns1 (SLC63A1) of 528 aas and 12 TMSs. It interacts with Bc1-2/Bc1-XL to induce a caspase-independent autophagic cell death (Yanagisawa et al., 2003). It is a spingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) (or sphingolipid) exporter (Nijnik et al. 2012). S1P is important for lymphocyte trafficking, immune responses, vascular and embryonic development, cancer, and bone homeostasis…

2.A.1.49.3.name: Probable sphingosine-1-phosphate (or sphingolipid) transporter, spinster homologue 3 (by similarity).
2.A.1.49.3.description: Probable sphingosine-1-phosphate (or sphingolipid) transporter, spinster homologue 3 (by similarity).

2.A.1.49.4.name: Protein Spinster homologue 2 (Spns2 or protein two of hearts).
2.A.1.49.4.description: Protein Spinster homologue 2 (Spns2 or protein two of hearts). Exports sphingosine-1-P (S1P) and the immunomodulating agent, FTY720 (Hisano et al. 2011; Nijnik et al. 2012). S1P is a secreted lipid mediator that functions in vascular development. In the yolk syncytial layer, Spns2 functions in S1P secretion, thereby regulating myocardial precursor migration (Kawahara et al. 2009).

2.A.1.49.5.name: Probable sphingosine-1-phosphate or sphingolipid transporter, Spinster homologue 1 (by similarity).
2.A.1.49.5.description: Probable sphingosine-1-phosphate or sphingolipid transporter, Spinster homologue 1 (by similarity).

2.A.1.49.6.name: Sphingosine-1-phosphate/dehydrosphingosine-1-P transport protein, Spinster 2, SPNS2 of 549 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.49.6.description: Sphingosine-1-phosphate/dehydrosphingosine-1-P transport protein, Spinster 2, SPNS2 of 549 aas and 12 TMSs. It is involved in immune development and lymphocyte trafficing (Nijnik et al. 2012; Fukuhara et al. 2012). The functions and the mechanisms of SPNS2 in the pathogenesis of cancer have been reviewed (Fang et al. 2020).

2.A.1.49.7.name: Bacterial Spinster homologue; possible sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter (by similarity only).
2.A.1.49.7.description: Bacterial Spinster homologue; possible sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter (by similarity only).

2.A.1.49.8.name: Bacterial spinster homologue.
2.A.1.49.8.description: Bacterial spinster homologue. Possible sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter (by similarity only).

2.A.1.5.1.name: β- and α-galactopyranoside:H+ symporter, LacY.
2.A.1.5.1.description: β- and α-galactopyranoside:H+ symporter, LacY. Transports lactose, melibiose, thio-β-methyl galactopyranoside (TMG), isopropyl-β-thiogalactoside (IPTG), 4-nitrophenyl-beta-D-galactopyranoside, 4-nitrophenyl-alpha-D-galactopyranoside and galactopyranosyl-1-glycerol. Single point mutations allow transport of sucrose and maltose (King and Wilson 1990). Crystal structures and modeling reveal the…

2.A.1.5.2.name: Raffinose:H+ symporter, RafB, can be mutated to transport maltose.
2.A.1.5.2.description: Raffinose:H+ symporter, RafB, can be mutated to transport maltose (Van Camp et al., 2007).

2.A.1.5.3.name: Sucrose:H+ symporter, CscB, also transports maltose.
2.A.1.5.3.description: Sucrose:H+ symporter, CscB, also transports maltose (Peng et al. 2009). CscB recognizes not just sucrose but also fructose and lactulose, but glucopyranosides are not transported and do not inhibit sucrose transport (Sugihara et al. 2011). Direct interactions between LacY and its lipid environment uniquely contribute to its membrane protein organization and function (Vitrac et al. 2020).

2.A.1.5.4.name: Melibiose:H+ symporter, MelY.
2.A.1.5.4.description: Melibiose:H+ symporter, MelY (Shinnick et al., 2003). Transports melibiose and lactose, but not TMG, which does however bind to the transporter (Tavoulari and Frillingos, 2008)

2.A.1.5.6.name: MFS transporter specific for fructooligosaccharides, FosT, of 412 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.5.6.description: MFS transporter specific for fructooligosaccharides, FosT, of 412 aas and 12 TMSs (Schouler et al. 2009).

2.A.1.50.2.description: Thymic stromal cotransporter, TSCOT (Kim et al. 2000)

2.A.1.50.4.description: Multidrug efflux transporter, MET, of 507 aas and 12 TMSs (Chahine et al. 2012). Exposure to dietary methotrexate was associated with increased fluid secretion rate and increased flux of methotrexate, but not salicylate. 2.A.1.52.4.name: The glycerophosphodiester, glycerophosphocholine uptake porter, GlpU.
2.A.1.52.4.description: The glycerophosphodiester, glycerophosphocholine uptake porter, GlpU. The cytoplasmic compound is hydrolyzed to α-glycerolphosphate and choline (Großhennig et al. 2013).

2.A.1.53.1.name: The threonine uptake permease, PhtA (required for maximal growth in macrophages and Acanthamoeba castellanii)
2.A.1.53.1.description: The threonine uptake permease, PhtA (Sauer et al., 2005) (required for maximal growth in macrophages and Acanthamoeba castellanii)

2.A.1.53.2.name: The valine uptake permease, PhtJ (required for maximal growth in macrophages and Acanthamoeba castellanii)
2.A.1.53.2.description: The valine uptake permease, PhtJ (required for maximal growth in macrophages and Acanthamoeba castellanii) (Chen et al., 2008)

2.A.1.53.3.name: The MFSD1 (SMAP4) transporter (465 aas; 12 TMSs).
2.A.1.53.3.description: The MFSD1 (SMAP4) transporter (465 aas; 12 TMSs). Expression is increased in mice by amino acid starvation and decreased by a high fat diet (Perland et al. 2016). This lysosomal transporter is essential for liver homeostasis and critically depends on its accessory subunit GLMP (Massa López et al. 2019). MFSD1 is not N-glycosylated but contains a dileucine-based sorting motif needed for its…

2.A.1.53.5.name: Putative amino acid transporter of 478 aas and 12 TMSs, CG8602, isoform A. May play a role in macrophage migration in the Drosophila embryo.
2.A.1.53.5.description: Putative amino acid transporter of 478 aas and 12 TMSs, CG8602, isoform A. May play a role in macrophage migration in the Drosophila embryo (Dr. Daria Siekhaus, personal communication).

2.A.1.53.6.name: MFS uptake permease specific for pyrimidines, PhtC of 422 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.53.6.description: MFS uptake permease specific for pyrimidines, PhtC of 422 aas and 12 TMSs. Together with PhtD (TC# 2.A.1.53.6), it contributes to protection of L. pneumophila from dTMP starvation, protects the cell from 5-fluorodeoxyuridine (FUdR) toxicity and is required for growth of L. pneumophila in macrophage (Fonseca et al. 2014).

2.A.1.53.7.name: MFS uptake permease, probably specific for pyrimidines, PhtD of 427 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.53.7.description: MFS uptake permease, probably specific for pyrimidines, PhtD of 427 aas and 12 TMSs. Together with PhtC (TC# 2.A.1.53.6), it contributes to protection of L. pneumophila from dTMP starvatioin, protects the cell from 5-fluorodeoxyuridine (FUdR) toxicity and is required for growth of L. pneumophila in macrophage (Fonseca et al. 2014).

2.A.1.54.3.name: Functionally uncharacterized MFS porter of 414 aas
2.A.1.54.3.description: Functionally uncharacterized MFS porter of 414 aas

2.A.1.55.5.name: MFS protein of 373 aas and 11 TMSs.
2.A.1.55.5.description: MFS protein of 373 aas and 11 TMSs. The protein is probably N-terminally truncated due to an error, and probably has 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.55.5.proteins: MFS porter of Labrenzia sp. THAF82

2.A.1.56.1.name: The 1,3-dihydroxybenzene (resorcinol) uptake permease, MFS_1 of 402 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.56.1.description: The 1,3-dihydroxybenzene (resorcinol) uptake permease, MFS_1 (Darley et al., 2007) of 402 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.57.3.description: Iron-yersiniabactin (Ybt) transporter of 467 aas and 12 TMSs, YbtX (Bobrov et al. 2014). Yersiniabactin can also bind zinc ions with high affinity and feed the Zn2+ into this MFS transporter, YbtX (Bobrov et al. 2014). 2.A.1.58.1.name: The N-acetylglucosamine:H+ symporter, Ngt1
2.A.1.58.1.description: The N-acetylglucosamine:H+ symporter, Ngt1 (Alvarez and Konopka, 2007)

2.A.1.58.2.name: May contribute to coordination of muscle contraction as regulatory subunit of a nonessential potassium channel complex.
2.A.1.58.2.description: May contribute to coordination of muscle contraction as regulatory subunit of a nonessential potassium channel complex. Subunit structure: May form a complex with sup-9 and sup-10 where unc-93 and sup-10 act as regulatory subunits of the two pore potassium channel sup-9.

2.A.1.59.2.name: UMF10b (in an operon with a sensor kinase/response regulator pair and an 8 TMS rhomboid protease)
2.A.1.59.2.description: UMF10b (in an operon with a sensor kinase/response regulator pair and an 8 TMS rhomboid protease)

2.A.1.59.5.description: Putative pantothenate:H+ importer of 417 aas and 12 TMSs (Wunderlich 2022).
2.A.1.59.5.proteins: Putative pantothenate uptake porter of Plasmodium falciparum

2.A.1.6.10.name: Inner membrane metabolite transport protein YhjE.
2.A.1.6.10.description: Inner membrane metabolite transport protein YhjE. YhjE is an L-isoleucine and L-valine transporter (Molev et al. 2025). Kinetic analysis yielded apparent KM values of 70.5 μM (L-isoleucine) and 86.7 μM (L-valine), establishing YhjE as a lower-affinity system compared with LIV-I (encoded by the livKHMGF operon and livJ gene) and BrnQ. Energetically, transport was proton-motive-force-dependent: the…

2.A.1.6.11.name: Acetate/haloacid transporter, Dehp2, with a possible atypical topology.
2.A.1.6.11.description: Acetate/haloacid transporter, Dehp2, with a possible atypical topology (Tse et al. 2009). Transports acetate, chloroacetate, bromoacetate, 2-chloropropionate, and possibly, with low affinity, glycolate, lactate and pyruvate (based on weak inhibition results). Inducible by chloroacetate (Su and Tsang 2012). This protein is 79% identical to its paralogue, Deh4p (TC# 2.A.1.6.8) which differs in that…

2.A.1.6.12.name: The putative thiazole transporter, ThiU.
2.A.1.6.12.description: The putative thiazole transporter, ThiU. Regulatyed by TPP riboswitch (Rodionov et al. 2002)

2.A.1.6.13.name: Acetate/monochloroacetate permease, Deh4p, of 468 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.6.13.description: Acetate/monochloroacetate permease, Deh4p, of 468 aas and 12 TMSs. Transports various carboxylates. Dehalococcoides mccartyi degrades haloacids (Su et al. 2016).

2.A.1.6.14.name: Proline/glycine betaine uptake transporter, ProP, of 466 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.6.14.description: Proline/glycine betaine uptake transporter, ProP, of 466 aas and 12 TMSs. It is not the major proline transporter found in S. aureus (Lehman et al. 2023).

2.A.1.6.2.name: α-Ketoglutarate (oxoglutarate):H+ symporter.

2.A.1.6.3.name: Dicarboxylate:H+ symporter.
2.A.1.6.3.description: Dicarboxylate:H+ symporter. Transports and serves as a chemoreceptor for β-ketoadipate (Karimian and Ornston 1981).

2.A.1.6.4.name: (Proline/glycine-betaine):(H+/Na+) symporter, ProP (subject to osmotic activation).
2.A.1.6.4.description: (Proline/glycine-betaine):(H+/Na+) symporter, ProP (also transports taurine, ectoine, pipecolate, proline-betaine, N,N-dimethylglycine, carnitine, and 1-carboxymethyl-pyridinium) (subject to osmotic activation). Transmembrane helix I and periplasmic loop 1 are involved in osmosensing and osmoprotectant transport (Keates et al., 2010). ProP detects the increase in cytoplasmic cation concentration…

2.A.1.6.7.name: The citrate/tricarballylate:H+ symporter (CitA or TcuC); probably orthologous to 2.A.1.6.1
2.A.1.6.7.description: The citrate/tricarballylate:H+ symporter (CitA or TcuC); probably orthologous to 2.A.1.6.1 (Lewis et al., 2004)
2.A.1.6.7.proteins: TcuC of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium LT2 (P0A2G3)

2.A.1.6.8.name: The acetate/monochloroacetate (haloacid) permease, Deh4p (Km = 5.5 mμM for acetate; 9 mμM for monochloroacetate).
2.A.1.6.8.description: The acetate/monochloroacetate (haloacid) permease, Deh4p (Km = 5.5 mμM for acetate; 9 mμM for monochloroacetate) (Yu et al., 2007; Su and Tsang 2012).
2.A.1.6.8.proteins: Deh4 of Burkholderia cepacia or sp. MBA4 (Q7X4L6)

2.A.1.6.9.name: YdfJ.
2.A.1.6.9.description: YdfJ. Can function as an inward rectifying K+ channel when expressed in animal cells as measured by whole cell patch clamping. Blocked by barium and protopine (Tang et al., 2011).

2.A.1.60.3.name: The multidrug (quinolone; tetarcycline) resistance pump, TcrA.
2.A.1.60.3.description: The multidrug (quinolone; tetarcycline) resistance pump, TcrA (Chang et al. 2011).

2.A.1.62.2.name: Putative Macrolide efflux pump (P-MEP), possibly involved in transport of amino acids and their derivatives.
2.A.1.62.2.description: Putative Macrolide efflux pump (P-MEP), possibly involved in transport of amino acids and their derivatives.

2.A.1.66.1.name: MFS permease of unknown function (First half resembles 2.A.1.3.7 (e-11) and 2.A.1.15.3 (e-8)).
2.A.1.66.1.description: MFS permease of unknown function (First half resembles 2.A.1.3.7 (e-11) and 2.A.1.15.3 (e-8)). Very likely to be a galactoside/galactose transporter; encoded within a gene cluster with β-galactosidase and galactose metabolic genes.

2.A.1.66.2.name: Putative 4-hydroxybenzoate uptake transporter, MFS_1, using S-adenyl methionine (SAM) as substrate.
2.A.1.66.2.description: Putative 4-hydroxybenzoate uptake transporter, MFS_1 (in an operon with 2,3-diketo-5-methylthiopentyl-1-phosphate enolase-phosphatase of the methionine salvage pathway), using S-adenyl methionine (SAM) as substrate. May transport SAM.

2.A.1.66.8.name: Pantothenate:H+ symporter, PAT or TMP1 of 565 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.66.8.description: Pantothenate:H+ symporter, PAT or TMP1 of 565 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement (Wunderlich 2022).

2.A.1.67.6.name: MfsB (Smlt0548) (B2FL18) of 404 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.67.6.description: MfsB (Smlt0548) (B2FL18) of 404 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Its function is not known (Boonyakanog et al. 2022).

2.A.1.68.1.name: The glucose transporter, OEOE_1574; does not transport fructose.
2.A.1.68.1.description: The glucose transporter, OEOE_1574; does not transport fructose (Kim et al., 2011).

2.A.1.7.1.name: L-Fucose:H+ symporter.
2.A.1.7.1.description: L-Fucose:H+ symporter. The x-ray structure (3.1Å resolution) with an outward open, amphipathic cavity has been solved. Asp46 and Glu135 can undergo cycles of protonation (Dang et al., 2010).

2.A.1.7.10.name: The putative glucose porter, GlcP.
2.A.1.7.10.description: The putative glucose porter, GlcP (Rodionov et al., 2010).

2.A.1.7.11.name: The putative mannose porter, ManPl.
2.A.1.7.11.description: The putative mannose porter, ManPl (Rodionov et al., 2010).

2.A.1.7.12.name: The putative trehalose porter, TreT
2.A.1.7.12.description: The putative trehalose porter, TreT (Rodionov et al., 2010)

2.A.1.7.14.name: Protein TsgA, also called GutS, YhfC, YhfH. tsgA i(gutS) gene expression is up-regulated by tellurite and selenite.
2.A.1.7.14.description: Protein TsgA, also called GutS, YhfC, YhfH. tsgA i(gutS) gene expression is up-regulated by tellurite and selenite (Guzzo and Dubow 2000).

2.A.1.7.16.name: The putative mannose porter, ManP (Rodionov D.A., personal communication).
2.A.1.7.16.description: The putative mannose porter, ManP (Rodionov D.A., personal communication). Regulated by mannose regulon ManR.

2.A.1.7.17.name: The putative fructose porter, FruP (Rodionov D.A., personal communication).
2.A.1.7.17.description: The putative fructose porter, FruP (Rodionov D.A., personal communication). Regulated by fructose oligosaccharide utilization regulon.

2.A.1.7.18.name: The putative N-acetylglucosamine porter, NagP (Rodionov D.A., personal communication).
2.A.1.7.18.description: The putative N-acetylglucosamine porter, NagP (Rodionov D.A., personal communication). Regulated by heparin utilization regulon.

2.A.1.7.19.name: Probable glucose transporter encoded by a gene sandwiched in between two genes encoding a glucose 1-dehydrogenase and a gluconolactonase.
2.A.1.7.19.description: Probable glucose transporter encoded by a gene sandwiched in between two genes encoding a glucose 1-dehydrogenase and a gluconolactonase.

2.A.1.7.23.name: Na+-dependent glucose transporter 1, Mfsd4b, of 491 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.7.23.description: Na+-dependent glucose transporter 1, Mfsd4b, of 491 aas and 12 TMSs. May also serve as a channels for urea in the inner medulla of the kidney.
2.A.1.7.23.proteins: Mfsd4b of Xenopus laevis (African clawed frog)

2.A.1.7.27.name: Na+/Glucose co-transporter, SGLT1, SLC60A2 or MfsD4B, of 518 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.7.27.description: Na+/Glucose co-transporter, SGLT1, SLC60A2 or MfsD4B, of 518 aas and 12 TMSs (Perland et al. 2017). SY009 is a novel SGLT1 inhibitor that exerts effects on the plasma metabolome and bile acids in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (Yang et al. 2025).

2.A.1.7.3.name: Glucose/Mannose/Xylose: H+ symporter.
2.A.1.7.3.description: Glucose/Mannose/Xylose: H+ symporter (Paulsen et al., 1998; G.Gosset, personal communication).

2.A.1.7.4.name: Rat kidney Na+-dependent glucose (methyl α-glucoside) transporter, NaGLT1 or SGLT1 (glucose:Na+:Na+=1:1).
2.A.1.7.4.description: Rat kidney Na+-dependent glucose (methyl α-glucoside) transporter, NaGLT1 or SGLT1 (glucose:Na+:Na+=1:1) (Horiba et al., 2003). Position 170 of Rabbit Na+/glucose cotransporter (rSGLT1) lies in the Na+ pathway, and modulation of polarity/charge at this site regulates charge transfer and carrier turnover (Huntley et al. 2004). The fine-tuning of glucose uptake mechanisms is rendered by various…

2.A.1.7.5.name: 2-Deoxy-D-ribose porter, DeoP.
2.A.1.7.5.description: 2-Deoxy-D-ribose porter, DeoP (Christensen et al., 2003). Plays a role in colonization of the mouse intestine (Martinez-Jéhanne et al. 2009).

2.A.1.7.7.name: The Na+-dependent sugar transporter, HP1174 (transports glucose, galactose, mannose and 2-deoxyglucose). (most similar to 2.A.1.7.2; 49% identity)
2.A.1.7.7.description: The Na+-dependent sugar transporter, HP1174 (transports glucose, galactose, mannose and 2-deoxyglucose (Psakis et al. 2009)). (most similar to 2.A.1.7.2; 49% identity)

2.A.1.7.9.name: The putative N-acetylgalactosamine porter, AgaP.
2.A.1.7.9.description: The putative N-acetylgalactosamine porter, AgaP (Leyn et al. 2012).

2.A.1.70.4.name: Uncharacterized MFS protein of 412 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.70.4.description: Uncharacterized MFS protein of 412 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.70.9.name: ArsK, exporter of arsenite, antimonite, trivalent roxarsone and methylarsenite.
2.A.1.70.9.description: ArsK, exporter of arsenite, antimonite, trivalent roxarsone and methylarsenite (Shi et al. 2018). Expression of arsK is induced by arsenite [As(III)], antimonite [Sb(III)], trivalent roxarsone [Rox(III)], methylarsenite [MAs(III)] and arsenate [As(V)], and heterologous expression of ArsK in an arsenic-hypersensitive E. coli strain showed that ArsK is essential for resistance to As(III), Sb(III)…

2.A.1.71.1.name: The Valanimycin-resistance determinant, VlmF (probably a valanimycin:H antiporter)
2.A.1.71.1.description: The Valanimycin-resistance determinant, VlmF (probably a valanimycin:H antiporter (Ma et al., 2000))

2.A.1.71.3.name: MFS transporter of 375 aas and 11 TMSs
2.A.1.71.3.description: MFS transporter of 375 aas and 11 TMSs

2.A.1.75.1.name: Probable transporter MCH1.
2.A.1.75.1.description: Probable transporter MCH1. Although the name, "monocarboxylate transporter homologue 1" implies that this system transports monocarboxylates such as lactate, pyruvate and acetate, no evidence for this possibility was obtained (Makuc et al. 2001). Instead, the mch1-5 mutant strain, lacking all 5 such paralogues in yeast showed strongly reduced biomass yields in aerobic glucose-limited chemostat…

2.A.1.75.2.name: MFS putative monocarboxylic acid transporter, UMF23B
2.A.1.75.2.description: MFS putative monocarboxylic acid transporter, UMF23B

2.A.1.75.8.name: PICLORAM RESISTANT30 (PIC30) protein of 601 aas and 12 or 14 TMSs.
2.A.1.75.8.description: PICLORAM RESISTANT30 (PIC30) protein of 601 aas and 12 or 14 TMSs. It is a plasma membrane anion uptake porter, transporting picloram and other picolinate herbicides as well as nitrate, chlorate and chloride anions (Kathare et al. 2019).

2.A.1.8.1.name: Nitrate/H+ symporter (K1);Nitrate/nitrite antiporter (K2).
2.A.1.8.1.description: Nitrate/H+ symporter (K1);Nitrate/nitrite antiporter (K2). The 3-d structure is available revealing a positively charged pathway for nitrate/nitrite lined with arginine residues with no apparent proton pathway suggesting exchange transport is the primary or sole mechanism. The pathway is between the two halves of the protein and a rocker switch mechanism was proposed (Zheng et al. 2013). In an in…

2.A.1.8.10.name: NO3-/NO2- transporter (NO3- uptake permease; NO2- exporter) (probable NO3-/NO2- antiporter)
2.A.1.8.10.description: NO3-/NO2- transporter (NO3- uptake permease; NO2- exporter) (probable NO3-/NO2- antiporter) (stress-induced; Clegg et al., 2006; Jia et al. 2009)

2.A.1.8.11.name: The 24 TMS, 2 domain, NarK1-NarK2 porter (NarK1 = a NO3-/H+ symporter; NarK2 = a NO3-/NO2- antiporter).
2.A.1.8.11.description: The 24 TMS, 2 domain, NarK1-NarK2 porter (NarK1 = a NO3-/H+ symporter; NarK2 = a NO3-/NO2- antiporter). NarK1 is a nitrate/proton symporter with high affinity for nitrate while NarK2 is a nitrate/nitrite antiporter with lower affinity for nitrate (Goddard et al., 2008). Each transporter requires two conserved arginine residues for activity. A transporter consisting of inactivated NarK1 fused to…

2.A.1.8.12.name: The root cortical and epidermal cell, high affinity, plasma membrane, NO3- uptake transporter, NRT2.1.
2.A.1.8.12.description: The root cortical and epidermal cell, high affinity, plasma membrane, NO3- uptake transporter, NRT2.1 (Wirth et al., 2007). Also functions in nitrate sensing and signaling (Miller et al., 2007; Girin et al., 2010). Activity only occurs when NRT2.1 is complexed with NAR2.1 (WR3; 8.A.20.1.1) in a 2:2 tetrameric complex (Yong et al., 2010). NAR2.1 has an N-terminal and a C-terminal TMS and has been…

2.A.1.8.13.name: High affinity nitrate/nitrite antiporter and uptake porter, NrtB.
2.A.1.8.13.description: High affinity nitrate/nitrite antiporter and uptake porter, NrtB (Unkles et al., 1991; 2011; Wang et al. 2008).

2.A.1.8.14.name: Nitrate/nitrite uptake porter, NapA
2.A.1.8.14.description: Nitrate/nitrite uptake porter, NapA (Wang et al., 2000)

2.A.1.8.15.name: Probable nitrate transporter NarT of 388 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.8.15.description: Probable nitrate transporter NarT of 388 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. In Corynebacterium pseudotuberculosis, an insertional mutation in the MFS transporter, NarT, may influence pathogenesis (Hiller et al. 2024).

2.A.1.8.17.name: Nitrate/nitrite transporter, NarK2, of 468 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.8.17.description: Nitrate/nitrite transporter, NarK2, of 468 aas and 12 TMSs. The narK1 and narK2 genes are located in an operon, narK1K2GHJI, with the structural genes for the nitrate reductase complex. Utilizing an isogenic narK1 mutant, a narK2 mutant, and a narK1K2 double mutant, Sharma et al. 2006 explored the effect on growth under denitrifying conditions. While the ΔnarK1::Gm mutant was only slightly…

2.A.1.8.18.name: NRT2.1 high affinity Na+-dependent nitrate uptake porter of 517 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.8.18.description: NRT2.1 high affinity Na+-dependent nitrate uptake porter of 517 aas and 12 TMSs. It functions with the aoxillary protein, NAR2 (TC# 8.A.20.1.2) (Rubio et al. 2019). Functional characterization of the GhNRT2.1e gene revealed its role in improving nitrogen use efficiency in Gossypium hirsutum (Zhang et al. 2023). The high-affinity nitrate transporter 2 (NRT2) gene family proteins have been examined…

2.A.1.8.19.name: Nitrate transporter, NRT2.4, of 527 aas with 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.8.19.description: Nitrate transporter, NRT2.4, of 527 aas with 12 TMSs. AtNRT2.4 responds to local and systemic nitrogen signaling in Arabidopsis thaliana (Zhang et al. 2025). It plays a crucial role in local and systemic nitrate signals sensing, adjustment of root architecture, and anthocyanin accumulation.

2.A.1.8.5.name: Nitrate/nitrite transporter/antiporter, CrnA/NrtA.
2.A.1.8.5.description: Nitrate/nitrite transporter/antiporter, CrnA/NrtA (Unkles et al., 1991; Beckham et al. 2010). The nitrate signature sequences (NS1 and NS2) in TMSs 5 and 11 and arg residues in TMSs 2 and 8 may influence substrate binding (Unkles et al., 2012).

2.A.1.8.7.name: High affinity Nitrate/nitrite uptake transporter, Nar4.
2.A.1.8.7.description: High affinity Nitrate/nitrite uptake transporter, Nar4.

2.A.1.8.8.name: NO2- extrusion, NO3-/NO2- exchange permease, NarK1
2.A.1.8.8.description: NO2- extrusion, NO3-/NO2- exchange permease, NarK1

2.A.1.8.9.name: NO2- extrusion, NO3-/NO2- exchange permease, NarK2
2.A.1.8.9.description: NO2- extrusion, NO3-/NO2- exchange permease, NarK2

2.A.1.81.1.name: The copper (Cu2+) uptake porter, CcoA of 405 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.81.1.description: The copper (Cu2+) uptake porter, CcoA of 405 aas and 12 TMSs. CcoA-mediated Cu2+ import relies on conserved Met and His residues that could act as metal ligands at the membrane-embedded Cu2+-binding domain (Khalfaoui-Hassani et al. 2016). It provides cytoplasmic Cu needed for cbb3-type cytochrome c oxidase (cbb3-Cox) biogenesis (Khalfaoui-Hassani et al. 2021). Residues important for and/or…

2.A.1.81.2.name: Putative copper uptake porter, MFS_1 of 420 aas
2.A.1.81.2.description: Putative copper uptake porter, MFS_1 of 420 aas

2.A.1.81.4.name: MFS porter of 350 aas
2.A.1.81.4.proteins: MFS porter of Candidatus Caldiarchaeum subterraneum

2.A.1.81.5.name: Riboflavin uptake transporter of 398 aas and 12 TMSs, RfnT.
2.A.1.81.5.description: Riboflavin uptake transporter of 398 aas and 12 TMSs, RfnT (Gutiérrez-Preciado et al. 2015).

2.A.1.82.1.name: The barley copper uptake porter, CT-1 of 749 aas; nearly identical to the wheat orthologue.
2.A.1.82.1.description: The barley copper uptake porter, CT-1 of 749 aas; nearly identical to the wheat orthologue (Li et al. 2013).

2.A.1.82.2.name: The putative copper uptake porter, CT1, of 825 aas.
2.A.1.82.2.description: The putative copper uptake porter, CT1, of 825 aas. The C-terminal domain of 300 aas is a DUF572 (COG5134) domain.

2.A.1.82.3.name: Synaptic vesicle 2-related protein (SV2-related protein), SVOP or SLC22B4.
2.A.1.82.3.description: Synaptic vesicle 2-related protein (SV2-related protein), SVOP or SLC22B4. This protein localizes to neurotransmitter-containing vesicles and has a nucleotide binding site (Yao and Bajjalieh 2009). ATP, GTP, TTP, CTP and NAD biind, with the highest affinity for NAD, in contrast to SV2 (TC# 2.A.1.22.1), which binds both NAD and ATP with equal affinity. May transport nicotinate.

2.A.1.82.4.name: Niacin uptake porter NiaP
2.A.1.82.4.description: Niacin uptake porter NiaP (Jeanguenin et al. 2012)

2.A.1.83.1.name: MFS porter; 1-arseno-3-phosphoglycerate (1As3PGA) exporter, ArsJ.
2.A.1.83.1.description: MFS porter; 1-arseno-3-phosphoglycerate (1As3PGA) exporter, ArsJ. Encoded in an operon concerned with arsenic resistance, encoding the enzymes and transporters of a new pathway of arsenic biotransformation. The adjacent gene encodes a 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase homologue that probably forms the substrate of this MFS porter which could be expelled from the cell (Chen et al. 2016).

2.A.1.86.4.name: Uncharacterized putative S-adenosyl-L-methionine-dependent methyltransferase with a 7 TMS N-terminus.
2.A.1.86.4.description: Uncharacterized putative S-adenosyl-L-methionine-dependent methyltransferase with a 7 TMS N-terminus (Pegg and Michael 2010).

2.A.1.86.5.name: Polyamine aminopropyltransferase or spermidine synthase of 516 aas and 7 N-terminal TMSs.
2.A.1.86.5.description: Polyamine aminopropyltransferase or spermidine synthase of 516 aas and 7 N-terminal TMSs.

2.A.1.9.1.name: High affinity Pi uptake porter, SUL1, Sul-1, SFP2 of 859 aas and 10 TMSs.; may transport a phosphate·Mn2+ complex.
2.A.1.9.1.description: High affinity Pi uptake porter, SUL1, Sul-1, SFP2 of 859 aas and 10 TMSs. (also functions in Mn2+ homeostasis); may transport a phosphate·Mn2+ complex (Jensen et al., 2003). Also takes up selenite (Lazard et al., 2010). May be a "transceptor", combining transport and receptor functions (Diallinas 2017).

2.A.1.9.10.name: High affinity (25 mμM) phosphate uptake porter, PiPT.
2.A.1.9.10.description: High affinity (25 mμM) phosphate uptake porter, PiPT (Yadav et al. 2010). The high resolution structure has been determined by x-ray crystallography (Pedersen et al. 2013).

2.A.1.9.11.name: Phosphate transporter, PT, of 543 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.9.11.description: Phosphate transporter, PT, of 543 aas and 12 TMSs. It has a micormolar Km for phosphate uptake, is found in the plasma membrane and is induced by low medium phosphate concentrations (Wang et al. 2014).
2.A.1.9.11.proteins: PT in the ectomycorrhizal fungus, Boletus edulis

2.A.1.9.12.name: Phosphate transporter and receptor (transceptor) of 543 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.9.12.description: Phosphate transporter and receptor (transceptor) of 543 aas and 12 TMSs. Important for signalling and uptake of phosphate. The majority of terrestrial vascular plants can form mutualistic associations with obligate biotrophic arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi from the phylum Glomeromycota. This mutualistic symbiosis provides carbohydrates to the fungus, and reciprocally improves plant phosphate…

2.A.1.9.13.name: High-affinity phosphate transporter of 511 aas and 12 TMSs, PHT1.
2.A.1.9.13.description: High-affinity phosphate transporter of 511 aas and 12 TMSs, PHT1. It is root inducible by phosphate starvation but is not expressed in leaves (Ahmadi et al. 2018).
2.A.1.9.13.proteins: PHT1 of Elaeis guineensis var. tenera (Oil palm)

2.A.1.9.14.name: Pho84 inorganic phosphate transporter of 572 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.9.14.description: Pho84 inorganic phosphate transporter of 572 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Phosphate starvation upregulates the expression of the pho84 gene as well as varioius phosphatase genes (Innokentev et al. 2024).

2.A.1.9.15.name: SIPT3 or PHT1 phosphate transporter of 534 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.9.15.description: SIPT3 or PHT1 phosphate transporter of 534 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. A mycorrhiza-inducible phosphate transporter SlPT3 regulates phosphate uptake, iron homeostasis, and arbuscule development in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) under combined nutrient stress conditions (Fan et al. 2026).

2.A.1.9.2.name: Phosphate-repressible, high affinity Pi uptake porter, Pho84 or Pho-5 of 570 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.9.2.description: Phosphate-repressible, high affinity Pi uptake porter, Pho84 or Pho-5 of 570 aas and 12 TMSs (Versaw 1995).

2.A.1.9.3.name: Pi uptake porter.
2.A.1.9.3.description: Pi uptake porter. Four close paralogues in Medicago truncatula (PT1-4), all localized to roots, show differing affinities for phosphate (Liu et al. 2008).

2.A.1.9.4.name: Pht1;2(1;4) (PT2), a low affinity Pi uptake transporter, functioning throughout the plant (76% identical to 2.A.1.9.3).
2.A.1.9.4.description: Pht1;2(1;4) (PT2), a low affinity Pi uptake transporter, functioning throughout the plant (Ai et al., 2009) (76% identical to 2.A.1.9.3).

2.A.1.9.5.name: Pht1;6 (PT6), a high affinity Pi uptake transporter, functioning thoughout the plant (75% identical to 2.A.1.9.3)
2.A.1.9.5.description: Pht1;6 (PT6), a high affinity Pi uptake transporter, functioning thoughout the plant (Ai et al., 2009) (75% identical to 2.A.1.9.3)

2.A.1.9.6.name: Phosphate transporter-5, PT5.
2.A.1.9.6.description: Phosphate transporter-5, PT5. Catalyzes phosphate:H+ symport (Liu et al., 2008).

2.A.1.9.7.name: Organic phosphate transport protein GIT1.
2.A.1.9.7.description: Organic phosphate (glycerophosphoinositol and glycerophosphocholine, the products of phospholipase-B mediated deacylation of phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylcholine, respectively) transport protein GIT1 (Almaguer et al. 2006).

2.A.1.9.9.name: Inorganic phosphate transporter 1-1 (AtPht1;1; APT2, PHT1) (H+/Pi cotransporter).
2.A.1.9.9.description: Inorganic phosphate transporter 1-1 (AtPht1;1; APT2, PHT1) (H+/Pi cotransporter). A Brassica napus homologue, Pht1;4, catalyzes phosphate uptake and affects root architecture (Ren et al. 2014). The phylogeny and expression levels in plant tissues of the proteins of this family in potato have been examined (Liu et al. 2017). The chrysanthemum Pht1;2 is induced in the roots by phosphate starvation…

2.A.10.1.3.name: Probable galacturonate uptake porter of 330 aas and 10 TMSs.
2.A.10.1.3.description: Probable galacturonate uptake porter of 330 aas and 10 TMSs (Pujic et al. 1998).
2.A.10.1.3.proteins: Probable galacturonate uptake porter of Bacillus subtilis

2.A.10.1.5.name: N-terminal KdgT domain with 10 TMS and a C-terminal N-acetyl transferase (NAT) domain.
2.A.10.1.5.description: N-terminal KdgT domain with 10 TMS and a C-terminal N-acetyl transferase (NAT) domain. 462 aas total.

2.A.102.2.1.name: Sulfolactate (sulfite/organosulfonate) exporter,TauE of 256 aas with 8 TMSs in a 4 + 4 TMS arrangement.

2.A.17.1.4.name: DtpD (YbgH) peptide transporter.
2.A.17.1.4.description: DtpD (YbgH) peptide transporter. A projection structure at 19 Å resolution and a high resolution x-ray structure are available; Casagrande et al., 2009; Zhao et al. 2014). Glu21 is the only conserved proton-titratable amino acyl residue (among POTs) that is located in the central cavity, and it is critical for in vivo transport (Zhao et al. 2014).

2.A.17.1.5.name: Peptide transporter, YjdL (preference for di-peptides).
2.A.17.1.5.description: Peptide transporter, YjdL (preference for di-peptides) (Ernst et al., 2009; Gabrielsen et al., 2011; Jensen et al., 2011). The motif, ExxERFxxYY has been shown to be involved in proton translocation, and the nearby K117 may play a dual role in protonation and substrate binding (Jensen et al. 2014).

2.A.17.1.6.name: POT famiy di- and tri-peptide porter, DtpT.
2.A.17.1.6.description: POT famiy di- and tri-peptide porter, DtpT. 3-d structures (PDB:24APS; 5MMT: 5D58' 5D59) are available for an inward open conformation. A hinge-like movement in the C-terminal half facilitates opening of an intracellular gate controlling access to a central peptide binding site. Salt bridges may orchestrate alternating access (Solcan et al., 2012; Quistgaard et al. 2017).
2.A.17.1.6.proteins: Peptide porter, DtpT of Streptococcus thermophilus (Q5M4H8)

2.A.17.1.7.name: Peptide uptake transporter of 496 aas, POT.
2.A.17.1.7.description: Peptide uptake transporter of 496 aas, POT. The 3-d structure has been determined to 1.9Å resolution leading to a proposed mechanism (Doki et al. 2013). Glu310 first may bind the carboxyl group of the peptide substrate. Then deprotonation of Glu310 in the inward open state triggers the release of the bound peptide toward the intracellular space, and salt bridge formation between Glu310 and Arg43…

2.A.17.1.8.name: Proton-coupled oligopeptide uptake transporter of 485 aas and 14 TMSs, DtpT or Pot.
2.A.17.1.8.description: Proton-coupled oligopeptide uptake transporter of 485 aas and 14 TMSs, DtpT or Pot. Expression of the encoded gene is upregulated upon infection. Transports di- and tripeptides but can not accumulate peptides with a positively charged residue in the C-terminal position. An aromatic residue patch in the active site of the transporter may be responsible for it's unusual specificity (Sharma et al…

2.A.17.1.9.name: Di-/tripeptide transporter DtpT of 501 aas with 13 TMSs.
2.A.17.1.9.description: Di-/tripeptide transporter DtpT of 501 aas with 13 TMSs. DtpT plays an important role in biofilm formation and stress resistance in foodborne Staphylococcus aureus RMSA49 (Wu et al. 2025).

2.A.17.2.2.name: Peptide:H+ symporter dipeptides and tripeptides preferred.
2.A.17.2.2.description: Peptide:H+ symporter (dipeptides and tripeptides preferred (Cai et al., 2007). Substrate preference is altered by mutations in the fifth TMS of Ptr2p (Hauser et al. 2013).

2.A.17.2.3.name: Dipeptide uptake porter, Ptr2.
2.A.17.2.3.description: Dipeptide uptake porter, Ptr2. Transports dipeptides such as Ala-Leu, Ala-Tyr and Tyr-Ala (Belmondo et al. 2014).
2.A.17.2.3.proteins: Ptr2 of Rhizophagus irregularis (Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus) (Glomus intraradices)

2.A.17.2.4.name: Di- and tripeptide uptake transporter, Ptr2 of 577 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.17.2.4.description: Di- and tripeptide uptake transporter, Ptr2 of 577 aas and 12 TMSs. The ptr2 gene showed increased expression upon interaction with the plant-pathogenic fungus Botrytis cinerea, suggesting that it is involved in the mycoparasitic process. Its expression was triggered by nitrogen starvation (Vizcaíno et al. 2006).

2.A.17.2.5.name: Oligopeptide transporter of 576 aas and 12 TMSs, PTR22.
2.A.17.2.5.description: Oligopeptide transporter of 576 aas and 12 TMSs, PTR22. Transports a variety of peptides as well as derivatives of antifungal agents, such as chlorotetaine and lysyl-cholortetaine (Liu et al. 2018).

2.A.17.3.1.description: Dual affinity Nitrate/Chlorate symporter, Nrt1.1; CHL1 of 590 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement (Martin et al., 2008). The low affinity form is a homo-dimer and has Thr101 in the non-phosphorylated form; the high affinty form (0.1 micromolar Km) is a monomer and has Thr101 phosphorylated (Sun and Zheng 2015). Rehmannia glutinosa (Chinese foxglove) has 18 ntr1 genes encoding proteins of…

2.A.17.3.10.name: solute carrier family 15, member 5.
2.A.17.3.10.description: solute carrier family 15, member 5. Function unknown as of 1/17, but probably a di- and tri-peptide uptake porter (Verri et al. 2016). The tissue expression profile has been reported (Sreedharan et al. 2011). SLC15A5 and RERG are linked with fat yield in cow's milk (Silva et al. 2026).

2.A.17.3.11.name: Solute carrier family 15 member 4 (Peptide transporter 4) (Peptide/histidine transporter 1) (hPHT1; SLC15A4;) is present in immune cells.
2.A.17.3.11.description: Solute carrier family 15 member 4 (Peptide transporter 4) (Peptide/histidine transporter 1) (hPHT1; SLC15A4;) is present in immune cells (Verri et al. 2016). 2.A.17.3.16.name: Nitrate transporter 1.2 (Nitrate transporter NTL1; NRT1:2; PRT family protein 4.6; NPF4.6; AIT1).
2.A.17.3.16.description: Nitrate transporter 1.2 (Nitrate transporter NTL1; NRT1:2; PRT family protein 4.6; NPF4.6; AIT1). Low-affinity proton-dependent nitrate transporter involved in constitutive nitrate uptake but not histidine or dipeptides transport. Involved in (+)-abscisic acid (ABA) transport, but not in gibberellin, indole-3-acetic acid or jasmonic acid import; ABA and nitrate do not compete for substrate uptake…

2.A.17.3.2.name: Histidine or peptide:H+ symporter of 585 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.17.3.2.description: Histidine or peptide:H+ symporter of 585 aas and 12 TMSs. It mediates the transport of di- and tripeptides with high affinity, low capacity (Rentsch et al. 1995).

2.A.17.3.20.name: High-affinity, proton-dependent glucosinolate-specific transporter-2, GTP2 or NPF2.11.
2.A.17.3.20.description: High-affinity, proton-dependent glucosinolate-specific transporter-2, GTP2 or NPF2.11. Involved in apoplasmic phloem-loading of glucosinolates and in bidirectional long-distance transport of aliphatic but not indole glucosinolates. May be involved in removal of glucosinolates from the xylem in roots (Nour-Eldin et al. 2012; Andersen et al. 2013).

2.A.17.3.21.description: Low affinity nitrate transporter, Nrt1, of 584 aas and 13 putative TMSs. Two splice variants, Ntr1.1a and Ntr1.1b, have been identified. Under low nitrogen condition, Nrt1.1b accumulates more nitrogen in plants and improves rice growth, but Ntr1.1a had no such effect (Fan et al. 2015). 2.A.17.3.27.name: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glycerate transporter AtNPF8.4 or Npf8.4, of 545 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.
2.A.17.3.27.description: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glycerate transporter AtNPF8.4 or Npf8.4, of 545 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs. It facilitates shuttling of glycerate between peroxysomes and chloroplasts (Lin and Tsay 2023). It is a tonoplast glycerate uptake system that plays a role of photorespiration in C/N balance (Lin and Tsay 2023).

2.A.17.3.3.description: Nitrate (chlorate) or histidine:H+ symporter of 589 aas and 12 TMSs, Ntr1. Its structural gene is specifically expressed in the floral nectaries of Brassica species (Song et al. 2000).

2.A.17.3.8.description: The germinating pollen dipeptide/tripeptide transporter, PTR5 (Komarova et al., 2008). Transport is electrogenic and dependent on protons. Leak currents are inhibited by Phe-Ala when this peptide binds at the active site with high affinity (Hammes et al., 2010).

2.A.17.3.9.description: solute carrier family 15, member 3, SLC15A3, OCTP, PHT2, PHT3, of 581 aas and 12 TMSs in a 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 TMS arrangement. It is a histidine + di- and tri-peptide uptake transporter in immune cells (Verri et al. 2016). The functions, regulation and pathophysiology of PHT2 and PHT1, specifically in immunoregulation have been reviewed (Dong et al. 2023).

2.A.17.4.3.name: High affinity oligopeptide transporter, CPTA.
2.A.17.4.3.description: High affinity oligopeptide transporter, CPTA. It transports di-, tri- and tetra peptides with low specificity. Neuropeptides (FMRF-amide and N-acetyl-Asp-Glu) are also transported (Fei et al. 1998).

2.A.17.4.4.description: The renal brush-border electrogenic, proton-coupled, broad specificity, high affinity, peptide transporter, PepT2 (Rubio-Aliaga et al., 2000). 2.A.19.2.12.description: Ca2+/Mg2+/Mn2+:H+ antiporter, CAX or CHA, of 441 aas with a 90 residue hydrophilic N-terminus followed by 11 TMSs (Wunderlich 2022).

2.A.19.2.3.description: High affinity vacuolar (tonoplast) Ca2+:H+ antiporter (also exports Cd2+ and Zn2+; Shigaki et al., 2005) It is expressed in leaves (Cheng et al., 2005). Cotransports glutamic acid with three Na+ followed by countertransport of K+(Teichman et al., 2009). The 50 residue 4B-4C loop (following TMS4) binds Na+ (Koch et al., 2007). (The dicarboxylic aminoaciduria protein in humans; NP_004161; Bröer, 2008a…

2.A.23.2.4.name: Aspartate/taurine (not glutamate):Na+ symporter, dEAAT2; L-glutamate is transported with low affinity and efficiency.
2.A.23.2.4.description: Aspartate/taurine (not glutamate):Na+ symporter, dEAAT2 (mediates both uptake and heteroexchange of its two substrates, both dependent on external Na+ (with taurine outside and Asp inside)); L-glutamate is transported with low affinity and efficiency (Besson et al., 2005).

2.A.23.2.6.name: Excitatory amino acid transporter 1 (EAAT1) (Sodium-dependent glutamate/aspartate transporter 1) (GLAST-1) (Solute carrier family 1 member 3).
2.A.23.2.6.description: Excitatory amino acid transporter 1 (EAAT1) (Sodium-dependent glutamate/aspartate transporter 1) (GLAST-1) (Solute carrier family 1 member 3). Mutations cause episodic ataxia type 6 (EA6) (Choi et al. 2016; Iwama et al. 2017). EAAT1 regulates the extent and duration of glutamate-mediated signals by the clearance of glutamate after synaptic release. It also has an anion channel activity that…

2.A.23.2.7.name: Excitatory amino acid transporter 2, EAAT2 (Glutamate/aspartate transporter II) (Solute carrier family 1 member 2).
2.A.23.2.7.description: Excitatory amino acid transporter 2, EAAT2 (Glutamate/aspartate transporter II) (Sodium-dependent glutamate/aspartate transporter 2) (Solute carrier family 1 member 2). This system may be important for the pathophysiology of schizophrenia (Parkin et al. 2018). Amino acids in the TMS2 of EAAT2 are essential for membrane-bound localization, substrate binding, transporter function and anion currents…

2.A.23.2.8.name: Excitatory amino acid transporter 4, EAAT4 (Sodium-dependent glutamate/aspartate transporter) (Solute carrier family 1 member 6).
2.A.23.2.8.description: Excitatory amino acid transporter 4, EAAT4 (Sodium-dependent glutamate/aspartate transporter) (Solute carrier family 1 member 6). Klotho, a 1012 aa protein with N- and C-terminal TMSs, is a regulator of the excitatory amino acid transporters EAAT3 and EAAT4 (Almilaji et al. 2013). Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), a protein kinase C (PKC) activator, enhanced Cl- currents via EAAT4, but this…

Syncytin-1, of 538 aas with 4-7 TMSs, is a viral fusion protein and is involved in the development of multiple sclerosis (Antony et al. 2007). Mutation causes nuerological problems including global developmental delay, severe…

2.A.23.3.2.name: Insulin-activated, Na+-dependet amino acid (serine, alanine, glutamate, glutamine and other neutral amino acids):amino acid antiporter.
2.A.23.3.2.description: Insulin-activated, Na+-dependet amino acid (serine, alanine, glutamate, glutamine and other neutral amino acids):amino acid antiporter (Ndaru et al. 2019). Also transports homocysteine (Jiang et al., 2007). V-9302 is a selective and potent competitive small molecule antagonist of glutamine uptake via ASCT2. Blockage of ASCT2 activity with V-9302 resulted in attenuated cancer cell growth and…
2.A.23.3.2.proteins: Insulin-dependent amino acid transporter B of Mus musculus, AscT2

2.A.23.3.3.name: Broad-specificity amino acid:Na+ symporter, LAT1, M7V1, RDR, RDRC, or SLC1A5.
2.A.23.3.3.description: Broad-specificity amino acid:Na+ symporter, LAT1, M7V1, RDR, RDRC, or SLC1A5 (transports most neutral, zwitterionic and dibasic amino acids either uptake or bidirectional transport) (Scalise et al. 2018). Required for intracellular multiplication of Legionella pneumophila (Wieland et al., 2005). SLC7A5 with accessory protein SLC3A2 (the heavy chain; TC# 8.A.9.2.2) mediates bidirectional transport…

2.A.25.1.2.description: Alanine:Na+ (or H+) symporter (Kamata et al. 1992; Kanamori et al. 1999). The sequence as reported appears to lack the first 45 aas and the first two tMSs, probably because of incorrect initiation codon selection.

2.A.25.1.4.name: The putative glycine porter, GlyP.
2.A.25.1.4.description: The putative glycine porter, GlyP. Regulated by Glycine riboswitch (Rodionov et al. 2011)

2.A.25.1.5.description: Amino-acid carrier protein, AlsT. Negatively regulated by TnrA (Yoshida et al. 2003).

2.A.25.1.6.description: Putative bifunctional protein of 748 aas and 12 TMSs with an N-terminal sodium:alanine symporter domain and a C-terminal phosphatidylserine decarboxylase proenzyme domain.

2.A.25.1.9.description: Probable Glycine/alanine/asparagine/glutamine uptake porter, AgcS (Bualuang et al. 2014).

2.A.26.1.1.description: Branched chain amino acid: Na+ symporter

2.A.26.1.10.name: Branched chain amino acid transporter 2 of 439 aas and 12 TMSs, BrnQ.
2.A.26.1.10.description: Branched chain amino acid transporter 2 of 439 aas and 12 TMSs, BrnQ (Guardiola et al. 1974). The brnQ gene can be mutated to give rise to threonine tolerance (Radi et al. 2022). However the wild type protein takes up threonine (in addition to leucine, isoleucine and valine) but with low affinity and high flux (Khozov et al. 2023).

2.A.26.1.4.name: The branched chain amino acid transporter BrnQ (transports Leu, Ile, Val, Phe, and Met).
2.A.26.1.4.description: The branched chain amino acid transporter BrnQ (transports Leu, Ile, Val, Phe, and Met) (Braun et al., 2008).

2.A.26.1.9.description: Branched chain amino acid (Leucine, Isoleucine, Valine) transporter of 456 aas and 12 TMSs, BrnQ (Trip et al. 2013).

2.A.27.1.1.name: Glutamate:Na+ symporter, GltS, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.27.1.1.description: Glutamate:Na+ symporter, GltS, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs. It transports L- and D-glutamate, α-methylglutamate and homocysteate. Swapping the order of the two halves (repeat units) does not decrease activity (Dobrowolski and Lolkema, 2010).

2.A.27.1.3.name: Probable L-glutamate/N-acetylglutamate uptake porter, GltS.
2.A.27.1.3.description: Probable L-glutamate/N-acetylglutamate uptake porter, GltS. Involved in N-acetylglutamate catabolism as a carbon and nitrogen source (Johnson et al. 2008).

2.A.27.1.4.name: Sodium/glutamate symporter, GltS, YbfA, JemA, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.27.1.4.description: Sodium/glutamate symporter, GltS, YbfA, JemA, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs. Note, the Na+:Glutamate symporter with TC# 2.A.27.1.1 is also called GltS. YbfA regulates the sensitivity of E. coli K12 to plantaricin BM-1 via the BasS/BasR two- component regulatory system (Chen et al. 2021).

2.A.27.1.5.name: sodium:glutamate symporter of 476 aas and 12 TMSs, GltS.
2.A.27.1.5.description: sodium:glutamate symporter of 476 aas and 12 TMSs, GltS. It has a Km for glutamate of 5 μM, but has low affinity for Na+. Glutamate uptake is inhibited by glu, gln, asp and asn (Boonburapong et al. 2012).

2.A.27.1.6.name: Na2+:glutamate symporter, GltS, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement, functioning with a periplasmic L-glutamate binding protein.
2.A.27.1.6.description: Na2+:glutamate symporter, GltS, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement, functioning with a periplasmic L-glutamate binding protein (Jaques et al. 2025). BP0403 binds L-glutamate with nanomolar affinity. Genome context analysis of BP0403 reveals no TRAP membrane component genes; instead, it co-localizes with translational coupling with gltS, encoding a Na+/glutamate symporter. In other…
2.A.27.1.6.proteins: GltS with a periplasmic L-glutamate BP of Bordetella pertussis

2.A.27.1.7.name: Fused L-glutamate periplasmic binding protein N-terminal (residues 1 - 306) followed by a 12 TMS integral membrane GltS transporter domain.
2.A.27.1.7.description: Fused L-glutamate periplasmic binding protein (N-terminal (residues 1 - 306) followed by a 12 TMS integral membrane GltS transporter domain (residues 325 - 712). It is probably a heterotetramer (Jaques et al. 2025).
2.A.27.1.7.proteins: Fused BP0403-like domain (N-terminal) - GltS (C-terminal) of Lachnoanerobaculum gingivalis

2.A.27.1.8.name: Fused L-glutamate periplasmic binding protein N-terminal (residues 1 - 306) followed by a 12 TMS integral membrane GltS transporter domain.
2.A.27.1.8.description: Fused L-glutamate periplasmic binding protein (N-terminal (residues 1 - 306) followed by a 12 TMS integral membrane GltS transporter domain (residues 325 - 712). It is probably a heterotetramer (Jaques et al. 2025).
2.A.27.1.8.proteins: Fused BP0403-like domain (N-terminal) - GltS of Lachnoanerobaculum saburreum

2.A.28.1.1.name: Organic acid/(conjugated) bile acid (taurocholate):Na+ symporter.
2.A.28.1.1.description: Organic acid/(conjugated) bile acid (taurocholate):Na+ symporter. Taurine conjugates > glycine conjugates > unconjugated bile salts. The initial effect on hepatic bile flow of cholestatic agents such as thorazine and estradiol 17beta-glucuronide are on water flow and not bile salt export pump-mediated bile acid transport (Javitt 2020).
2.A.28.1.1.proteins: Liver bile acid uptake system of Rattus norvegicus

2.A.28.1.10.proteins: BASS family homologue of Myxococcus xanthus

2.A.28.1.11.description: Apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter, SBAT of 546 aas and 9 - 12 TMSs. It is essential for survival of a carcinogenic liver fluke Clonorchis sinensis in the bile (Dai et al. 2020).

2.A.28.1.2.name: Liver/ileal bile acid:Na+ symporter, ASBT, ISBT or NTCP2 of 348 aas and 7 TMSs essential for liver or intestinal bile acid transport and homeostasis.
2.A.28.1.2.description: Liver/ileal bile acid:Na+ symporter, ASBT, ISBT or NTCP2 (SLC10A2) of 348 aas and 7 TMSs (Mareninova et al. 2005) (essential for liver or intestinal bile acid transport and homeostasis (Rao et al., 2008). This BART superfamily protein has been modeled in 3-dimensions using the 3-D structure of bacteriorhodopsin (a TOG superfamily member) (Zhang et al. 2004). TMS4 forms part of the substrate…

2.A.28.1.3.description: The organic anion:Na+ symporter, SOAT (transports estrone-3-sulfate (Km= 31 μM) and dehydropiandrosterone sulfate (Km = 30 μM) but not taurocholate, estradiol-17β-glucuronide or ouabain) (Geyer et al., 2004)

2.A.28.1.4.name: The organic anion:Na+ symporter, SOAT (probable paralogue of 2.A.28.1.3); a 7 TMS protein with the N-terminus out and the C-terminus in.
2.A.28.1.4.description: The organic anion:Na+ symporter, SOAT (probable paralogue of 2.A.28.1.3); a 7 TMS protein with the N-terminus out and the C-terminus in. Transports dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, estrone-3-sulfate, and pregnenolone sulfate with Km values of 30, 12 and 11 μM, respectively. Sulfoconjugated taurolithocholate is also a substrate. Cholate, taurocholate and chenodeoxycholate are not substrates. (Geyer…

The rat orthologue is found in cholinergic neurons of the brain together with the vesicular acetyl choline transporter, VAChT (TC# 2.A.1.2.28), and the high affinity choline transporter, CHT1 (TC#s 2.A.21.8.1 & 2) (Geyer et al. 2008). It is a protease-activated bile acid transporter (Abe et al. 2013). It has also been…

2.A.28.1.9.description: Sodium/bile acid cotransporter (Cell growth-inhibiting gene 29 protein; Na+/bile acid cotransporter; Na+/taurocholate transport protein; NTCP; Solute carrier family 10 member 1). Transports steroids and xenobiotics, including HMG-CoA reductase inhibiitors (statins). This protein is the hepatitis B and D virus receptor (Yan et al. 2012). Specific inhibitors are known and include cyclosporin A (Wu…

2.A.28.2.1.name: The chloroplastic glucosinolate uptake porter, BAT5 [glucosinolates are thioglucosides of amino acid derivatives.
2.A.28.2.1.description: The chloroplastic glucosinolate uptake porter, BAT5 (Gigolashvili et al., 2009) [glucosinolates are thioglucosides of amino acid derivatives. These bitter natural pesticides are present in most plants of the order Brassicales among others].

2.A.28.2.2.name: Chloroplast envelope membrane pyruvate:Na+ symporter, called Bile acid:sodium symporter, protein 2, BASS2.
2.A.28.2.2.description: Chloroplast envelope membrane pyruvate:Na+ symporter, called Bile acid:sodium symporter, protein 2, BASS2 (widely distributed in all land plants tested) (Furumoto et al., 2011).

2.A.28.2.3.name: Chloroplast envelope membrane pyruvate:Na+ symporter, BASS2. (Orthologous to 2.A.28.2.2).
2.A.28.2.3.description: Chloroplast envelope membrane pyruvate:Na+ symporter, BASS2. (Orthologous to 2.A.28.2.2) (Furumoto et al., 2011; Furumoto 2016). The wheat ortholog functions in salt tolerance (Zhao et al. 2016).

2.A.28.2.4.name: Na+:bile acid symporter (AstB).
2.A.28.2.4.description: Na+:bile acid symporter (AstB). The 3-d structure is available (3ZUX).

2.A.28.2.6.name: Probable macrolide resistance porter (very similar to the orthologue in B. brevis).
2.A.28.2.6.description: Probable macrolide resistance porter (very similar to the orthologue in B. brevis) (Margolles et al. 2005).

2.A.28.2.9.name: Sodium bile acid symporter family protein, ASBT, of 307 aas and 10 TMSs.
2.A.28.2.9.description: Sodium bile acid symporter family protein, ASBT, of 307 aas and 10 TMSs. The 3-d structure has been solved (4N7W and 4N7X) (Zhou et al. 2014). This structure has been used to model the yeast Acr3 protein (TC# 2.A.59.1.1) which is in a distinct family of the BART superfamily (Wawrzycka et al. 2016).

2.A.28.3.4.name: Putative Na+-dependent transporter, YfeH (332 aas; 7-10 TMSs)
2.A.28.3.4.description: Putative Na+-dependent transporter, YfeH (332 aas; 7-10 TMSs)

2.A.28.3.7.name: RCh1p transporter (SLC10 family).
2.A.28.3.7.description: RCh1p transporter (SLC10 family). Regulates cytosolic Ca2+ homeostasis (Jiang et al., 2012). Rch1p is part of the low-affinity calcium uptake system (LACS) system and does not functionally interact with Cch1p (Alber et al. 2013). It regulates O-GalNAc glycosylation as well as Ca2+ homeostasis in the secretory pathway: insights into SLC10A7-CDG (congenital disorders of glycosylation) (Durin et al…

2.A.3.1.1.name: Phenylalanine:H+ symporter, PheP of 458 aas and 12 established TMSs.
2.A.3.1.1.description: Phenylalanine:H+ symporter, PheP of 458 aas and 12 established TMSs (Pi and Pittard 1996; Pi et al. 2002). Catalytic residues have been identified (Pi et al. 1993), and interhelical interactions have been proposed (Dogovski et al. 2003).

2.A.3.1.12.name: Aromatic amino acid permease, AroP
2.A.3.1.12.description: Aromatic amino acid permease, AroP (Wehrmann et al., 1995)

2.A.3.1.17.name: D-serine/L-alanine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine uptake porter of 556 aas, CycA.
2.A.3.1.17.description: D-serine/L-alanine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine uptake porter of 556 aas, CycA. Can be mutated to D-cycloserine (a seconary line antitubercular drug) resistance (Chen et al. 2012).

2.A.3.1.18.name: The lysine specific transporter, LysP of 488 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.18.description: The lysine specific transporter, LysP of 488 aas and 12 TMSs (Trip et al. 2013).

2.A.3.1.19.name: Transporter of lysine, histidine and arginine, HisP or LysQ, of 477 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.19.description: Transporter of lysine, histidine and arginine, HisP or LysQ, of 477 aas and 12 TMSs (Trip et al. 2013).

2.A.3.1.2.name: Lysine:H+ symporter.
2.A.3.1.2.description: Lysine:H+ symporter. Forms a stable complex with CadC to allow lysine-dependent adaptation to acidic stress (Rauschmeier et al. 2013). The Salmonella orthologue is 95% identical to the E. coli protein and is highly specific for Lysine. Residues involved in lysine binding have been identified (Kaur et al. 2014).

2.A.3.1.20.name: Serine transporter, SerP2 or YdgB, of 459 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.20.description: Serine transporter, SerP2 or YdgB, of 459 aas and 12 TMSs (Trip et al. 2013). Transports L-alanine (Km = 20 μM), D-alanine (Km = 38 μM), L-serine, D-serine (Km = 356 μM) and glycine (Noens and Lolkema 2015). The encoding gene is adjacent to the one encoding SerP1 (TC# 2.A.3.1.21).

2.A.3.1.21.name: Serine uptake transporter, SerP1, of 259 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.21.description: Serine uptake transporter, SerP1, of 259 aas and 12 TMSs (Trip et al. 2013). L-serine is the highest affinity substrate (Km = 18 μM), but SerP1 also transports L-threonine and L-cysteine (Km values = 20 - 40 μM). Does not transport D-serine (Noens and Lolkema 2015). The encoding gene is adjacent to a paralogue (serP2) with broad specificity for D- and L-small semipolar amino acids and glycine…

2.A.3.1.22.name: Transporter for phenylalainine, tyrosine and tryptophan of 449 aas and 12 TMSs, FywP or YsjA.
2.A.3.1.22.description: Transporter for phenylalainine, tyrosine and tryptophan of 449 aas and 12 TMSs, FywP or YsjA (Trip et al. 2013).

2.A.3.1.23.name: ProY of 457 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.23.description: ProY of 457 aas and 12 TMSs. 96% identical to ProY of Salmonella enterica, a cryptic proline transporter in this organism (Liao et al. 1997).

2.A.3.1.24.name: Asparagine transporter of 499 aas and 12 TMSs, 91% identical to the orthologue in Salmonella enterica (2.A.3.1.8).
2.A.3.1.24.description: Asparagine transporter of 499 aas and 12 TMSs, 91% identical to the orthologue in Salmonella enterica (2.A.3.1.8) (Jennings et al. 1995).

2.A.3.1.25.name: D-serine/D-alanine/glycine transporter, LysP or AnsP, of 453 aas and 11 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.25.description: D-serine/D-alanine/glycine transporter, LysP or AnsP, of 453 aas and 11 TMSs (Xiao et al. 2020).

2.A.3.1.3.name: Aromatic amino acid:H+ symporter, AroP of 457 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.3.description: Aromatic amino acid:H+ symporter, AroP of 457 aas and 12 TMSs (Cosgriff and Pittard 1997). Transports phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan (Honoré and Cole 1990).

2.A.3.1.4.name: γ-aminobutyrate:H+ symporter, GabP.
2.A.3.1.4.description: γ-aminobutyrate:H+ symporter, GabP. It also transports a variety of pyridine carboxylates. Phosphatidylethanolamine is required for its proper topological organization(Zhang et al. 2005). GabP in citrus may also play a role in GABA uptake (Nehela and Killiny 2025).

2.A.3.1.5.name: β-alanine/γ-aminobutyrate/proline/3,4-dehydroproline:H+ symporter, GabP.
2.A.3.1.5.description: β-alanine/γ-aminobutyrate/proline/3,4-dehydroproline:H+ symporter, GabP (Ferson et al. 1996; Zaprasis et al. 2014). Also transports 3-aminobutyrate, 3-aminopropanoate, cis-4-aminobutenoate (Brechtel and King 1998).

2.A.3.1.7.name: D-Serine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine:H+ symporter.
2.A.3.1.7.description: D-Serine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine:H+ symporter (regulated by the small RNA, GcvB; Pulvermacher et al., 2009). The system is active after growth in minimal medium but not after growth in complex medium (Baisa et al. 2013).

2.A.3.1.8.name: Asparagine permease (AnsP) of 497 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.8.description: Asparagine permease (AnsP) of 497 aas and 12 TMSs (Jennings et al. 1995).

2.A.3.10.1.description: High affinity histidine permease (also implicated in Mn2+ efflux; Co2+, Ni2+, Zn2+ and Cu2+ uptake)

2.A.3.10.10.name: Lysine permease of 611 aas and 13 putative TMSs, Lyp1.
2.A.3.10.10.description: Lysine permease of 611 aas and 13 putative TMSs, Lyp1. Extracellular loops affect either the localization or activity of Lyp1. Half of the mutants are located in the extension of extracellular loop 3 or in a predicted alpha-helix in extracellular loop 4 (Van't Klooster et al. 2020). Phosphatidylserine and ergosterol are essential for Lyp1 function, and the transport activity displays a sigmoidal…

2.A.3.10.12.name: Leucine sensor/transcription factor.
2.A.3.10.12.description: Leucine sensor/transcription factor. Mutants hyper- and hyposensitive to inducer (Poulsen et al., 2008) suggest a sensor mechanism involving outward and inward facing conformations.

2.A.3.10.18.description: The aromatic amino acid and leucine permease, ArlP (may be a general amino acid permease for neutral and basic [but not acidic] amino acids)

2.A.3.10.19.name: The high affinity carnitine/polyamine (spermidine > putrescine)/carnitine), low affinity amino acid transporter, AGP2, of 596 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.10.19.description: The high affinity carnitine/polyamine (spermidine > putrescine)/carnitine), low affinity amino acid transporter, AGP2, of 596 aas and 12 TMSs (Aouida et al., 2005; Uemura et al., 2007). Loss of the yeast transporter Agp2 upregulates the pleiotropic drug-resistant pump Pdr5 (TC# 3.A.1.205.1) and confers resistance to the protein synthesis inhibitor, cycloheximide (Manzoor et al. 2024).

2.A.3.10.2.name: General amino acid permease (all L-amino acids and some D-amino acids as well as β-alanine, polyamines and GABA).
2.A.3.10.2.description: General amino acid permease (all L-amino acids and some D-amino acids as well as β-alanine, polyamines and GABA). Systematic mutational analysis of the intracellular regions of yeast Gap1 permease revealed multiple intracellular regions involved in its secretion, transport activity, and down-regulation (Igarashi and Kashiwagi 2010; Merhi et al., 2011). GAP1 is a "transceptor", fuctioning in both…

2.A.3.10.21.name: The basic amino acid (canavanine sensitivity) transporter, Cat1.
2.A.3.10.21.description: The basic amino acid (canavanine sensitivity) transporter, Cat1 (Aspuria and Tamanoi, 2008).

2.A.3.10.22.name: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal proline:H+ symporter, AAP1 (binds and probably transports nonpolar, hydrophobic amino acids).
2.A.3.10.22.description: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal proline:H+ symporter, AAP1 (binds and probably transports nonpolar, hydrophobic amino acids) (Cappellazzo et al., 2008).

2.A.3.10.23.name: Amino acid permease, GAP1.
2.A.3.10.23.description: Amino acid permease, GAP1. Transports Arg, Met, Leu and Phe (Kraidlova et al., 2011).

2.A.3.10.24.description: General amino and permease and transceptor, GAP2. Transports all amino acids including citruline and eight tested toxic amino acid derivatives (Kraidlova et al., 2011).

2.A.3.10.26.name: General amino acid porter, GAP6.
2.A.3.10.26.description: General amino acid porter, GAP6. Transports almost all amino acids tested except arginine and citruline (Kraidlova et al., 2011).

2.A.3.10.28.name: Probable amino-acid permease Meu22 (Meiotic expression up-regulated protein 22)
2.A.3.10.28.description: Probable amino-acid permease Meu22 (Meiotic expression up-regulated protein 22)

2.A.3.10.8.description: Tryptophan permease, Tat2. Regulated via endocytosis by ATP-binding Cassette Transporters, Pdr5 (3.A.1.205.1) and Yor1 (3.A.208.3) as well as a seven-transmembrane protein, RSB1 (9.A.27.1.2) (Johnson et al., 2010). Residues involved in binding and catalysis have been identified (Kanda and Abe 2013). residues and regions important for proper folding and ER retention have been identified (Mochizuki…

2.A.3.11.1.name: The aspartate uptake permease, YveA
2.A.3.11.1.description: The aspartate uptake permease, YveA (also transports L-aspartate hydroxamate and glutamate, and possibly asparagine and glutamine; Lorca et al., 2003)

2.A.3.12.1.name: The plasma membrane polyamine (putrescine, spermidine):H+ uptake symporter, LmPOT1 (inhibited by pentamidine and protonophores).
2.A.3.12.1.description: The plasma membrane polyamine (putrescine, spermidine):H+ uptake symporter, LmPOT1 (inhibited by pentamidine and protonophores) (Hasne and Ullmann, 2005; Zhang et al. 2022).

2.A.3.12.3.name: Plasma membrane polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 490 aas, RMV1.
2.A.3.12.3.description: Plasma membrane polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 490 aas, RMV1. Also called PUT3 and LAT1. Mutations give rise to partial paraquot (a toxic common herbicide that generates superoxide and reactive oxygen species (ROS)) (Fujita and Shinozaki 2014).

2.A.3.12.4.name: Golgi polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 478 aas, LAT4.
2.A.3.12.4.description: Golgi polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 478 aas, LAT4. Also called PUT2 and PAR1. Mutations give rise to paraquot resistance (Par1) both in A. thaliana and in rice. Probably present in the chloroplast membrane (Fujita and Shinozaki 2014).

2.A.3.12.5.name: Spermidine-preferring polyamine transporter, PUT1 of 531 aas.
2.A.3.12.5.description: Spermidine-preferring polyamine transporter, PUT1 of 531 aas. Also transports paraquot (Fujita and Shinozaki 2014).

2.A.3.13.1.name: The hydrophobic amino acid efflux transporter, YjeH.
2.A.3.13.1.description: The hydrophobic amino acid efflux transporter, YjeH (exports L-methionine and other neutral, hydrophobic amino acids such as Leu, Ile and Val; R. Figge, personal communication; Liu et al. 2015).

2.A.3.13.2.name: The Ceftriaxone resistance porter, YjeH.
2.A.3.13.2.description: The Ceftriaxone resistance porter, YjeH (Hu et al. 2007).

2.A.3.13.3.name: L-Leucine uptake porter, YjeH, of 426 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.13.3.description: L-Leucine uptake porter, YjeH, of 426 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs (Deutschbauer et al. 2011).

2.A.3.14.3.name: APC protein with 610 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.14.3.description: APC protein with 610 aas and 12 TMSs. 77% identical to an orthologue in Weissella viridescens that serves as a receptor or uptake transporter for the two peptide bacteriocin, plantaricin JK (1.C.30.1.1) (Oppegård et al. 2016; Ekblad et al. 2017).
