2.A.3.2.1.description: Putrescine:ornithine antiporter for putrescine export; putrescine:H+ symporter for uptake (Igarashi and Kashiwagi 1996). Modeling tools have been used to gain information about the structures and functions of CadB and PotE in E. coli (Tomitori et al., 2012).

2.A.3.2.2.description: Cadaverine:lysine antiporter [Catalyzes cadaverine uptake via H+ symport (Km=21μM) and cadaverine export (Km=300 μM) via cadaverine:lysine antiport.] (Soksawatmaekhin et al., 2004). Modeling tools have been used to gain information about the structures and functions of CadB and PotE in E. coli (Tomitori et al., 2012).

2.A.3.2.5.name: Homodimeric electrogenic arginine (Km=80μM):agmatine antiporter, AdiC, involved in extreme acid resistance.
2.A.3.2.5.description: Homodimeric electrogenic arginine (Km=80μM):agmatine antiporter, AdiC, involved in extreme acid resistance (Fang et al., 2007; Gong et al., 2003; Iyer et al., 2003). A projection structure at 6.5 Å resolution has been published (Casagrande et al., 2008), and the 3.2 Å resolution X-ray structure was determined by Fang et al., 2009 and Gao et al., 2009. 2.A.3.3.10.description: Cationic amino acid transporter 3 (CAT-3) (CAT3) (Cationic amino acid transporter y+) (Solute carrier family 7 member 3). Mutations in CAT3 are potential causes of childhood epilepsy (Sourbron et al. 2021).

2.A.3.3.19.name: Histamine uptake transporter; involved in the utilization of histamine as a nitrogen source.
2.A.3.3.19.description: Histamine uptake transporter; involved in the utilization of histamine as a nitrogen source. In an operon with two histamine catabilic enzymes, and all are induced by hsitamine (Johnson et al. 2008).

2.A.3.3.2.description: Low affinity basic amino acid transporter (CAT2) (T-cell early activation protein (TEA)) (transports arginine, lysine and ornithine; Na+-independent) (Habermeier et al., 2003)

2.A.3.3.24.description: Plastidic cationic amino acid transporter, CAT, of 582 aas and 14 TMSs. Exports phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan our of chloroplasts into the cytoplasm (Widhalm et al. 2015).

2.A.3.3.3.name: Amino acid transporter, AAT1 or CAT1, of 594 aas and 14 TMSs.
2.A.3.3.3.description: Amino acid transporter, AAT1 or CAT1, of 594 aas and 14 TMSs. It is a high-affinity permease involved in the transport of the cationic amino acids (e.g., arginine, lysine, histidine, citrulline, valine, and glutamate). It transports mostly basic amino acids, and, to a lesser extent, neutral and acidic amino acids. It probably functions as a proton symporter. It transports histidine with a Km of…

2.A.3.3.4.name: The amino acid transporter, CAT6.
2.A.3.3.4.description: The amino acid transporter, CAT6. Mediates electrogenic transport of large neutral and cationic amino acids in preference to other amino acids. Present in lateral root primordia, flowers and seeds (Hammes et al., 2006)

2.A.3.3.5.name: The brain L-cationic (Arg, Lys, Orn, 2,4-diamino-n-butyrate) transporter, CAT3 (capacity of trans-stimulation by internal Arg)
2.A.3.3.5.description: The brain L-cationic (Arg, Lys, Orn, 2,4-diamino-n-butyrate) transporter, CAT3 (capacity of trans-stimulation by internal Arg) (Ito and Groudine, 1997)

2.A.3.3.8.name: Low affinity cationic amino acid transporter 2 (CAT-2) (CAT2) (Solute carrier family 7 member 2).
2.A.3.3.8.description: Low affinity cationic amino acid transporter 2 (CAT-2) (CAT2) (Solute carrier family 7 member 2) (Closs 1996). Elevated SLC7A2 expression is associated with an abnormal neuroinflammatory response and nitrosative stress in Huntington's disease (Gaudet et al. 2024).

2.A.3.3.9.name: High affinity cationic amino acid transporter 1 (CAT-1) (CAT1, CTR1) (ERR), (SLC7a1) (System Y+ basic amino acid transporter).
2.A.3.3.9.description: High affinity cationic amino acid transporter 1 (CAT-1) (CAT1, CTR1) (Ecotropic retroviral leukemia receptor homologue) (ERR), (SLC7a1) (System Y+ basic amino acid transporter) (Closs 1996). It takes up Arginine, Lysine and Ornithine. Its gene shows increased expression in various cancers such as colorectal cancer (CRC) (Okita et al. 2020). Treatment of a blood-brain barrier (BBB) mimetic with…

2.A.3.4.1.name: The single high affinity plasma membrane choline transporter of 563 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.4.1.description: The single high affinity plasma membrane choline transporter of 563 aas and 12 TMSs. Expression of the CTR/HNM1 gene in wild-type cells is regulated by phospholipid precursors, inositol and choline, but no such effect is seen in cells bearing mutations in the phospholipid regulatory genes INO2, INO4 and OPI1. There is no regulation by INO2 and OPI1 in the absence of a conserved decamer motif…

2.A.3.4.3.name: γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) permease, Uga4 (also transports the polyamine, putrescine).
2.A.3.4.3.description: γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) permease, Uga4 (also transports the polyamine, putrescine) (Uemura et al., 2007; Kashiwagi and Igarashi 2011).

2.A.3.4.6.name: The thiamine (vitamin B1) transporter, Thi9 (SPAC9.10).
2.A.3.4.6.description: The thiamine (vitamin B1) transporter, Thi9 (SPAC9.10). Uptake is inhibited by pyrithiamine, oxythiamine, amprolium, and the thiazole part of thiamine indicating that these compounds are substrates of Thi9 (Vogl et al., 2008).

2.A.3.4.8.name: SwnT of 501 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.3.4.8.description: SwnT of 501 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Slafractonia leguminicola infects red clover and other legumes, causing black patch disease. This fungus produces two mycotoxins, slaframine and swainsonine, that are toxic to livestock grazing on clover hay or pasture infested with S. leguminicola. Swainsonine toxicosis causes locoism, while slaframine causes slobbers syndrome. SwnT may…

2.A.3.6.1.description: Putative cationic amino acid permease of 736 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.

2.A.3.6.3.name: ApcT, a proton coupled broad specificity amino acid transporter.
2.A.3.6.3.description: ApcT, a proton coupled broad specificity amino acid transporter. 3-d structure available at 2.3Å resolution (3GIA_A; Shaffer et al., 2009).

2.A.3.7.1.name: Glutamate:γ-aminobutyrate antiporter of 477 aas and 12 TMSs, GadC.
2.A.3.7.1.description: Glutamate:γ-aminobutyrate antiporter of 477 aas and 12 TMSs, GadC. Expression of gadCB in L. lactis in the presence of chloride is increased when the culture pH decreases to low levels, while glutamate stimulated gadCB expression (Sanders et al. 1998). These genes encode a glutamate-dependent acid resistance mechanism that is optimally active when needed for acid neutralization.

2.A.3.7.3.name: Glutamate:GABA antiporter, GadC (YcaM).
2.A.3.7.3.description: Glutamate:GABA antiporter, GadC (YcaM). GadC, transports GABA/Glu only under acidic conditions, with no detectable activity at pH values higher than 6.5 (Ma et al., 2012). Ma et al. (2012) determined the crystal structure of GadC at 3.1 Å resolution under basic conditions. GadC, comprising 12 TMSs, exists in a closed state, with its carboxy-terminal domain serving as a plug to block an otherwise…

2.A.3.7.6.name: Aspartate/Glutamate transporter of 488 aas and 12 TMSs, AcaP.
2.A.3.7.6.description: Aspartate/Glutamate transporter of 488 aas and 12 TMSs, AcaP (Trip et al. 2013).

2.A.3.7.7.description: Putriscine/agmatine transporter of 466 aas and 12 TMSs, AguD or YrfD (Trip et al. 2013).

2.A.3.8.1.name: L-type neutral amino acid transporter, LAT1 (Na+-independent).
2.A.3.8.1.description: L-type neutral amino acid transporter, LAT1 (Na+-independent) (prefers amino acids with branched or aromatic side chains: Phe, Ile, Leu, Val, Trp, His; catalyzes obligatory exchange with μM affinities on the outside and mM affinities on the inside [1000x difference]). Both LAT1 and LAT2 (2.A.3.8.6) catalyze uptake of S-nitroso-L-cysteine. These and other LAT family members are specifically…

2.A.3.8.10.description: Aromatic amino acid exchanger, AAT-9 (Veljkovic et al., 2004b)

2.A.3.8.11.name: The aromatic-preferring amino acid transporter (ArpAT or Slc7a15).
2.A.3.8.11.description: The aromatic-preferring amino acid transporter (ArpAT or Slc7a15). Functions with rBAT or 4F2hc (8.A.9) and transports preferentially tyr and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA), but also ala, glu, ser, cys and arg by a Na+-independent mechanism (present in mouse, rat, dog and chicken, but silenced in humans and chimps)(Fernández et al., 2005; Sato et al., 2005). It is expressed in the CNS…

2.A.3.8.12.name: The Ser/Thr exchange transporter (SteT) (also transports aromatic amino acids with lower efficiency).
2.A.3.8.12.description: The Ser/Thr exchange transporter (SteT) (also transports aromatic amino acids with lower efficiency) (Reig et al., 2007). The substrate-bound state of SteT shows increased conformational flexibility and kinetic stability, enabling transport of substrate across the cell membrane (Bippes et al. 2009). TMS8 sculpts the substrate-binding site and undergoes conformational changes during the transport…

2.A.3.8.13.name: The Asc-type small neutral D- and L-amino acid:H+ symport transporter-1, Asc-1 (Slc7a10).
2.A.3.8.13.description: The Asc-type small neutral D- and L-amino acid:H+ symport transporter-1, Asc-1 (Slc7a10). Also transports amino acid related compounds. Heterodimeric; associates with 4F2hc (TC# 8.A.9.2.1) Most highly expressed in brain and lung, but to a lesser degree in placenta and small intestine. (Fukasawa et al., 2000)

2.A.3.8.14.name: The Asc-type small neutral L-amino acid:H+ symport transporter-2 (Asc-2).
2.A.3.8.14.description: The Asc-type small neutral L-amino acid:H+ symport transporter-2 (Asc-2). Does not associate with 4F2hc or rBAT, but probably associates with some comparable heavy chain. Doesn't transport some substrates of Asc-1 such as α-aminoisobutyric acid and β-alanine (Chairoungdua et al., 2001)

2.A.3.8.15.name: The b0,+ amino acid transporter associated with the cystinuria-related type II membrane glycoprotein, BAT1 which forms a heterodimer with rBAT.
2.A.3.8.15.description: The b0,+ amino acid (cystine) transporter associated with the cystinuria-related type II membrane glycoprotein, BAT1 which forms a heterodimer with rBAT (TC# 8.A.9.1.1). Present in the apical membrane of renal proximal tubules (Chairoungdua et al., 1999)

2.A.3.8.17.name: Putative fructoselysine transporter FrlA.
2.A.3.8.17.description: Putative fructoselysine transporter FrlA (Wiame and Van Schaftingen 2004). Also transports psicoselysine.

2.A.3.8.18.name: Cystine/glutamate antiporter (Amino acid transport system xCT; Asc1; CD98hc) (Solute carrier family 7 member 11; SLC7A11).
2.A.3.8.18.description: Cystine/glutamate antiporter (Amino acid transport system xCT; Asc1; CD98hc) (Calcium channel blocker resistance protein CCBR1) (Solute carrier family 7 member 11; SLC7A11). 2.A.3.8.2.name: L-type neutral amino acid transporter, ASUR4 (Na+-independent) of 507 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.8.2.description: L-type neutral amino acid transporter, ASUR4 (Na+-independent) of 507 aas and 12 TMSs. Pregabalin (PGB), a drug for the treatment of epilepsy, neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and generalized anxiety disorder, may be transported by L-type transporters (Su et al. 2005).

2.A.3.8.20.name: Large neutral amino acids transporter small subunit 2 (L-type amino acid transporter 2) (hLAT2) (Solute carrier family 7 member 8).
2.A.3.8.20.description: Large neutral amino acids transporter small subunit 2 (L-type amino acid transporter 2) (hLAT2) (Solute carrier family 7 member 8). Certain detergents stabilize and allow purification of the 4F2hc-LAT2 complex, allowing the measurement of substrate binding. In addition, an improved 3D map could be obtained (Meury et al. 2014). Transports many amino acids including thyroid hormones 3',3-T2 and T3…

2.A.3.8.21.description: Asc-type amino acid transporter 1 (Asc-1) (Solute carrier family 7 member 10)

2.A.3.8.9.description: Heteromeric amino acid transporter #1 (transports most neutral aas with highest rates for Ala and Ser (Km≈100 μM)). They function by obligatory aa:aa exchange (Veljkovic et al., 2004b).

2.A.35.1.3.description: The putative tyrosine permease, TyrT, of 472 aas and 12 TMSs. Also called NhaC2 (Panina et al., 2003; Rodionov et al. 2004).

2.A.35.1.4.name: The arginine/ornithine antiporter ArcD
2.A.35.1.4.description: The arginine/ornithine antiporter ArcD (Wimmer et al. 2008)

2.A.35.1.5.name: The putative methionine porter, MetT.
2.A.35.1.5.description: The putative methionine porter, MetT. Regulated by S-adenosylmethionine-dependent repressor MetJ (Rodionov et al. 2011).

2.A.35.1.6.name: YheL; TyrT, putative tyrosine uptake cation symporter; NhaC, putative Na+/H+ antiporter (Sodium/hydrogen antiporter).
2.A.35.1.6.description: YheL; TyrT, putative tyrosine uptake cation symporter; NhaC, putative Na+/H+ antiporter (Sodium/hydrogen antiporter) (Rodionov et al. 2004).

2.A.35.1.8.name: Predicted methionine uptaie cation symporter, MetT, of 433 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.35.1.8.description: Predicted methionine uptaie cation symporter, MetT, of 433 aas and 12 TMSs (Rodionov et al. 2004).

2.A.35.1.9.name: Predicted methioine:cation symporter of 459 aas and 12 TMSs, MetT.
2.A.35.1.9.description: Predicted methioine:cation symporter of 459 aas and 12 TMSs, MetT (Rodionov et al. 2004). Also called NhaC.

2.A.35.2.1.name: Na+/H+ antiporter of the NhaC family
2.A.35.2.1.description: Na+/H+ antiporter of the NhaC family

2.A.35.2.2.name: Putative lysine transporter, LysW.
2.A.35.2.2.description: Putative lysine transporter, LysW. Regulated by Lysine riboswitch (Rodionov et al. 2003)

2.A.35.2.3.name: The NhaC Na+:H+ antiporter, G1-NhaC (functions in Na+ extrusion at lower pH values and in pH homeostasis at pH 10 under Na+-limiting conditions).
2.A.35.2.3.description: The NhaC Na+:H+ antiporter, G1-NhaC (functions in Na+ extrusion at lower pH values and in pH homeostasis at pH 10 under Na+-limiting conditions) (Liew et al., 2007).

2.A.36.1.1.name: Na+:H+ antiporter 1 (Nhe-1) (Regulated by Daxx (O35613)).
2.A.36.1.1.description: Na+:H+ antiporter 1 (Nhe-1) (Regulated by Daxx (O35613)). An integral membrane protein that regulates intracellular pH and has a large N-terminal membrane domain of 12 transmembrane segments and an intracellular C-terminal regulatory domain (Reddy et al., 2008). The dimer catalyzes antiport with 2Na+/2H+ stoichiometry (Fuster et al., 2008). Nedd4-1 and β-arrestin-1 are key regulators of Na+/H+…

2.A.36.1.11.name: The Na+:H+ Exchanger, NHE1, is developmentally regulated and necessary for cell polarity.
2.A.36.1.11.description: The Na+:H+ Exchanger, NHE1, is developmentally regulated and necessary for cell polarity (Patel and Barber, 2005).

2.A.36.1.12.name: Na+:H+ antiporter, NHX1; (vacuolar/endosomal Na+ tolerance protein).
2.A.36.1.12.description: Na+:H+ antiporter, NHX1; (vacuolar/endosomal Na+ tolerance protein). Plays roles in ion homeostasis and vesicle trafficing (Mukherjee et al. 2006). The structures and functions of these NHX homologues have been reviewed (Dutta and Fliegel 2018). K+ influx/efflux regulates mitochondrial energetics while maintaining mitochondrial ionic balance and volume homeostasis (Malas et al. 2022).

2.A.36.1.13.name: Na+ /H+ exchanger-1 (NHE1).
2.A.36.1.13.description: Na+ /H+ exchanger-1 (NHE1). Stoichiometry = 1:1. TMS VI of NHE1 is a discontinuous pore-lining helix with residues Asn(227), Ile(233), and Leu(243) lining the translocation pore (Tzeng et al., 2010). (orthologous to NHE1 of rat, TC# 2.A.36.1.1). Both Pro167 and Pro168 in TMS IV are required for normal NHE activity (Slepkov et al. 2004). NHE1 regulates internal pH in human monocytes and is…

2.A.36.1.14.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 6 (Na+/H+ exchanger 6) (NHE-6) (Solute carrier family 9 member 6; SLC9A6).
2.A.36.1.14.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 6 (Na+/H+ exchanger 6) (NHE-6) (Solute carrier family 9 member 6; SLC9A6). This Na+/H+ exchanger is encoded by an X-linked gene that is widely expressed and especially abundant in brain, heart and skeletal muscle where it is implicated in endosomal pH homeostasis and trafficking as well as maintenance of cell polarity. Several mutations in the coding region of NHE6 are…

2.A.36.1.15.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 3 (Na+/H+ exchanger 3) (NHE-3) of 834 aas and 12 TMSs (Solute carrier family 9 member 3).
2.A.36.1.15.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 3 (Na+/H+ exchanger 3) (NHE-3) of 834 aas and 12 TMSs (Solute carrier family 9 member 3) (Dominguez Rieg et al. 2016). A missense mutation in SLC26A3 is associated with human male subfertility and impaired activation of CFTR (Wedenoja et al. 2017). SLC9A3 affects vas deferens development (Wu et al. 2019). SLC9A3 deficiency-mediated micturition dysfunction is caused by…

2.A.36.1.16.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 5 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 5) (NHE-5) (Solute carrier family 9 member 5)
2.A.36.1.16.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 5 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 5) (NHE-5) (Solute carrier family 9 member 5)

2.A.36.1.17.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2 (Na+/H+ exchanger 2) (NHE-2 or NHE2) (Solute carrier family 9 member 2).
2.A.36.1.17.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2 (Na+/H+ exchanger 2) (NHE-2 or NHE2) (Solute carrier family 9 member 2). Mediates butyrate-dependent Na+ absorption (Rajendran et al. 2015).

2.A.36.1.18.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 4) (NHE-4) (Solute carrier family 9 member 4).
2.A.36.1.18.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 4) (NHE-4) (Solute carrier family 9 member 4). NHE4 had previously been suggested to play a critical role in renal ammonia metabolism through its role in thick ascending limb (TAL) ammonia transport. Lee et al. 2025 showed that its deletion does not alter renal ammonia handling and that neither the mouse nor human kidney expresses NHE4 in the TAL.

2.A.36.1.19.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 9 (Na+/H+ exchanger 9) (NHE-9; NHE9) (Solute carrier family 9 member 9, SLC9A9) of 645 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.36.1.19.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 9 (Na+/H+ exchanger 9) (NHE-9; NHE9) (Solute carrier family 9 member 9, SLC9A9) of 645 aas and 12 TMSs. It may act in electroneutral exchange of protons for Na+ across membranes and is involved in the effusion of Golgi luminal H+ in exchange for cytosolic cations. It is also involved in organellar ion homeostasis by contributing to the maintenance of the unique acidic pH…

2.A.36.1.2.name: N+:H+ antiporter 3 (NHE-3 or NHE3).
2.A.36.1.2.description: N+:H+ antiporter 3 (NHE-3 or NHE3). Regulated by Na+/H+ exchange regulatory cofactors (NHERF; O14745; TC #8.A.24.1.1) (Seidler et al., 2009). Cyclic AMP-mediated endocytosis of intestinal epithelial NHE3 requires binding to synaptotagmin 1 (Musch et al., 2010). Decreased activity is responsible for congenital Na+ diarrhea in the human brush boarder (Janecke et al. 2015). Reduced functional…

2.A.36.1.20.name: Endomembrane (Golgi) K+, Na+/H+ exchanger 5, NHX5, of 521 aas and 11 TMSs.
2.A.36.1.20.description: Endomembrane (Golgi) K+, Na+/H+ exchanger 5, NHX5, of 521 aas and 11 TMSs. Three acidic residues are critical for transport activity as well as seedling growth, regulation of protein transport into vesicles and ionic homeostasis (Qiu 2016). NHX6 is 80% identical to NHX5 (535 aas and 11 TMSs) and serves the same function. They are all located in Golgi, trans-Golgi network (TGN), endoplasmic…

2.A.36.1.22.name: Na+/H+ exchanger, beta-like, NHE, of 917 aas and 11 putative TMSs.
2.A.36.1.22.description: Na+/H+ exchanger, beta-like, NHE, of 917 aas and 11 putative TMSs. Involved in pH homeostasis (Li et al. 2019).
2.A.36.1.22.proteins: NHE of Penaeus vannamei (Pacific white shrimp)

2.A.36.1.23.name: Sodium/proton exchanger of 529 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.
2.A.36.1.23.description: Sodium/proton exchanger of 529 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs. The six NHXs in grape have been bioinformatically characterized (Ayadi et al. 2019). This protein is 81% identical to the exchanger with TC# 2.A.36.1.5.

2.A.36.1.24.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2a NHE2a, of 818 aas and 13 TMSs.
2.A.36.1.24.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2a NHE2a, of 818 aas and 13 TMSs. Expression of several NHE genes were regulated bylow, isotonic or high salinity treatments, indicating an involvements in salinity and osmotic regulation in teleosts (Liu et al. 2019).

2.A.36.1.3.name: Na+/K+:H+ antiporter, Nhe-7, present in the Golgi apparatus and endosomes.
2.A.36.1.3.description: Na+/K+:H+ antiporter, Nhe-7, present in the Golgi apparatus and endosomes. There are four isoforms, NHE6-9. They regulate the luminal pH as well as intracellular trafficking, and function in cell polarity development (Ohgaki et al., 2011). Nhe-6 (Nhe6) is associated with X-linked intellectural disability and autism when processing and trafficking is impaired (Ilie et al. 2013).

2.A.36.1.4.name: Cl--dependent Na+:H+ antiporter (Nhe) (residues 1-375 are identical to Nhe-1 [TC #2.A.36.1.1]).
2.A.36.1.4.description: Cl--dependent Na+:H+ antiporter (Nhe) (residues 1-375 are identical to Nhe-1 [TC #2.A.36.1.1]).

2.A.36.1.5.name: Na+/K+:H+ antiporter, NHX2, of531 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.36.1.5.description: Na+/K+:H+ antiporter, NHX2, of531 aas and 12 TMSs. It is involved in salt tolerance.

2.A.36.1.6.name: Zebrafish Na+:H+ antiporter NheC (most similar to TC# 2.A.36.1.2, 48% identical)
2.A.36.1.6.description: Zebrafish Na+:H+ antiporter NheC (Yan et al., 2007) (most similar to TC# 2.A.36.1.2, 48% identical)

2.A.36.1.7.name: The basolateral intestinal Na+/H+ antiporter PBO-4
2.A.36.1.7.description: The basolateral intestinal Na+/H+ antiporter PBO-4 (Beg et al., 2008)

2.A.36.1.9.name: Human Na+/H+ Exchanger, NHE-8 or SLC9A8.
2.A.36.1.9.description: Human Na+/H+ Exchanger, NHE-8 or SLC9A8. Functions in intracellular pH homeostasis, cell volume regulation, and electroneutral NaCl absorption in epithelia. It attenuates Ca2+ influx in the proximal tubular epithelium (Wiebe et al. 2019).

2.A.36.2.2.name: The electroneutral Na+/Li+:H+ antiporter, Nha2.
2.A.36.2.2.description: The electroneutral Na+/Li+:H+ antiporter, Nha2. Catalyzes Na+:Li+ antiport; contributes to salt homeostasis. It correlates with heritable hypertension (Xiang et al., 2007) and is critical for insulin secretion (Deisl et al. 2013). Like electrogenic Na+/H+ exchangers, it has two conserved aspartyl residues in the Na+ binding site but seems to be electroneutral (Uzdavinys et al. 2017). The…

2.A.36.2.3.name: solute carrier family 9, subfamily B, SLC9B. (NHA1, cation proton antiporter 1).
2.A.36.2.3.description: solute carrier family 9, subfamily B, SLC9B. (NHA1, cation proton antiporter 1). The SLC9 gene family encodes Na+/H+ exchangers (NHEs), a group of membrane transport proteins critically involved in the regulation of cytoplasmic and organellar pH, cell volume, as well as systemic acid-base and volume homeostasis (Anderegg et al. 2022). NHEs of the SLC9A subfamily (NHE 1-9) are well-known for their…

2.A.36.3.1.name: Putative antiporter of 549 aas (function unknown).
2.A.36.3.1.description: Putative antiporter of 549 aas (function unknown) (Verkhovskaya et al. 2001).

2.A.36.3.2.name: Na+, K+, Li+, Rb+:H+ antiporter, YvgP
2.A.36.3.2.description: Na+, K+, Li+, Rb+:H+ antiporter, YvgP

2.A.36.4.1.name: [Na+ or K+]:H+ antiporter Nha1 of 985 aas and 13 or 14 predicted TMSs, all at the N-terminus of the protein in a possible 6 +1 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.36.4.1.description: [Na+ or K+]:H+ antiporter Nha1 of 985 aas and 13 or 14 predicted TMSs, all at the N-terminus of the protein in a possible 6 +1 + 6 TMS arrangement. The ceontral TMS is much lower in hydrophobicity than the other TMSs. All TMSs are in residues 1 - 430 while the rest of the protein is strongly hydrophilic.

2.A.36.4.2.name: Na+:H+ antiporter, Nha2 or Sod2-22.
2.A.36.4.2.description: Na+:H+ antiporter, Nha2 or Sod2-22. Exports Na+ and Li+ but not K+. Three residues, T141 in TMS 4, A179 in TMS 5 and V375 in TMS 11, determine the cation selectivity (Kinclova-Zimmermannova et al. 2015).

2.A.36.4.3.name: Na+:H+ antiporter, Nha1 or Sod2 of 468 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.
2.A.36.4.3.description: Na+:H+ antiporter, Nha1 or Sod2 of 468 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs. It provides salt tolerance by removing sodium and lithium ions in exchange for protons, and TMS 4 plays an important role (Ullah et al. 2013). The Asp266/Asp267 pair are critical for Sod2 function (Fliegel 2005). Residues within TMS 11 also play important roles in transport, suggesting that this TMS forms part of the ion translocation…

2.A.36.4.4.name: The K+, Rb+ and other alkali metal cation efflux porter, Cnh1.
2.A.36.4.4.description: The K+, Rb+ and other alkali metal cation efflux porter, Cnh1 (Kinclova-Zimmermannova and Sychrova, 2007). Transports Na+, K+, Li+ and Rb+ in several Candida species. Confers tolerance to high salt concentrations (Krauke and Sychrova 2008).

2.A.36.5.1.name: Low-affinity Na+ (K+, Li+ or Cs+):H+ antiporter, Nhx1.
2.A.36.5.1.description: Low-affinity Na+ (K+, Li+ or Cs+):H+ antiporter, Nhx1. It is up-regluated in response to high salt stress conditions (Yang et al. 2018). It has the same general architecture as CHX17 of A. thaliana (TC# 2.A.37.4.2) (Sze and Chanroj 2018). Four NHX proteins (1-4) have been identified in Argania spinosa L (Karim et al. 2020). Structural features of Grapevine NHX antiporters have been determined…

2.A.36.5.2.name: Vacuolar Na+/H+ antiporter, NHX1.
2.A.36.5.2.description: Vacuolar Na+/H+ antiporter, NHX1. A class-I type NHX. Confers NaCl tolerance and therefore pumps Na+ from the cytosol to the vacuole (Jha et al., 2011).

2.A.36.5.3.name: Vacuolar Na+/H+ exchanger, DgNHX1 or NHX1, of 510 aas and 13 putative (but possibly 9 actual) TMSs.
2.A.36.5.3.description: Vacuolar Na+/H+ exchanger, DgNHX1 or NHX1, of 510 aas and 13 putative (but possibly 9 actual) TMSs. Involved in adaptation to salt stress conditions and expressed under these same conditions (Liu et al. 2013).
2.A.36.5.3.proteins: NHX1 of Chrysanthemum morifolium (Florist's daisy) (Dendranthema grandiflorum)

2.A.36.5.4.name: Vacuorlar Na+/H+ exchanger, Nhx1 of 542 aas and 13 TMSs.
2.A.36.5.4.description: Vacuorlar Na+/H+ exchanger, Nhx1 of 542 aas and 13 TMSs. Involved in salt tolerance (Mishra et al. 2014).

2.A.36.5.5.name: Na+:H+ antiporter, Nhx1 of 470 aas and 9 TMSs.
2.A.36.5.5.description: Na+:H+ antiporter, Nhx1 of 470 aas and 9 TMSs. NHX1 can confer a high level of salinity tolerance when overexpressed in Brassica juncea. Verma et al. 2007 reported its functional characterization. Overexpression conferred a high level of salinity tolerance in rice. Transgenic rice plants overexpressing PgNHX1 developed more extensive root systems and completed their life cycle by setting flowers…
2.A.36.5.5.proteins: Nhx1 of Pennisetum americanum (Pearl millet) (Pennisetum glaucum)

2.A.36.5.6.name: Na+/Li+/H+ exchanger of 545 aas and 12 TMSs, NHX3.
2.A.36.5.6.description: Na+/Li+/H+ exchanger of 545 aas and 12 TMSs, NHX3. It is localized to the tonoplast membrane where it increases salt tolerance and reduces Li+ toxicity. TMS 11 is important in Li+ and Na+ transport (Pan et al. 2017).

2.A.36.5.8.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4, NHX4, of 529 aas and 8 TMSs.
2.A.36.5.8.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4, NHX4, of 529 aas and 8 TMSs. This endosomal protein is critical for salt tolerance in cotton (Ma et al. 2020). It probably acts as a low affinity electroneutral exchanger of protons for cations such as Na+ or K+ across membranes, but may also exchange Li+ and Cs+ with lower affinities.

2.A.36.5.9.name: The sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2, NHX2, of 546 aas and 13 TMSs.
2.A.36.5.9.description: The sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2, NHX2, of 546 aas and 13 TMSs. It catalyzes the low affinity electroneutral exchange of protons for cations such as Na+ or K+ across membranes, and may also exchange Li+ and Cs+ with a lower affinity. It is involved in vacuolar ion compartmentalization necessary for cell volume regulation and cytoplasmic Na+ detoxification (Yokoi et al. 2002). Its ortholog has also…

2.A.36.6.1.name: Putative Na+:H+ antiporter, Nhe2
2.A.36.6.1.proteins: The AF0846 gene (Nhe2) of Archaeoglobus fulgidus

2.A.36.6.10.name: Na+/H+ antiporter of 403 aas and 11 predicted TMSs, NhaH.
2.A.36.6.10.description: Na+/H+ antiporter of 403 aas and 11 predicted TMSs, NhaH. Exchanges Na+ or Li+ but not K+ for H+ (Zou et al. 2008). Confers Na+ and Li+ tolerance.

2.A.36.6.11.name: Na+/H+ antiporter, NhaP2 (YcgO; CvrA) of 578 aas and 13 TMSs.
2.A.36.6.11.description: Na+/H+ antiporter, NhaP2 (YcgO; CvrA) of 578 aas and 13 TMSs. Involved in growth at low osmolarity, intracellular K+ maintenance, and volume regulation (Verkhovskaya et al. 2001). Hyposaline xonsiriona induces oxidative stress and disrupts gut microbiome stability in C. notata, thereby triggering complex physiological and molecular responses (Kim et al. 2025).

2.A.36.6.2.name: Na+ (Li+):H+ antiporter NhaG.
2.A.36.6.2.description: Na+ (Li+):H+ antiporter NhaG (Gouda et al. 2001). Several very similar antiporters have been isolated from uncultured bacteria from a lake in China (Wang et al. 2013).

2.A.36.6.3.name: K+:H+ antiporter, KhaP2 (NhaP2).
2.A.36.6.3.description: K+:H+ antiporter, KhaP2 (NhaP2). Participates in volume control under low osmorality conditions (Radchenko et al., 2006; Resch et al., 2010)

2.A.36.6.4.name: The K+(NH4+):H+ antiporter, NhaP (confers alkali resistance for alkaline pH homeostasis)
2.A.36.6.4.description: The K+(NH4+):H+ antiporter, NhaP (confers alkali resistance for alkaline pH homeostasis) (Wei et al., 2007)

2.A.36.6.5.name: K+:H+ antiporter NhaP2. (84% identical to 2.A.36.6.3).
2.A.36.6.5.description: K+:H+ antiporter NhaP2 (catalyzes K+:H+ and Na+:H+ exchange; Resch et al., 2010). (84% identical to 2.A.36.6.3). A cation binding pocket in the middle of the membrane and a pathway leading to it have been identified (Mourin et al. 2018). There are 3 NhaP types in Vibrio cholerae (Vc-NhaP1, 2, and 3). They are critical for maintenance of K+ homeostasis in the cytoplasm, and all 3 are required for…

2.A.36.6.6.name: Na+/H+ antiporter 1 (MjNhaP1).
2.A.36.6.6.description: Na+/H+ antiporter 1 (MjNhaP1). NhaP1 is a dimer with 13 TMSs per monomer as revealed by electron crystalography of 2-d crystals (Goswami et al. 2011). This structure is contrasted with that of the distantly related bacterial NhaA; these two structures are quite different in detail, but similar within the 6 TMS repeat unit. Asp234/235 of helix VIII are involved in ligand-binding, and helix X plays…

2.A.36.6.8.name: Na+/H+ antiporter of 424 aas, NhaP, that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons.
2.A.36.6.8.description: Na+/H+ antiporter of 424 aas, NhaP, that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons. Has weak (if any) Li+/H+ antiport activity (Kuroda et al. 2004).

2.A.36.6.9.name: Na+/H+ antiporter, NhaP, of 443 aas.
2.A.36.6.9.description: Na+/H+ antiporter, NhaP, of 443 aas. Several 3-d structures are known (Wöhlert et al. 2014). The ion is coordinated by three acidic side chains, a water molecule, a serine and a main-chain carbonyl in an unwound stretch of TMS 5 at the deepest point of a negatively charged cytoplasmic funnel. A second narrow polar channel may facilitate proton uptake from the cytoplasm. Transport activity is…

2.A.36.7.1.name: ApNhaP: a Na+:H+ antiporter at pH 5-9; a Ca2+:H+ antiporter at alkaline pH (not an Li:H+ antiporter).
2.A.36.7.1.description: ApNhaP: a Na+:H+ antiporter at pH 5-9; a Ca2+:H+ antiporter at alkaline pH (not an Li:H+ antiporter) (Waditee et al. 2001). When the gene for ApNhaP is expressed in the fresh water cyanobacterium, Synechococcus sp. PCC 7942, it became salt tolerant and could live in salt water (Waditee et al. 2002;).

2.A.36.7.10.name: Na+/H+ antiporter of 1145 aas and 12 TMSs, SOS1.
2.A.36.7.10.description: Na+/H+ antiporter of 1145 aas and 12 TMSs, SOS1. Suppresses salt (200 mM NaCl) sensitivity, promoting tolerance (Wu et al. 2007). It is 65% identical to the A. thaliana homologue (TC# 2.A.36.7.6). In Solanum tuberosum, there are 37 salt overly sensitive 1 (SOS1) genes (Liang et al. 2023). Most of the gene products are located in the plasma membrane. Promoter analysis revealed that the majority of…

2.A.36.7.2.name: Low affinity (Km=8 mM) Na+(Li+):H+ antiporter, NhaS1
2.A.36.7.2.description: Low affinity (Km=8 mM) Na+(Li+):H+ antiporter, NhaS1

2.A.36.7.3.name: Li+/H+ antiporter, AtNHX8.
2.A.36.7.3.description: Li+/H+ antiporter, AtNHX8 (An et al., 2007). An orthologue in Puccinellia tenuiflora (alkali grass) is up regulated under salt stress and confers tolerance to high NaCl stress (Wang et al. 2011). SlNHX6 and SlNHX8 from tomato, are significantly upregulated by salt shock in open flower tissues (Cavusoglu et al. 2023).

2.A.36.7.4.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 11 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 11) (NHE-11) (Solute carrier family 9 member 11) (Solute carrier family 9 member C2)
2.A.36.7.4.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 11 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 11) (NHE-11) (Solute carrier family 9 member 11) (Solute carrier family 9 member C2)

2.A.36.7.5.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 10 (Na+/H+ exchanger 10) (NHE-10) (Solute carrier family 9 member C1) (Sperm-specific Na+/H+ exchanger) (sNHE).
2.A.36.7.5.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 10 (Na+/H+ exchanger 10) (NHE-10) (Solute carrier family 9 member 10) (Solute carrier family 9 member C1) (Sperm-specific Na+/H+ exchanger) (sNHE). It is predicted to have 17 TMSs in a 13 + 4 TMS arrangement. The last 4 TMSs are homologous to the 4 TMS voltage sensor of the Ca2+ channel, 1.A.1.11.7. sNHE is a target for inhibition, for use in male contraception, causing…

2.A.36.7.6.name: Dimeric Salt-Overly-Sensitive 1 (SOS1) sodium:proton exchanger 7 (NHX7).
2.A.36.7.6.description: Dimeric Salt-Overly-Sensitive 1 (SOS1) sodium:proton exchanger 7 (NHX7) (Núñez-Ramírez et al. 2012). The salt stress-induced SOS pathway in A. thaliana involves the perception of a calcium signal by the SOS3 and SOS3-like CALCIUM-BINDING PROTEIN8 (SCaBP8; TC# 5.B.1.1.8) calcium sensors, which then interact with and activate the SOS2 protein kinase (9.B.106.3.4), forming a complex at the plasma…

2.A.36.7.7.name: Testis-specific sodium:proton exchanger, mtsNHE (Slc9c1) of 1175 aas and 12 - 16 TMSs.
2.A.36.7.7.description: Testis-specific sodium:proton exchanger, mtsNHE (Slc9c1) of 1175 aas and 12 - 16 TMSs. It is present in sperm flagellae and seems to be required for optimal sperm motility, fertilization and the acrosome reaction (Liu et al. 2010). 69% identical to the human NHE, TC# 2.A.36.7.5. It may have a 12 TMS topology, but has a long C-terminal hydrophilic domain with a segment showing 2 - 4 TMSs.

2.A.37.1.1.name: Glutathione-regulated K+ efflux protein C, KefC; regulated by ancillary protein KefF (YabF)

2.A.4.2.1.name: Mitochondrial Co2+/Zn2+ uptake (into mitochondria) permease.
2.A.4.2.1.description: Mitochondrial Co2+/Zn2+ uptake (into mitochondria) permease. A single mutation (N45I) increases the specificity for Fe2+ and decreases it for Co2+ (Lin et al., 2008).

2.A.4.2.2.name: Vacuolar Zn2+, Cd2+ uptake (into vacuoles) permease (Zn2+/Cd2+:H+ antiporter).
2.A.4.2.2.description: Vacuolar Zn2+, Cd2+ uptake (into vacuoles) permease (Zn2+/Cd2+:H+ antiporter). A single mutation (N44I) changes the specificity from Zn2+ to Fe2+ (Lin et al., 2008). Lin et al. (2009) have identified transmembrane residues that determine metal specificity.

2.A.4.2.3.name: Plasma membrane Zn2+ efflux permease.
2.A.4.2.3.description: Plasma membrane Zn2+ efflux permease. Substituing H43 with N (asn) changed the specificity from Zn2+ to Mn2+, and this difference was found in the Mn2+-specific metal ion exporter, ZnT10 (TC# 2.A.4.2.5) (Nishito et al. 2016). Expression on the cell surface is controlled by cellular zinc levels (Nishito and Kambe 2019).

2.A.4.2.5.name: Solute carrier family 30, member 10, ZnT10.
2.A.4.2.5.description: Solute carrier family 30, member 10, ZnT10. Manganese efflux transporteer of 485 aas and 6 TMSs in a 4 + 2 TMS arrangement with two long hydrophilic regions between residues 135 and 240, and residues 300 and 485 (Nishito et al. 2016). Homozygous mutations lead to the development of familial manganese Mn2+-induced parkinsonism; it is a cell surface-localized Mn2+ efflux transporter, and…
2.A.4.2.5.proteins: SLC30A10 or ZnT10 of Homo sapiens

2.A.4.2.6.name: Zinc transporter 1 (ZnT-1 or ZnT1) (Solute carrier family 30 member 1).
2.A.4.2.6.description: Zinc transporter 1 (ZnT-1 or ZnT1) (Solute carrier family 30 member 1). The loss of the sialic acid transporter SLC35A1/CST (TC# 2.A.7.12.11) and the zinc transporter, ZnT1, affected cell survival upon infection with cytolytic vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). Both of these transporters seem to play a role in the apoptotic response induced by VSV (Moskovskich et al. 2019). ZnT1 functions by…

2.A.4.2.7.name: ZnT63C Zinc exporter, ZnT1, of 545 aas and 5 putative TMSs.
2.A.4.2.7.description: ZnT63C Zinc exporter, ZnT1, of 545 aas and 5 putative TMSs (Lye et al. 2013; Dechen et al. 2015).

2.A.4.2.8.name: Vacuolar CDF1 transporter.
2.A.4.2.8.description: Vacuolar CDF1 transporter. Transports Zn2+, Co2+ and Cd2+ but not Mn2+, of 487 aas and 6 TMSs (Sácký et al. 2016).

2.A.4.2.9.name: The plasma membrane zinc efflux system, ZnT-1, of 485 aas and 6 predicted TMSs with a large histidine-rich intracellular loop between TMSs 4 and 5…
2.A.4.2.9.description: The plasma membrane zinc efflux system, ZnT-1, of 485 aas and 6 predicted TMSs with a large histidine-rich intracellular loop between TMSs 4 and 5 and intracellular C- and N-termini (Balesaria and Hogstrand 2006).
2.A.4.2.9.proteins: ZnT-1 of Takifugu rubripes (Japanese pufferfish) (Fugu rubripes)

2.A.4.3.1.name: Vesicular Zn2+ uptake (into endosomal/lysosomal vesicles) permease, ZnT2.
2.A.4.3.1.description: Vesicular Zn2+ uptake (into endosomal/lysosomal vesicles) permease, ZnT2. There are two isoforms due to alternative splicing, 35 kDa (plasma membrane localized) and 42 kDa (endosome/secretory compartment localized) (Lopez and Kelleher, 2009).

2.A.4.3.10.name: CDF transporter, MTP1 of 640 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.3.10.description: CDF transporter, MTP1 of 640 aas and 6 TMSs. It transports zinc (Zn2+) and cobalt (Co2+) (Ibuot et al. 2020).

2.A.4.3.12.name: Zinc transporter, Ttm-1, of 410 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.
2.A.4.3.12.description: Zinc transporter, Ttm-1, of 410 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement. It promotes excretion of zinc from intestinal cells into the intestinal lumen in response to increased dietary zinc (Roh et al. 2013). It is also involved in cadmium resistance, possibly by promoting its transport from cells (Huffman et al. 2004). It is also involved in resistance to B. thuringiensis pore-forming toxin…

2.A.4.3.13.name: Zn2+, Fe2+ and Co2+ exporter, AitP, of 321 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.3.13.description: Zn2+, Fe2+ and Co2+ exporter, AitP, of 321 aas and 6 TMSs. The N2-fixing bacteria, Sinorhizobium meliloti, is a suitable model to determine the roles of Co2+-transporting Co-eCDF in Fe2+ homeostasis because it has a putative member of this subfamily, AitP, and two specific Fe2+-export systems. An insertional mutant of AitP showed Co2+ sensitivity and accumulation, Fe accumulation and hydrogen…

2.A.4.3.2.name: Vesicular Zn2+ uptake (into synaptic vesicles) permease, ZnT3 (SLC30A subfamily).
2.A.4.3.2.description: Vesicular Zn2+ uptake (into synaptic vesicles) permease, ZnT3 (SLC30A subfamily). ZnT-3 regulates presynaptic Erk1/2 signaling and hippocampus-dependent memory (Sindreu et al., 2011). Cryo-EM structures of the zinc transporters ZnT3 and ZnT4 provide insights into their transport mechanisms (Ishida et al. 2024). SLC30A3 is a zinc transporter-related biomarker and a potential therapeutic target in…

2.A.4.3.3.name: Mammary epithelia/brain Zn2+ transporter ZnT4. (see TC# 2.A.4.3.2 for more details revealed by cryoEM analyses).
2.A.4.3.3.description: Mammary epithelia/brain Zn2+ transporter ZnT4 (the cause of inherited zinc deficiency in the lethal milk (lm) syndrome of mice, due to a nonsense mutation at codon 297 (arg) in the ZnT4 gene) (Huang and Gitschier, 1997). (see TC# 2.A.4.3.2 for more details revealed by cryoEM analyses) (Ishida et al. 2024).

2.A.4.3.4.name: Plant root and leaf vacuolar Zn2+ transporter, ZAT-1 or MTP1 (metal tolerance protein 1).
2.A.4.3.4.description: Plant root and leaf vacuolar Zn2+ transporter, ZAT-1 or MTP1 (metal tolerance protein 1) (Desbrosses-Fonrouge et al., 2005). Loss of the cytoplasmic histidine-rich loop, where 4 Zn2+ (or Ni2+ or Co2+) bind, stimulates transport activity (Kawachi et al., 2008), presumably providing a feedback sensor of cytoplasmic Zn2+ (Tanaka et al. 2013). The barley orthologue has broader metal specificity…

2.A.4.3.5.name: Homodimeric solute carrier family 30 (zinc transporter), member 8, ZnT8 or ZnT-8.
2.A.4.3.5.description: Homodimeric solute carrier family 30 (zinc transporter), member 8, ZnT8 or ZnT-8. An inherited R325W mutant gives aberant zinc transport in pancreatic beta cells (Weijers 2010). It is chiefly expressed in pancreatic islet cells, where it mediates zinc (Zn2+) uptake into secretory granules. It plays a role in glucose tolerance (Mitchell et al. 2016). ZnT8 is one of four human vesicular zinc…

2.A.4.3.8.name: Metal tolerance protein 4, MTP4, of 386 aas.
2.A.4.3.8.description: Metal tolerance protein 4, MTP4, of 386 aas. Exports Zn2+ and Cd2+ (Migocka et al. 2015). MTP1 transports the same two ions but is less restrictive with respect to the tissues in which the protein is synthesized.

2.A.4.3.9.name: Co2+ resistance protein, DmeF, of 382 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.3.9.description: Co2+ resistance protein, DmeF, of 382 aas and 6 TMSs. Co2+ export appears to be its dominant physiological function, but it may also export other heavy metal ions such as Zn2+ and Cd2+ (Munkelt et al. 2004).

2.A.4.4.1.name: Heteromeric nuclear/ER Zn2+ uptake permease, Msc2/Zrg17.
2.A.4.4.1.description: Heteromeric nuclear/ER Zn2+ uptake permease, Msc2/Zrg17 (Ellis et al., 2005). Zrg17 is also called Meiotic sister-chromatid recombination-related protein or metal cation transporter Msc2p of 724 aas and 15 TMSs in a 7 + 2 + 6 TMS arrangement. Only the last 6 TMSs are homologous to CDF transporters.
2.A.4.4.1.proteins: Msc2/Zrg17 heteromeric Zn2+ transporter of Saccharomyces cerevisiae; Msc2 (Q03455); Zrg17 (P53735)

2.A.4.4.3.name: Golgi/secretory granule Zn2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT5 or ZTL1 (ZnT5 forms heterooligomers with ZnT6)
2.A.4.4.3.description: Golgi/secretory granule Zn2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT5 or ZTL1 (ZnT5 forms heterooligomers with ZnT6) (Ellis et al., 2005; Ishihara et al., 2006; Fukunaka et al. 2009) (Variant B catalyzes bidirectional transport (Valentine et al., 2007))
2.A.4.4.3.proteins: SLC30A5 or ZnT5 of Homo sapiens

2.A.4.4.4.name: Golgi/secretory granule/endoplasmic reticulum Zn2+ uptake (into Golgi, the ER, or granules) permease, ZnT6.
2.A.4.4.4.description: Golgi/secretory granule/endoplasmic reticulum Zn2+ uptake (into Golgi, the ER, or granules) permease, ZnT6. ZnT6 forms heterooligomers with ZnT5 (Ellis et al., 2005; Ishihara et al., 2006; Fukunaka et al. 2009). Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) primarily originates from the exocrine cells of the pancreas. SLC transporters, [more than 450 proteins divided into 65 families] are integral to…

2.A.4.4.5.name: Golgi/secretory granule Zn2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT7.
2.A.4.4.5.description: Golgi/secretory granule Zn2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT7 (Ishihara et al., 2006). Bui et al. 2023 presented the 2.2-3.1 Å-resolution cryo-EM structures of the human Zn2+/H+ antiporter ZnT7 in Zn2+-bound and unbound forms. Cryo-EM analyses show that hZnT7 exists as a dimer via tight interactions in both the cytosolic and transmembrane (TM) domains of two protomers, each of which…

2.A.4.4.6.name: Metal tolerance protein C2 (AtMTPc2) (AtMTP5).
2.A.4.4.6.description: Metal tolerance protein C2 (AtMTPc2) (AtMTP5). Forms a large, active, heteromeric complex with MTP12 in the golgi and pumps Zn2+ into this organelle (Fujiwara et al. 2015). MTP12 has 798 aas and 14 TMSs. Its UniProt acc # is A0A0A8IL98. In Citrus sinensis, expression is induced by Zn2+ in roots (Fu et al. 2017).
2.A.4.4.6.proteins: MTPC2 or MTP5 of Arabidopsis thaliana

2.A.4.4.7.name: Lead (Pb2+) efflux transporter of 211 aas, PbtF.
2.A.4.4.7.description: Lead (Pb2+) efflux transporter of 211 aas, PbtF (Hložková et al. 2013).

2.A.4.5.1.name: Golgi/endomembrane Mn2+-specific CDF transporter (394 aas).
2.A.4.5.1.description: Golgi/endomembrane Mn2+-specific CDF transporter (394 aas) (Peiter et al., 2007). A rice homologue, MTP8.1, has been characterized (Chen et al. 2016).

2.A.4.5.2.name: CDF2 transporter for Zn2+ and Co2+ but not Cd2+ or Mn2+ of 417 aas and 5 TMSs.
2.A.4.5.2.description: CDF2 transporter for Zn2+ and Co2+ but not Cd2+ or Mn2+ of 417 aas and 5 TMSs (Sácký et al. 2016).

2.A.4.5.4.name: Metal tolerance protein 8, MTP8, of 411 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.5.4.description: Metal tolerance protein 8, MTP8, of 411 aas and 6 TMSs. In Citrus sinensis, expression is induced by Mn2+ in roots (Fu et al. 2017). In A. thaliana, MPT8 determines the localization of manganese and iron in seeds (Chu et al. 2017). The endodermal vacuole is the iron and manganese storage compartment in the A. thaliana embryo (Roschzttardtz et al. 2009).

2.A.4.5.6.name: CDF transporter, MTP3, of 458 aas and 7 TMSs.
2.A.4.5.6.description: CDF transporter, MTP3, of 458 aas and 7 TMSs. It transports Mn2+, Zn2+ and Co2+ (Ibuot et al. 2020).

2.A.4.5.7.name: Mn2+ transporting CDF porter, MTP4, of 538 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.5.7.description: Mn2+ transporting CDF porter, MTP4, of 538 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.5.8.name: Metal tolerance protein 4 (MTP4) of 412 aas and 6 central TMSs It has dual functions in maintaining zinc homeostasis in tea plants.
2.A.4.5.8.description: Metal tolerance protein 4 (MTP4) of 412 aas and 6 central TMSs It has dual functions in maintaining zinc homeostasis in tea plants (Li et al. 2024).

2.A.4.6.1.name: CDF transporter, ZnT9 (568 aas).
2.A.4.6.1.description: CDF transporter, ZnT9 (568 aas) (Montanini et al., 2007). Mutations cause autosomal recessive cerebro-renal syndrome and affect intracellular Zinc homeostasis (Perez et al. 2017). Birk-Landau-Perez syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC30A9, causing a complex movement disorder, developmental regression, oculomotor abnormalities, and renal impairment (Steel…

2.A.4.6.2.name: Metal tolerance protein C4, MTPC4 of 457 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.6.2.description: Metal tolerance protein C4, MTPC4 of 457 aas and 6 TMSs. It is involved in sequestration of excess metal ions, including Zn2+ in the cytoplasm into vacuoles to maintain metal homeostasis.

2.A.4.7.1.name: Zn2+/Cd2+/Hg2+/Fe2+:H+ antiporter, YiiP or FieF.
2.A.4.7.1.description: Zn2+/Cd2+/Hg2+/Fe2+:H+ antiporter, YiiP or FieF (Chao and Fu, 2004b; Grass et al., 2005; Wei et al., 2004; Wei and Fu, 2006). The structure (3.8 Å resolution) reveals a homodimer interconnected at the cytoplasmic domain through four Zn2+ ions. A 6 TMS bundle features of a tetrahedral Zn2+ binding site (Lu and Fu, 2007). The gated water access to the transport site enables a stationary proton…

2.A.4.7.10.name: Cobalt/zinc resistance protein B, CzrB, of 291 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.7.10.description: Cobalt/zinc resistance protein B, CzrB, of 291 aas and 6 TMSs. It has a cytosolic extramembranal C-terminus. This 92-residue fragment may function independently of the full-length integral membrane protein. X-ray analyses of this fragment to 2.2 A resolution with and 1.7 A without zinc ions have been solved. The former has at least two zinc ions bound per monomer (Höfer et al. 2007). Full-length…

2.A.4.7.12.name: Mn2+ uptake and efflux system of the rice node.
2.A.4.7.12.description: Mn2+ uptake and efflux system of the rice node (Li et al. 2026).

2.A.4.7.3.name: Magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamB.
2.A.4.7.3.description: Magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamB. Forms a heterodimeric stable complex with MamM which stabilizes MamB. MamB also interacts with other proteins including the PDZ1 domain of MamE (Q6NE61). Both MamB and MamM are essential for magnetite biomineralization and are involved in several steps in magnetosome formation. MamM was used to probe the role of the hydrophilic C-terminal domain (CTD)…

2.A.4.7.4.name: Putative magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamM.
2.A.4.7.4.description: Putative magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamM. Forms a heterodimeric stable complex with MamB which it stabilizes. MamB (see TC# 2.A.4.7.3) also interacts with other proteins including the PDZ1 domain of MamE (Q6NE61). Both MamB and MamM are essential for magnetite biomineralization and are involved in several steps in magnetosome formation, but only MamB is essential for formation of…

2.A.4.7.5.name: Cd2+/Zn2+ efflux pump, YiiP or FieF.
2.A.4.7.5.description: Cd2+/Zn2+ efflux pump, YiiP or FieF. A low resolution structure in the open configuration has been determined by cryoelectron microscopy (Coudray et al. 2013).

2.A.4.7.6.name: Dimeric Mn2+ efflux transporter, MntE of 394 aas.
2.A.4.7.6.description: Dimeric Mn2+ efflux transporter, MntE of 394 aas (Rosch et al. 2009; Lisher et al. 2013; Jakubovics and Valentine 2009; Martin and Giedroc 2016).

2.A.4.7.7.name: Mn2+ efflux pump, YiiP, probably a Mn2+:H+ antiporter.
2.A.4.7.7.description: Mn2+ efflux pump, YiiP, probably a Mn2+:H+ antiporter. Necessary for efficient nodulation of alfalfa plants (Raimunda and Elso-Berberián 2014)

2.A.4.7.8.name: CDF protein, exporting Zn2+ and Cd2+ (323 aas).
2.A.4.7.8.description: CDF protein, exporting Zn2+ and Cd2+ (323 aas). It lacks the C-terminal hydrophilic domain (CTD) common to many CDF homologues (Kolaj-Robin et al. 2015).

2.A.4.7.9.name: Ferrous iron detoxifying protein, FieF, of 337 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.7.9.description: Ferrous iron detoxifying protein, FieF, of 337 aas and 6 TMSs. Also probably exports Zn2+, Co2+, Cd2+ and Ni2+ (Munkelt et al. 2004).

2.A.4.8.1.name: CDF Family homologue with MMT1 domain
2.A.4.8.1.description: CDF Family homologue with MMT1 domain

2.A.4.8.2.name: CDF Family member
2.A.4.8.2.proteins: CDF cation efflux carrier of Mycobacterium tuberculosis

2.A.4.8.3.name: Zn2+ transporter, TMEM163 or Znt11, of 289 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.8.3.description: Zn2+ transporter, TMEM163 or Znt11, of 289 aas and 6 TMSs. It interacts with TrpML1 (TC# 1.A.5.3.1), but by itself, it can pump out Zn2+ (Sanchez et al. 2019). It may be involved in the human lipid storage disorder, mucolipidosis type IV (MLIV), caused by Zn2+ overload (Cuajungco et al. 2014). TMEM163 is found in synaptic vesicles where it is called SV31 (Burré et al. 2007). It plays a role in…

2.A.40.name: The Nucleobase/Ascorbate Transporter (NAT) or Nucleobase:Cation Symporter-2 (NCS2) Family

2.A.40.1.1.name: Uracil permease, UraA.
2.A.40.1.1.description: Uracil permease, UraA. The crystal structure of UraA with bound uracil at 2.8 Å resolution is available (PDB: 3QE7) (Lu et al., 2011). UraA has a novel structural fold, with 14 TMSs divided into two inverted repeats. A pair of antiparallel β-strands is located between TMS3 and TMS10 and has an important role in structural organization and substrate recognition. The structure is spatially arranged…

2.A.40.1.2.name: High affinity uracil permease.
2.A.40.1.2.description: High affinity uracil permease (Martinussen et al. 2001).

2.A.40.1.3.name: Pyrimidine transporter of broad specificity, RutG of 442 aas and 14 TMSs; transports both uracil and thymine with high affinity as well as, xanthine…
2.A.40.1.3.description: Pyrimidine transporter of broad specificity, RutG of 442 aas and 14 TMSs; transports both uracil and thymine with high affinity as well as, xanthine with low efficiency (Loh et al., 2006; Kim et al. 2010; Botou et al. 2018).

2.A.40.3.2.name: Uric acid permease of 449 aas and 13 TMSs, PucJ.
2.A.40.3.2.description: Uric acid permease of 449 aas and 13 TMSs, PucJ. May function together with PucK (TC# 2.A.40.3.4) (Schultz et al. 2001).

2.A.40.3.3.name: Uric acid (urate) permease YgfU.
2.A.40.3.3.description: Uric acid (urate) permease YgfU. YgfU exhibits low affinity (0.5 mM) but high capacity for urate and very poor activity for xanthine. Essential residues were identified. Coversion of Thr-100 to ala resulted in efficient xanthine transport (Papakostas and Frillingos 2012).

2.A.40.3.4.name: Uric acid uptake porter of 430 aas and 13 TMSs, PucK.
2.A.40.3.4.description: Uric acid uptake porter of 430 aas and 13 TMSs, PucK. May function together with PucJ (TC# 2.A.40.3.2) (Schultz et al. 2001).

2.A.40.4.1.name: High affinity uric acid-xanthine permease, UapA.
2.A.40.4.1.description: High affinity uric acid-xanthine permease, UapA. Functionaly critical residues in transmembrane segments 1 and 3 have been identified (Amillis et al., 2011). The substrate recognition and transport pathway have been proposed (Kosti et al., 2012; Kosti et al. 2010). UapA oligomerization is essential for membrane trafficking and turnover and is a common theme in fungi and mammalian cells…

2.A.40.4.2.name: The putative xanthine permease, YicE
2.A.40.4.2.description: The putative xanthine permease, YicE (Karatza and Frillingos, 2005)

2.A.40.4.3.name: The YgfO (XanQ) purine (xanthine) transporter.
2.A.40.4.3.description: The YgfO (XanQ) purine (xanthine) transporter. Residues involved in substrate binding have been identified (Georgopoulou et al., 2010). TMS3 functions in substrate recognition (Karena and Frillingos, 2011). Many more essential residues have more recently been identified (Karena et al. 2015). An "ancestral" homolog (AncXanQ) has been constructed and proved to have broader specificity, transporting…

2.A.40.4.4.name: Purine (uric acid and xanthine) permease, UapC.
2.A.40.4.4.description: Purine (uric acid and xanthine) permease, UapC. Present in many Ascomycetes (Krypotou and Diallinas 2014). Drought is an important abiotic stress that constrains the quality and quantity of tea plants. The green leaf volatiles, Z-3-hexenyl acetate (Z-3-HAC), play an essential role in stress responses (Wang et al. 2023).

2.A.40.4.6.name: XanQ or PbuX, purine base uptake porter specific for xanthine and guanine.
2.A.40.4.6.description: XanQ or PbuX, purine base uptake porter specific for xanthine and guanine. It is of 463 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs in a 5 + 3 or 4 +1 + 4 TMS arrangement (Tatsaki et al. 2021).

2.A.40.5.1.name: Putative purine permease, YbbY.
2.A.40.5.1.description: Putative purine permease, YbbY. The ybbY gene is in an operon involved with allantoin metabolism, and is flanked by allB, encoding allantoinase, and the glxK gene, encoding glycerate kinase II. Downstream of glxK is YlbA, encoding S-uridoglycine aminohydrolase, the second enzyme involved in allantoin degradation (Moraes and Reithmeier 2012).

2.A.40.6.1.name: L-ascorbate:Na+ symporter, SVCT1..
2.A.40.6.1.description: L-ascorbate:Na+ symporter, SVCT1. (L-ascorbate:Na+= 1:2; Mackenzie et al., 2008). Iron regulates SVCT1 in human intestinal Caco-2 cells (Scheers and Sandberg, 2011).

2.A.40.6.2.name: Ca2+/Mg2+-dependent L-ascorbate:Na+ symporter, SVCT2; Na+:ascorbate = 2:1; binding order: Na+, ascorbate, Na+; Ca2+/Mg2+ are required for function).
2.A.40.6.2.description: Ca2+/Mg2+-dependent L-ascorbate:Na+ symporter, SVCT2; Na+:ascorbate = 2:1; binding order: Na+, ascorbate, Na+ (Na+ increases the affinity for ascorbate); Ca2+/Mg2+ are required for function) (Godoy et al., 2007; Bürzle et al. 2013). SVCT2-GLUT1-mediated ascorbic acid transport pathway in rat dental pulp has been studied, and its effects during wound healing have been described (Ohkura et al…

2.A.40.6.4.name: solute carrier family 23 (nucleobase transporters), member 3, SVCT3 or SLC23A3.
2.A.40.6.4.description: solute carrier family 23 (nucleobase transporters), member 3, SVCT3 or SLC23A3. Function not certain as of 1/2013 (Bürzle et al. 2013).

2.A.40.6.5.name: Solute carrier family 23 member 1 (hSVCT1; Yolk sac permease-like molecule 3).
2.A.40.6.5.description: Solute carrier family 23 member 1 (Na+/L-ascorbic acid transporter 1; Sodium-dependent vitamin C transporter 1) (hSVCT1; Yolk sac permease-like molecule 3) (Bürzle et al. 2013). Members of the SLC23 family have the UraA fold (Ferrada and Superti-Furga 2022). Gut microbiota remodeling mediates the therapeutic effects of a plant-based medicine on DSS-induced ulcerative colitis in mice via the…

2.A.40.6.7.name: Solute carrier family 23 member 2-like protein (SLC23.A.4) of 614 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs, SNBT1.
2.A.40.6.7.description: Solute carrier family 23 member 2-like protein (SLC23.A.4) of 614 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs, SNBT1. Mutations allowed functional insertion into fungal membranes (Kourkoulou et al. 2019). It transports urate and purine nucleobases in a sodium ion-dependent process (Yamamoto et al. 2010; Yasujima et al. 2018).
2.A.40.6.7.proteins: SNBT1 of Rattus norvegicus, the Norway rat.

2.A.40.7.1.name: The purine (hypoxanthine/adenine/guanine) transporter, AzgA.
2.A.40.7.1.description: The purine (hypoxanthine/adenine/guanine) transporter, AzgA (Cecchetto et al., 2004). Topological modeling has revealed a potential substrate binding cavity, and residues important for transport activity have been identified (Krypotou et al. 2014). AZGs proteins represent a new family of cytokinin transporters (Tessi and Maurino 2024). Cytokinins (CKs) are phytohormones structurally similar to…

2.A.40.7.2.name: Hypoxanthine/guanosine uptake transporter, PbuG
2.A.40.7.2.description: Hypoxanthine/guanosine uptake transporter, PbuG (Johansen et al., 2003)

2.A.40.7.3.name: The purine transporter Azg1 takes up 8-azaadenine and 8-azaguanine but not other toxic nucleobase analogues; similar to Azg2 of A. thaliana (Q84MA8);.
2.A.40.7.3.description: The purine transporter Azg1 (takes up 8-azaadenine and 8-azaguanine but not other toxic nucleobase analogues; similar to Azg2 of A. thaliana (Q84MA8); (Mansfield et al. 2009). AZG1 is a cytokinin transporter that interacts with auxin transporter PIN1 (TC# 2.A.69.1.1) and regulates the root stress response (Tessi et al. 2023). The structures and mechanisms of the Arabidopsis cytokinin transporter…

2.A.40.7.4.name: Adenine permease, YicO.
2.A.40.7.4.description: Adenine permease, YicO. Also recognizes with low micromolar affinity N(6)-benzoyladenine, 2,6-diaminopurine, and purines (Papakostas et al. 2013).

2.A.40.7.5.name: Purine base permease, GhxP or YjcD.
2.A.40.7.5.description: Purine base permease, GhxP or YjcD. Transports purines such as guanine, hypoxanthine, and xanthine. Also transports mutagenic purines such as 6-N-hydroxylaminopurine (HAP), 2-amino-HAP (AHAP), 6-mercaptopurine, 6-thioguanine, 1-methylguanine, 8-azaguanine, 6-thioguanine and 2-aminopurine (Kozmin et al. 2013; Papakostas et al. 2013).

2.A.40.7.6.name: Adenine permease, PurP.
2.A.40.7.6.description: Adenine permease, PurP. Also recognize with low micromolar affinity N(6)-benzoyladenine, 2,6-diaminopurine, and purine (Papakostas et al. 2013).

2.A.40.7.7.name: Guanine/hypoxanthine uptake porter of 455 aas, GhxQ, YgfQ or YgfR.
2.A.40.7.7.description: Guanine/hypoxanthine uptake porter of 455 aas, GhxQ, YgfQ or YgfR. Also takes up mutagens such as 1-methylguanine, 8-azaguanine, 6-thioguanine, and 6-mercaptopurine (Papakostas et al. 2013) and catalyzes dis-C3 (membrane-permeable, cationic fluorescent dye, the carbocyanine diS-C3 efflux (Jindal et al. 2019).

2.A.40.7.8.name: NCS2 family permease of 429 aas and 13 apparent TMSs in a 7 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.40.7.8.description: NCS2 family permease of 429 aas and 13 apparent TMSs in a 7 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.40.7.8.proteins: NCS2 family protein of Tissierellia bacterium

2.A.40.7.9.name: Purine transporter, PhZ, of 578 aas and probably 14 TMSs in a 2 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 4 TMS arrangement.
2.A.40.7.9.description: Purine transporter, PhZ, of 578 aas and probably 14 TMSs in a 2 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 4 TMS arrangement. Critical residues for transport are located in the TMSs and an internal helix. In the latter, the A418 residue was identified as playing a pivotal role in transport efficiency despite being far from the putative substrate binding site, as mutant A418V showed an increased initial uptake efficiency for…
2.A.40.7.9.proteins: PhZ of Phanerodontia chrysosporium (White-rot fungus) (Sporotrichum pruinosum)

2.A.40.8.1.name: Uncharacterized protein of 552 aas and 16 TMSs.
2.A.40.8.1.description: Uncharacterized protein of 552 aas and 16 TMSs.

2.A.40.8.2.name: Xanthine permease of 520 aas and 16 TMSs in a 7 + 2 + 7 TMS arrangement.
2.A.40.8.2.description: Xanthine permease of 520 aas and 16 TMSs in a 7 + 2 + 7 TMS arrangement.

2.A.41.1.1.name: Pyrimidine nucleoside:H+ symporter, NupC.
2.A.41.1.1.description: Pyrimidine nucleoside:H+ symporter, NupC (Craig et al. 1994; Patching et al. 2005). Wild-type NupC had an apparent affinity for uridine of 22.2 +/- 3.7 muM and an apparent binding affinity of 1.8-2.6 mM, and various mutants with alterred properties were isolated and characterized (Sun et al. 2017). ADP-glucose is also a substrate of this system (Almagro et al. 2018).

2.A.41.1.3.name: The purine nucleoside uptake transporter NupG (YxjA)
2.A.41.1.3.description: The purine nucleoside uptake transporter NupG (YxjA) (Johansen et al., 2003)

2.A.41.2.1.name: Purine-specific nucleoside:Na+ symporter
2.A.41.2.1.proteins: The bile canalicular purine-specific nucleoside:Na+ symporter of Rattus norvegicus (Q62773)

2.A.41.2.11.name: Concentrative nucleoside transporter, CNT, of 418 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.41.2.11.description: Concentrative nucleoside transporter, CNT, of 418 aas and 12 TMSs. A repeat-swapped model of VcCNT predicts that nucleoside transport occurs via a mechanism involving an elevator-like substrate binding domain movement across the membrane (Vergara-Jaque et al. 2015).

2.A.41.2.13.name: Sodium-dependent and pyrimidine-selective transporter, CNT1 or SLC26A1, of 649 aas and 16 TMSs in an apparent 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 4 + 2 arrangement.
2.A.41.2.13.description: Sodium-dependent and pyrimidine-selective transporter, CNT1 or SLC26A1, of 649 aas and 16 TMSs in an apparent 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 4 + 2 arrangement (Cano-Soldado et al. 2012, Loewen et al. 1999). It is selective for pyrimidine nucleosides and adenosine (Cano-Soldado et al. 2012). It transports uridine, cytidine, thymidine, and nucleoside-derived drugs (Yao et al. 2011), including the antiviral…

2.A.41.2.2.name: Nonspecific nucleoside:Na+ symporter
2.A.41.2.2.proteins: The nucleoside:Na+ symporter of Rattus norvegicus (Q62674)

2.A.41.2.3.name: Pyrimidine-preferring nucleoside:Na+ symporter, CNT1 (Na+/nucleoside = 2), but in addition to pyrimidine nucelosides, it transports adenosine.
2.A.41.2.3.description: Pyrimidine-preferring nucleoside:Na+ symporter, CNT1 (Na+/nucleoside = 2)(transports uridine, gemcitabine and 5'-deoxy-5'-fluorouridine) (Larráyoz et al., 2004), but in addition to pyrimidine nucelosides, it transports adenosine (Altaweraqi et al. 2020).

2.A.41.2.4.name: Purine and pyrimidien nucleosides, uridine, and 2'3'dideoxyinosine cladribrine:Na+ or H+ symporter, CNT2 of 658 aas and 11 - 14 TMSs.
2.A.41.2.4.description: Purine and pyrimidien nucleosides, uridine, and 2'3'dideoxyinosine cladribrine:Na+ or H+ symporter, CNT2 of 658 aas and 11 - 14 TMSs (Na+/nucleoside = 1) (Owen et al., 2006; Altaweraqi et al. 2020).

2.A.41.2.5.name: Broadly selective nucleoside:Na+ cotransporter, hfCNT (Na+/uridine = 2)
2.A.41.2.5.description: Broadly selective nucleoside:Na+ cotransporter, hfCNT (transports uridine, thymidine, inosine, 3'-azido-3'deoxythymidine, 2'3'dideoxycytidine, and 2'3'dideoxyinosine) (Na+/uridine = 2)

2.A.41.2.7.name: Broad specificity nucleoside:H+ symporter (1:1 stoichiometry).
2.A.41.2.7.description: Broad specificity nucleoside:H+ symporter (1:1 stoichiometry). Adenosine, uridine, inosine, and guanosine are transported but not cytidine, thymidine or the nucleobase hypoxanthine (Km range: 15-65 μM). Purine and uridine nucleoside drug analogues including cordycepin (3'-deoxyadenosine) are substrates.

2.A.41.2.8.name: Solute carrier family 28 member 3 (Concentrative Na+-nucleoside cotransporter 3) (CNT 3) (hCNT3).
2.A.41.2.8.description: Solute carrier family 28 member 3 (Concentrative Na+-nucleoside cotransporter 3) (CNT 3) (hCNT3). This protein is distinct from TC# 2.A.41.2.6 (78% identity) although these two proteins are called Slc28a3 and CNT3 and have the same description in UniProt (see 2.A.41.2.6 for a more complete description). hCNT3 can transport extracellular nucleosides and various nucleoside-derived anticancer drugs…

2.A.42.1.2.name: High affinity 3 μM tryptophan permease, Mtr.
2.A.42.1.2.description: High affinity (3 μM tryptophan permease, Mtr. Also transports indole. It functions to scavenge trace amounts of tryptophan in the medium for protein synthesis when concentrations are very low (Gu et al. 2013).

2.A.42.1.3.name: Low affinity (70 μM) tryptophan permease, coregulated with the enzyme tryptophanase.
2.A.42.1.3.description: Low affinity (70 μM) tryptophan permease, coregulated with the enzyme tryptophanase. It functions in tryptohan degradation, yielding carbon and nitrogen (Gu et al. 2013).

2.A.42.1.4.name: Tyrosine permease (most similar in sequence to Mtr of E. coli)
2.A.42.1.4.description: Tyrosine permease (most similar in sequence to Mtr of E. coli)

2.A.42.1.6.name: γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA):Na+ symporter.
2.A.42.1.6.description: γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA):Na+ symporter (Zhao et al. 2012). The GABA Km is 40 µM, and uptake is inhibited by L-Asn and L-Gln.

2.A.42.1.7.name: Aromatic amino acid permease of 367 aas and 11 TMSs
2.A.42.1.7.description: Aromatic amino acid permease of 367 aas and 11 TMSs
2.A.42.1.7.proteins: ArAAAP family member of Thermococcus barophilus

2.A.42.2.3.name: Inner membrane transport protein, YhjV, of 423 aas and 11 TMSs.
2.A.42.2.3.description: Inner membrane transport protein, YhjV, of 423 aas and 11 TMSs. It may play a role in the transport of fluorophores (fluorescent dyes) (Salcedo-Sora et al. 2021) as well as melatonin (Yang et al. 2022).

2.A.43.1.1.name: Lysosomal cystine transporter, cystinosin (CTNS) of 267 aas and 7 TMSs.
2.A.43.1.1.description: Lysosomal cystine transporter, cystinosin (CTNS) of 267 aas and 7 TMSs. It uses a cystine:H+ symport mechanism. H+ binds to an aspartate residue in one of the two PQ-loops (Ruivo et al., 2012). Several mutations in the CTNS gene gives rise to ocular cystinosis (Browning et al. 2019). Microvesicle delivery of cystinosin to ex vivo corneal keratocytes (corneal fibroblasts) corrects the cystine…
2.A.43.1.1.proteins: Cystinosin or CTNS of Homo sapiens

2.A.43.1.2.name: Cystinosin homolog of 397 aas and 7 TMSs.
2.A.43.1.2.description: Cystinosin homolog of 397 aas and 7 TMSs.

2.A.43.1.4.name: Cystinosin homolog of 270 aas and 6 or 7 TMSs uses the proton gradient to drive cystine export from the lysosome into the cytoplasm.
2.A.43.1.4.description: Cystinosin homolog of 270 aas and 6 or 7 TMSs uses the proton gradient to drive cystine export from the lysosome into the cytoplasm. Löbel et al. 2022 presented the crystal structures of cystinosin from Arabidopsis thaliana in both apo and cystine bound states. They establish a mechanism for cystine recognition and proton coupled transport. Mutational mapping and functional characterisation of…

2.A.43.2.1.name: The lysosomal lysine-arginine transporter, LAAT1, SLC66A1, PQ-loop repeat containing protein 2 (PQLC2) (291 aas; 7 TMSs).
2.A.43.2.1.description: The lysosomal lysine-arginine transporter, LAAT1, SLC66A1, PQ-loop repeat containing protein 2 (PQLC2) (291 aas; 7 TMSs). Also transports L-histidine, L-ornithine, the mixed disulfide of cysteine-cysteamine, a lysine analogue, as well as canavanine, a toxic arginine analogue. Cysteamine is used in the treatment of cystinosis (Liu et al., 2012; Jézégou et al. 2012).

2.A.43.2.10.name: The probable vacuolar amino acid transporter YPQ1 of 381 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.43.2.10.description: The probable vacuolar amino acid transporter YPQ1 of 381 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.43.2.11.description: The probable vacuolar amino acid transporter Ypq1 of 381 aas and 6 TMSs

2.A.43.2.13.name: Cdc50 supressor, CSF1 of 405 aas and 7 TMSs.
2.A.43.2.13.description: Cdc50 supressor, CSF1 of 405 aas and 7 TMSs. Appears to function as a phospholipid flippase or to regulate PL flipping in endosomes or late golgi vesicles (Yamamoto et al. 2017).

2.A.43.2.2.name: The lysosomal lysine-arginine transporter, LAAT1, PQ-loop superfamily member (qx42 gene product; 310aas; 7 TMSs).
2.A.43.2.2.description: The lysosomal lysine-arginine transporter, LAAT1, PQ-loop superfamily member (qx42 gene product; 310aas; 7 TMSs) (Liu et al., 2012).

2.A.43.2.3.name: Vacuolar (lysosomal) cationic amino acid transporter (YOL092W) (308aas; 7 TMSs), LAAT1.
2.A.43.2.3.description: Vacuolar (lysosomal) cationic amino acid transporter (YOL092W) (308aas; 7 TMSs), LAAT1. Involved in cationic amino acid homeostasis (Jézégou et al. 2012). It may function as an amino acid exporter of cationic amino acids from the vacuole. The vacuole-associated Rsp5 ubiquitin ligase uses a TMS in the substrate adaptor Ssh4 to recognize membrane helices in Ypq1, which targets this lysine…

2.A.43.2.7.name: Probable vacuolar (lysosomal) cationic amino acid exporter, RTC2 (Ypq3; Ybr147).
2.A.43.2.7.description: Probable vacuolar (lysosomal) cationic amino acid exporter, RTC2 (Ypq3; Ybr147). Involved in amino acid homeostasis. Up-regulated by addition of ammonia or amino acids to a nitrogen-depleted medium (Jézégou et al. 2012). Resistant to fluconazole. Increased resistance to caspofungin. Suppresses CDC13-1 temperature sensitivity.

2.A.43.2.8.name: Vacuolar (lysosomal) putative cationic amino acid exporter, Ypq2 (Ydr352); involved with cationic amino acid homeostasis.
2.A.43.2.8.description: Vacuolar (lysosomal) putative cationic amino acid exporter, Ypq2 (Ydr352); involved with cationic amino acid homeostasis (Jézégou et al. 2012).

2.A.43.2.9.description: PQ loop protein of 384 aas and 7 (3 + 4) TMSs

2.A.43.3.1.name: The Lec15/Lec35 suppressor, SL15, MPDU1 or SLC66A5, of 247 aas and probably 7 TMSs.
2.A.43.3.1.description: The Lec15/Lec35 suppressor, SL15, MPDU1 or SLC66A5, of 247 aas and probably 7 TMSs. It is a suppressor of the Lec15 and Lec35 glycosylation mutations (Ware and Lehrman 1998). The human ortholog is 89% identical to this protein. This protein may be required for normal utilization of mannose-dolichol phosphate (Dol-P-Man) in the synthesis of N-linked and O-linked oligosaccharides and GPI anchors.

2.A.43.3.2.name: PQ-loop-containing protein 3 (PQLC3) of 202 aas and 7 closely spaced TMSs.
2.A.43.3.2.description: PQ-loop-containing protein 3 (PQLC3) of 202 aas and 7 closely spaced TMSs. It may play a role in gestational diabetes mellitus (Li et al. 2021). It may also function in tumor mutation burden for predicting lymph node metastasis in breast cancer (Wang et al. 2021).

2.A.45.1.1.name: Arsenical resistance efflux pump (exports As(III) and Sb(III) probably as polymers of the hydroxides using an H+ antiport mechanism)
2.A.45.1.1.description: Arsenical resistance efflux pump (exports As(III) and Sb(III) probably as polymers of the hydroxides using an H+ antiport mechanism) (Meng et al., 2004)

2.A.45.1.2.description: Arsenic transporter, ArsB, of 422 aas and 11 TMSs.

2.A.45.2.1.description: P-protein of 838 aas and up to 16 TMSs in a 1 or 2 + 6 or 7 + 6 or 7 TMS arrangement; possible tyrosine transporter (also called "melanocyte-specific transporter", "oculocutaneous albinism-related protein (Oca2)" and "pink-eyed dilution gene product"). It has been reported to exhibit chloride-selective anion channel activity and to be required for melanin production, possibly by controling…

2.A.45.2.3.name: Putative ion transporter in magnetosome membranes of magentotactic bacteria, MamN of 437 aas and 10 TMSs.
2.A.45.2.3.description: Putative ion transporter in magnetosome membranes of magentotactic bacteria, MamN of 437 aas and 10 TMSs (Murat et al. 2010). Uebe and Schüler 2016 considered that MamN might be a proton exporter that releases H+ from the magentosome matrix to the cytosol.

2.A.45.2.4.name: The plasma membrane silicon (silicate) efflux pump, Low Silicon 2, Lsi2 (Ma et al., 2007a, b).
2.A.45.2.4.description: The plasma membrane silicon (silicate) efflux pump, Low Silicon 2, Lsi2 (localized to the proximal side of the cell, whereas the silicon uptake system, Lsi1 (TC# 1.A.8.12.2) is localized to the distal side of the same cells) (Ma et al., 2007a, b). It has 472 aas and 10 TMSs in a 5 + 5 TMS arrangement.

2.A.45.2.6.name: Putative plasma membrane low silicon efflux pump, Lsi2, of 393 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.45.2.6.description: Putative plasma membrane low silicon efflux pump, Lsi2, of 393 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.45.2.7.name: Citrate transporter, OsCT1 of 567 aas and 12 TMSs in a 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 TMS arrangement.
2.A.45.2.7.description: Citrate transporter, OsCT1 of 567 aas and 12 TMSs in a 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 TMS arrangement. It differs from previously known plant citrate transporters and is structurally close to rice silicon transporters (Panchal et al. 2023). OsCT1 carries a bacterial citrate-metal transporter domain, CitMHS. and showed citrate efflux activity when expressed in Xenopus laevis oocytes, being…
2.A.45.2.7.proteins: OsCT1 of Oryza sativa Japonica Group (Japanese rice)

2.A.45.2.8.name: Arsenite long-distance transporter from arsenic hyperaccumulator fern Pteris vittata of 578 aas and 9 to 11 TMSs in a 4 or 5 + 5 or 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.45.2.8.description: Arsenite long-distance transporter from arsenic hyperaccumulator fern Pteris vittata of 578 aas and 9 to 11 TMSs in a 4 or 5 + 5 or 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.45.2.9.name: Low silicon protein 3, Lsi3 (also Lsi6) of 485 aas and 10 TMSs in a 5 + 5 TMS arrangement from rice.
2.A.45.2.9.description: Low silicon protein 3, Lsi3 (also Lsi6) of 485 aas and 10 TMSs in a 5 + 5 TMS arrangement from rice. Opaline silica bodies (phytoliths) are found in plants, particularly grasses. They primarily contribute to plant strength and protection, and form from silicic acid, which is transported from the soil to the leaves. The structures of Lsi proteins have been determined (Sepay et al. 2026).

2.A.46.1.1.name: Benzoate permease, BenE of 394 aas and 11 - 13 TMSs.
2.A.46.1.1.description: Benzoate permease, BenE of 394 aas and 11 - 13 TMSs (Neidle et al. 1991).

2.A.46.1.10.description: Benzoate uptake porter of 423 aas and 12 TMSs, BenE (Choudhary et al. 2017).

2.A.46.1.11.description: Membrane protein PurT of 471 aas and 14 TMSs. 2.A.47.1.13.description: The Na+-coupled dicarboxylate (succinate; malate; fumarate) transporter, SdcL (transports aspartate, α-ketoglutarate and oxaloacetate with low affinity). Km for succinate, ~6 μM; Km for Na+, 0.9 mM; Na:substrate = 2:1 (Strickler et al., 2009).

2.A.47.1.14.name: solute carrier family 13 (sodium/sulfate symporters), member 4, NaS2.
2.A.47.1.14.description: solute carrier family 13 (sodium/sulfate symporters), member 4, NaS2. Transports anions such as sulfate, thiosulfate and selenate (Bergeron et al. 2013).

2.A.47.1.16.description: Solute carrier family 13 member 1 (Renal and intestinal sodium/sulfate cotransporter) (Na+/sulfate cotransporter) (hNaSi-1). Also transports thiosulfate and selenium. It is inhibited by many di- and tri-valent organic and inorganic anions (Markovich 2013).

2.A.47.1.17.description: Solute carrier family 13 member 2 (Na /di- and tricarboxylate cotransporter 1) (NaDC-1) (Renal sodium/dicarboxylate cotransporter). Transmembrane helices 7 and 11 in NaDC1 contains residues critical for function (Pajor…

2.A.47.1.18.name: Organic acid transporter, SdcF.
2.A.47.1.18.description: Organic acid transporter, SdcF. Transports succinate, malate, fumarate, tartrate and oxaloacetate (A. Pajor, personal communication)

2.A.47.1.19.name: Solute carrier family 13, Slc13a1; Sodium/sulfate symporter, member 1, NaS1 of 583 aas and 14 TMSs.

2.A.47.1.2.name: Renal sodium:sulfate cotransporter (Ssc, NaSi-1 or Nas1) (also transports tungstate, molybdate, thiosulfate and selenate).

2.A.47.1.3.name: The brush boarder intestinal and renal electrogenic, Na -dependent, low affinity (0.1-4.0mM), dicarboxylate:H cotransporter, NaDC-1 or SDCT1.
2.A.47.1.3.description: The brush boarder intestinal and renal electrogenic, Na -dependent, low affinity (0.1-4.0mM), dicarboxylate (succinate, fumarate, malate, α-ketoglutarate, oxaloacetate, L- and D-glutamate, and citrate):H cotransporter, NaDC-1 or SDCT1. 2.A.47.1.4.name: The basolateral intestinal and renal electrogenic, Na+-dependent high affinity (2-50µM) dicarboxylate:(Na+)3 cotransporter (NaDC-3).

2.A.47.2.1.description: Inorganic phosphate transporter, Pho87 of 923 aas and 12 TMSs. Also transports selenite (Lazard et al., 2010).

Also transports selenite (Lazard et al., 2010). 2.A.47.2.3.description: Low affinity phosphate transporters (881aas). Also transports selenite (Lazard et al., 2010).

2.A.47.3.2.name: Citrate:succinate antiporter.
2.A.47.3.2.description: Citrate:succinate antiporter (Pos et al. 1998). Binds and presumably regulates the heterodimeric citrate lyase, CitE/CitF which converts citrate to succinate and acetate (Quentmeier et al. 1987). These proteins form a metabolon which together catalyze citrate fermentation under anaerobic conditions.

2.A.47.3.3.name: L-tartrate:succinate antiporter, TtdT (YgjE). (also takes up meso and L-tartrate and succinate; does not transport D-tartrate).
2.A.47.3.3.description: L-tartrate:succinate antiporter, TtdT (YgjE). (also takes up meso and L-tartrate and succinate; does not transport D-tartrate) (Kim and Unden, 2007). It is induced in the presence of L- or meso tartrate under anaerobic conditions in the presence of TtdR (Kim et al. 2009).
