Therefore the annotation shown above may be incorrect and this protein may also be an S-adenosyl methionine uptake porter (Dridi et al. 2010).

2.A.71.1.5.name: High affinity plasma membrane constitutively synthesized S-Adenosylmethionine (AdoMet) uptake transporter, AdoMetT1 of 706 aas.
2.A.71.1.5.description: High affinity plasma membrane constitutively synthesized S-Adenosylmethionine (AdoMet) uptake transporter, AdoMetT1 of 706 aas. It also takes up the AdoMet analogue, Sinefungin (Dridi et al. 2010). This protein is nearly identical to 2.A.71.1.3 which may also be an AdoMet uptake transporter (by sequence similarity).

2.A.71.1.6.name: Folate/biopterin/methotrexate transporter, BT1, of 1057 aas and 14 TMSs in the N-terminal half of the protein with an equally long C-terminal…
2.A.71.1.6.description: Folate/biopterin/methotrexate transporter, BT1, of 1057 aas and 14 TMSs in the N-terminal half of the protein (residues 1 - 500) with an equally long C-terminal hydrophilic domain. Uptake of folate across the parasite plasma membrane is rapid, biphasic, temperature dependent, bi-directional, concentration dependent and specific (Massimine et al. 2005).

2.A.71.2.2.name: Folate/biopterin uptake carrier, Fbp.
2.A.71.2.2.description: Folate/biopterin uptake carrier, Fbp. Transports 5-formyl tetrahydrofolate monoglutamate but not 5-formyltetrahydrofolate triglutamate. (Also transports methotrexate and aminopterin) (Klaus et al., 2005) (Nine homologues are present in Arabidopsis thaliana.) (Klaus et al., 2005). Mutational analyses suggest that the folate binding site involves the core helices 1, 4, 7 and 10 and is in the center…

2.A.71.2.3.name: Folate/biopterin uptake carrier of 494 aas, Fbp (also transports methotrexate and aminopterin).
2.A.71.2.3.description: Folate/biopterin uptake carrier of 494 aas, Fbp (also transports methotrexate and aminopterin) (Klaus et al., 2005). Essential residues line the central cavity (based on the LacY structure) in TMSs 1, 4, 7 and 10 (Eudes et al. 2010). Analysis of folate-biopterin transporter (FBT) genes in grape berry reveals candidates associated with fruit ripening (Hu et al. 2025).

2.A.71.2.4.name: Folate transporter 3, FT3 of 537 aas and 14 putative TMSs.
2.A.71.2.4.description: Folate transporter 3, FT3 of 537 aas and 14 putative TMSs.

2.A.71.2.7.name: Folate/pABA/5-methyltetrahydrofolate transporter, putative, of 505 aas with 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.71.2.7.description: Folate/pABA/5-methyltetrahydrofolate transporter, putative, of 505 aas with 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.72.1.1.name: Low affinity K+ uptake permease, KUP or TrkD.
2.A.72.1.1.description: Low affinity K+ uptake permease, KUP or TrkD. It has 12 established TMSs with four transmembrane acidic residues important for K+ uptake (Sato et al. 2014).

2.A.72.1.2.name: Probable potassium transport system protein Kup
2.A.72.1.2.description: Probable potassium transport system protein Kup

2.A.72.1.3.name: Probable potassium transport system protein, Kup 1 of 670 aas
2.A.72.1.3.description: Probable potassium transport system protein, Kup 1 of 670 aas

2.A.72.2.2.name: The K+ uptake transporter, DhHAK1 (expressed when K+ starved)
2.A.72.2.2.description: The K+ uptake transporter, DhHAK1 (expressed when K+ starved) (Prista et al., 2007)

2.A.72.3.10.name: Tiny root hair-1 K+ transporter (TRH1) of 775 aas, also called K+ transporter-3 (POT3; KT3) or KUP4.
2.A.72.3.10.description: Tiny root hair-1 K+ transporter (TRH1) of 775 aas, also called K+ transporter-3 (POT3; KT3) or KUP4. It regulates root hair elongation (Daras et al. 2015).

2.A.72.3.11.name: K+ transporter, HAK1 of 777 aas and 13 TMSs.
2.A.72.3.11.description: K+ transporter, HAK1 of 777 aas and 13 TMSs (Guo et al. 2008). Also capable of anion channel activity at high voltages as those found in plants, fungi and bacteria, but not animal cells, possibly using to a new route formed by oligomerization (Pardo et al. 2015).

2.A.72.3.12.name: KUP9 (POT9; HAK12) potassium ion transporter of 784 aas and 12 - 14 TMSs in a 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 (+ 2?) TMS arrangement.
2.A.72.3.12.description: KUP9 (POT9; HAK12) potassium ion transporter of 784 aas and 12 - 14 TMSs in a 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 (+ 2?) TMS arrangement. It is up-regluated upon salt stress (Yang et al. 2018). KUP9 regulates plant response to K+ deficiency and affects carbohydrate allocation in A. thaliana (Šustr et al. 2024). A salt-responsive PvHAK12 from Paspalum vaginatum negatively regulates salt tolerance in transgenic…

2.A.72.3.2.name: K+:H+ symporter, HAK1.
2.A.72.3.2.description: K+:H+ symporter, HAK1. Hak1p is produced at high levels but is down regluated by extracellular K and by expression of Trk1 (2.A.38.2.2) (Rivetta et al. 2013).

2.A.72.3.3.name: High affinity K+ uptake transporter, Hak1, of 775 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.72.3.3.description: High affinity K+ uptake transporter, Hak1, of 775 aas and 12 TMSs. It is involved in drought resistance and is influenced by the H+-ATPases, HA1 and HA2 (see TC# 3.A.3.3.9) (Cai et al. 2019).

2.A.72.3.4.name: Low affinity, Na+-sensitive K+ uptake transporter (vacuolar ?)
2.A.72.3.4.description: Low affinity, Na+-sensitive K+ uptake transporter (vacuolar ?)

2.A.72.3.5.name: Dominant K+ uptake porter, Hak1 (47% identical to 3.A.72.3.4; 822aas)
2.A.72.3.5.description: Dominant K+ uptake porter, Hak1 (47% identical to 3.A.72.3.4; 822aas) (Garciadeblas et al., 2007)

2.A.72.3.6.name: High affinity K+ transporter, HAKCV (expressed at an early stage during viral infection).
2.A.72.3.6.description: High affinity K+ transporter, HAKCV (expressed at an early stage during viral infection) (Greiner et al., 2011).
2.A.72.3.6.proteins: HAKCV of Paramecium bursaria Chlorella virus (A7J6G4)

2.A.72.3.7.name: Potassium transporter 1 (OsHAK1)
2.A.72.3.7.proteins: HAK1 of Oryza sativa subsp. japonica

2.A.72.3.9.name: High affinity potassium transporter 5, HAK5.
2.A.72.3.9.description: High affinity potassium transporter 5, HAK5 (Nieves-Cordones et al. 2014). It is essential for seed development and postgermination growth in low potassium (Pyo et al. 2010) and probably plays a role in drought resistance (Cai et al. 2019). In rice, it alters the cell architecture via ATP-dependent transmembrane auxin transport (Yang et al. 2020).

2.A.73.name: The Short Chain Fatty Acid Uptake (AtoE) Family

2.A.73.1.1.name: Short chain C4 - C6) fatty acid uptake permease, AtoE.
2.A.73.1.1.description: Short chain C4 - C6) fatty acid uptake permease, AtoE. Encoded in the atoDAEB operon which is inducible by exogenous acetoacetate but not by other saturated short chain fatty acids such as butyrate and valerate (Jenkins and Nunn 1987; Matta et al. 2007).

2.A.73.1.2.name: Putative short chain fatty acid (SCFA) transporter of 464 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.73.1.2.description: Putative short chain fatty acid (SCFA) transporter of 464 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.74.name: The 4 TMS Multidrug Endosomal Transporter (MET) Family

2.A.75.1.1.name: D- and L-lysine, L-histidine and L-arginine exporter (LysE).
2.A.75.1.1.description: D- and L-lysine, L-histidine and L-arginine exporter (LysE) (Stäbler et al. 2011). The system may also export L-citrulline (Lubitz et al. 2016).

2.A.75.1.2.name: L-arginine exporter (ArgO or YggA).
2.A.75.1.2.description: L-arginine exporter (ArgO or YggA) (Nandineni and Gowrishankar 2004). ArgP-ArgO of E. coli exhibits transcriptional cross activity with the corresponding pair, LysG-LysE of Corynebacterium glutamicum (Marbaniang and Gowrishankar 2012). ArgO when overproducted confers sensitivity to the toxic arginine analogue, canavanine and catalyzes export of L-lysine (Pathania and Sardesai 2015). ArgO assumes…

2.A.75.1.4.name: Canavanine exporter of 202 aas and 6 TMSs, MsiA, promoting canavanine resistance.
2.A.75.1.4.description: Canavanine exporter of 202 aas and 6 TMSs, MsiA, promoting canavanine resistance (Cai et al. 2009). Canavanine is a plant product present in seeds and plant exudates.

2.A.76.1.1.name: Homoserine/homoserine lactone/β-hydroxynorvaline efflux permease (probable substrate:H+ antiporter), RhtB (YigK).
2.A.76.1.1.description: Homoserine/homoserine lactone/β-hydroxynorvaline efflux permease (probable substrate:H+ antiporter), RhtB (YigK). Expression is under the control of the leucine-responsive protein, Lrp, and amino acids in the medium (Kutukova et al. 2005).

2.A.76.1.10.name: RhtB family porter of 210 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.76.1.10.description: RhtB family porter of 210 aas and 6 TMSs. Based on homology, may export serine, threonine, homoserine and/or homoserine lactones. Possibly regulated by a LysR transcription factor. The gene maps adjacent to a probable heterodimeric DMT superfamily transporter (2.A.7.21.5).
2.A.76.1.10.proteins: RhtB family homologue of Klebsiella oxytoca

2.A.76.1.11.name: Amino acid exporter of 210 aas and 6 TMSs, MrsC.
2.A.76.1.11.description: Amino acid exporter of 210 aas and 6 TMSs, MrsC. Encoded by the mrsC gene in an operon for the biosynthesis of the toxic amino acid analogue, 3-methyarginine, the likely substrate (Braun et al. 2010). The epiphytic Pseudomonas syringae strain which produces and excretes 3-methyarginine does so to compete with pathogenic strains of P. syringae for which 3-methyarginine is toxic.

2.A.76.1.2.name: Threonine efflux permease (probable threonine:H+ antiporter), RhtC (YigJ).
2.A.76.1.2.description: Threonine efflux permease (probable threonine:H+ antiporter), RhtC (YigJ). Expression is under the control of the leucine-responsive protein, Lrp, and amino acids in the medium (Kutukova et al. 2005). Mutation of the rhtC gene can protect cells against toxic levels of threonine (Radi et al. 2022).

2.A.76.1.3.name: Probable amino acid exporter, YahN or YhaM, of 233 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.76.1.3.description: Probable amino acid exporter, YahN or YhaM, of 233 aas and 6 TMSs. Expression is under the control of the leucine-responsive protein, Lrp, and amino acids in the medium (Kutukova et al. 2005). The yahOM operon is induced by cysteine where the cysteine sensor is the DecR/YbaO protein, and this operon is involved in L-cysteine detoxification (Shimada et al. 2016).

2.A.76.1.4.name: O-aetylserine/cysteine/azaserine exporter, EamB or YfiK of 195 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.76.1.4.description: O-aetylserine/cysteine/azaserine exporter, EamB or YfiK of 195 aas and 6 TMSs (Franke et al., 2003). High level cell-free expression and specific labeling of EamB of E. coli has been achieved (Klammt et al. 2004).
2.A.76.1.4.proteins: EamB or YfiK of E. coli

2.A.76.1.5.name: The leucine exporter (LeuE; YeaS).
2.A.76.1.5.description: The leucine exporter (LeuE; YeaS) (binds and probably transports L-methionine, L-histidine, L-α-amino-n-butyrate, norleucine, azaleucine, S(2-aminoethyl)-L-cysteine, 3,4-dehydro-DL-proline, L-alanine, and both D- and L-valine) (Kutukova et al., 2005; Hori et al., 2011; Radi et al. 2022). Expression is under the control of the leucine-responsive protein, Lrp, and amino acids in the medium…

2.A.76.1.7.name: Putative amino acid exporter of 208 aas; RhtB family member; similar to 2.A.76.1.5.
2.A.76.1.7.description: Putative amino acid exporter of 208 aas; RhtB family member; similar to 2.A.76.1.5.
2.A.76.1.7.proteins: RhtB family member of Bacillus subtilis

2.A.76.1.8.name: Putative amino acid efflux porter of 210 aas, YrhP.
2.A.76.1.8.description: Putative amino acid efflux porter of 210 aas, YrhP. Most similar to 2.A.76.1.5 of the characterized proteins in TCDB.

2.A.76.1.9.name: Exporter for L-homoserine, L-serine, and L-homoserine lactone as well as the quorum-sensing pimaricin-inducer PI-factor, PimT.
2.A.76.1.9.description: Exporter for L-homoserine, L-serine, and L-homoserine lactone as well as the quorum-sensing pimaricin-inducer PI-factor (2,3-diamino-2,3-bis(hydroxymethyl)-1,4-butanediol), PimT (Vicente et al. 2009).

2.A.76.2.1.name: Potential coronamic acid exporter of 236 aas and 5 TMSs.
2.A.76.2.1.description: Potential coronamic acid exporter of 236 aas and 5 TMSs. Coronamic acid (CMA), an ethylcyclopropyl amino acid derived from isoleucine, functions as an intermediate in the biosynthesis of coronatine, a chlorosis-inducing phytotoxin produced by Pseudomonas syringae pv. glycinea PG4180. The DNA required for CMA biosynthesisincludes three distinct open reading frames (ORFs) which share a common…

2.A.76.2.2.name: CmaU of 203 aas and 5 or 6 TMSs.
2.A.76.2.2.description: CmaU of 203 aas and 5 or 6 TMSs. This protein resembles 2.A.76.2.1; one or the other may be an incomplete or inaccurate sequence.

2.A.76.2.3.name: CmaU homologue of 203 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.76.2.3.description: CmaU homologue of 203 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.78.name: The Branched Chain Amino Acid Exporter (LIV-E) Family

2.A.78.1.1.name: Branched chain amino acid efflux pump, AzlCD (extrudes azaleucine)
2.A.78.1.1.description: Branched chain amino acid efflux pump, AzlCD (extrudes azaleucine)

2.A.78.1.2.name: Branched chain amino acid efflux pump, BrnEF (extrudes L-methionine, L-isoleucine, L-leucine and L-valine).
2.A.78.1.2.description: Branched chain amino acid efflux pump, BrnEF (extrudes L-methionine, L-isoleucine, L-leucine and L-valine) (Trötschel et al., 2005). Its deletion results in a slight increase (13%) in lysine production and a decrease in cell mass (Xiao et al. 2020).
2.A.78.1.2.proteins: BrnEF of Corynebacterium glutamicum; BrnE (AAM46685); BrnF (AAM46686)

2.A.78.1.3.name: L-Methionine efflux pump (probably exports other neutral, hydrophobic amino acids as well; R. Figge, personal communication)
2.A.78.1.3.description: L-Methionine efflux pump (probably exports other neutral, hydrophobic amino acids as well; R. Figge, personal communication)
2.A.78.1.3.proteins: YgaZH of E. coli; YgaZ (P76630); YgaH (P43667)

2.A.78.2.1.name: AzlCD homologues of 6 and 3 TMSs, respectively.
2.A.78.2.1.description: AzlCD homologues of 6 and 3 TMSs, respectively.
2.A.78.2.1.proteins: AzlCD of Roseobacter sp. SK209-2-6; AzlC (A4EZB2); AzlD (A4EZB3)

2.A.78.2.3.name: Putative AzlCD amino acid exporter
2.A.78.2.3.proteins: AzlCD of Myxococcus xanthus AzlC (Q1D212) AzlD (Q1D213)

2.A.79.1.1.name: Threonine/Serine exporter, ThrE
2.A.79.1.1.description: Threonine/Serine exporter, ThrE (10 TMSs; DUF1212; Eggeling & Sahm, 2003)

2.A.79.1.5.name: Putative 2-component glycine/alanine porter
2.A.79.1.5.proteins: Putative gly/ala porter of Treponema denticola

2.A.79.2.1.name: YjjP /YjjB (P0ADD2) are of 256 aas and 5 TMSs; and of 157 aas and 4 or 5 TMSs, respectively. yjjPB gene expression is regulated by HNS and LeuO.
2.A.79.2.1.description: YjjP (P0ADD5)/YjjB (P0ADD2) are of 256 aas and 5 TMSs; (DUF1212) and of 157 aas and 4 or 5 TMSs, respectively. yjjPB gene expression is regulated by HNS (a repressor) and LeuO (which antagonizes the repressive activity of HNS) (Stratmann et al. 2008). These proteins are encoded within a two gene operon, yjjPB, which encodes a two component dicarboxylate (succinate, fumarate and malate)…

2.A.8.1.1.name: D-Gluconate:H+ symporter of 448 aas and 11 TMSs.
2.A.8.1.1.description: D-Gluconate:H+ symporter of 448 aas and 11 TMSs. It is encoded in an operon with gluconate kinase (Fujita et al. 1986).

2.A.8.1.10.name: D-glycerate transporter of 430 aas and 14 putative TMSs.
2.A.8.1.10.description: D-glycerate transporter of 430 aas and 14 putative TMSs. The gene is next to and probably in the same operon with a gene encoding D-glycerate kinase.

2.A.8.1.11.name: Putative gluconate analog transporter of 449 aas and 11 TMSs, YjhF.
2.A.8.1.11.description: Putative gluconate analog transporter of 449 aas and 11 TMSs, YjhF.

2.A.8.1.12.name: The putative histidine porter, YuiF.
2.A.8.1.12.description: The putative histidine porter, YuiF. Regulated by Histidine repressor HisR (Ravcheev et al. 2011)

2.A.8.1.13.name: A putative propionate/butyrate/hydroxybutyrate transporter
2.A.8.1.13.proteins: Putative propionate permease of Fusobacterium nucleatum (gi 19704150)

2.A.8.1.15.name: Gluconate porter of 463 aas and 13 TMSs, GntP.
2.A.8.1.15.description: Gluconate porter of 463 aas and 13 TMSs, GntP (Letek et al. 2006; Porco et al. 2008).

2.A.8.1.2.name: L-Idonate/D-Gluconate:H+ symporter, IdnT, GntW, YjgT, of 439 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.
2.A.8.1.2.description: L-Idonate/D-Gluconate:H+ symporter, IdnT, GntW, YjgT, of 439 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs. Also called the GNT-II system (Bausch et al., 1998; Gómez et al. 2011).

2.A.8.1.3.name: D-Fructuronate/D-gluconate:H+ symporter, GntP
2.A.8.1.3.description: D-Fructuronate/D-gluconate:H+ symporter, GntP (Bates Utz et al., 2004)

2.A.8.1.4.name: High affinity D-Gluconate:H+ symporter, GntT (GntM, UsgA, YhgC) of 438 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.
2.A.8.1.4.description: High affinity D-Gluconate:H+ symporter, GntT (GntM, UsgA, YhgC) of 438 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs (Porco et al., 1997). It is regulated at the transcriptional level by GntR and Crp (Peekhaus and Conway 1998).

2.A.8.1.5.name: The D-serine transporter, DsdX (KM=60µM) (may also transport D-threonine which inhibits D-serine uptake).
2.A.8.1.5.description: The D-serine transporter, DsdX (KM=60µM) (may also transport D-threonine which inhibits D-serine uptake) (Anfora and Welch, 2006). Eliminating the dsdX gene renders the cell more sensitive to chloramphenicol (Duo et al. 2008).

2.A.8.1.6.name: The putative D-glycerate transporter, GrtP.
2.A.8.1.6.description: The putative D-glycerate transporter, GrtP. Regulated by glycerate-responsive regulator SdaR (Rodionov et al. 2011)

2.A.8.1.8.name: Low-affinity (212 μM), gluconate-inducible, gluconate transporter (gluconate permease) (GntU/the Gnt-I system).
2.A.8.1.8.description: Low-affinity (212 μM), gluconate-inducible, gluconate transporter (gluconate permease) (GntU/the Gnt-I system) (Tong et al. 1996). The gntU gene is in an operon with gntK, encoding a gluconate kinase (Tong et al. 1996). This system has been utilized for the production of pyruvate from gluconate (Yang et al. 2017).

2.A.80.1.1.name: The tricarboxylate transporter, TctABC.
2.A.80.1.1.description: The tricarboxylate transporter, TctABC (Somers and Kay 1983; Winnen et al. 2003). The high resolution structure of the receptor, TctC, is known (Sweet et al. 1984).
2.A.80.1.1.proteins: TctABC of Salmonella enterica; TctA (M, 12 TMS); TctB (M, 4 TMS); TctC (R)

2.A.80.1.2.name: Terephthalate (TPA) aromatic acid uptake transport system, TpiBA/TphC.
2.A.80.1.2.description: Terephthalate (TPA) aromatic acid uptake transport system, TpiBA/TphC (Hosaka et al. 2013). May transport several aromatic acids including isophthalate, o-phthalate and protocatechuate. Consists of three subunits: TpiB (503 aas and 13 TMSs), TpiA (162 aas and 4-5 TMSs) and TphC (322 aas and 1 TMS. tpiAB comprise an operon while tphC maps elsewhere. o-phthalate and protocatecuate may use other…
2.A.80.1.2.proteins: TpiBA/TphC of Comamonas sp. strain E6; TpiB (M, large) (S6BBY9); TpiA (M, small) (S6CBZ0); TphC (R)

2.A.80.1.3.name: The putative tricarboxylic acid transporter, TctABC.
2.A.80.1.3.description: The putative tricarboxylic acid transporter, TctABC. This organism is claimed to have 66 TCT family members (Ma et al. 2009). The organism utilizes many aromatic and non-aromatic acids that could be substrates of these transporters.
2.A.80.1.3.proteins: TctABC of Comamonas testosteroni; TctA (M, large) (D0J0R9); TctB (M, small) (D0J2J4); TctC (R) (D0J060)

2.A.80.1.4.name: Pmf-dependent citrate uptake porter, TctABC.
2.A.80.1.4.description: Pmf-dependent citrate uptake porter, TctABC (Brocker et al. 2009).
2.A.80.1.4.proteins: TctABC of Corynebacterium glutamicum; TctA (M, large; 510 aas) (S5Y5N9); TctB (M, small; 188 aas) (S5XH28); TctC (R) (334 aas) (S5XTE7)

2.A.83.1.1.name: The HCO3-:Na+ symporter, SbtA.
2.A.83.1.1.description: The HCO3-:Na+ symporter, SbtA. Has a 10 TMS topology with two 5 + 5 repeats (Price et al., 2011) and bothe the N- and C-termini outside (Price and Howitt 2014).

2.A.84.1.2.name: The apple chloroplast maltose exporter, Mex.
2.A.84.1.2.description: The apple chloroplast maltose exporter, Mex (Reidel et al., 2008).

2.A.84.1.3.name: Hypothetical protein of 370 aas
2.A.84.1.3.proteins: Hypothetical protein of Synechococcus sp. PCC 7002 (B1XHU2)

2.A.85.1.1.name: Inner membrane protein, YccS, of unknown specificity but of 717 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement, each followed by an ~ 200 aa hydrophilic…
2.A.85.1.1.description: Inner membrane protein, YccS, of unknown specificity but of 717 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement, each followed by an ~ 200 aa hydrophilic domain.

2.A.85.1.2.name: p-hydroxybenzoate efflux carrier, AaeB.
2.A.85.1.2.description: p-hydroxybenzoate efflux carrier, AaeB (Van Dyk et al., 2004). Several aromatic carboxylic acids serve as inducers of yhcRQP operon expression.

2.A.85.1.4.name: Fusaric acid resistance protein
2.A.85.1.4.proteins: Fusaric acid resistance protein of Pantoea sp. aB (E0M081)

2.A.85.2.1.name: An inorganic anion (Cl-/NO3-) transporter, ALMT12 or QUAC1, reported to be incapable of transporting organic anions, is involved in stomatal closure.
2.A.85.2.1.description: An inorganic anion (Cl-/NO3-) transporter, ALMT12 or QUAC1 (Quickly activating Anion Channel 1), reported to be incapable of transporting organic anions, is involved in stomatal closure (Sasaki et al, 2010). It is an R-type inorganic anion channel required for stomatal movement in Arabidopsis guard cells (Meyer et al., 2010). The C-terminal cytosolic domain mediates voltage gating (Mumm et al…

2.A.85.2.4.name: The anion-selective transporter ALMT1 (transports anions) (35% identical to 2.A.85.2.3)
2.A.85.2.4.description: The anion-selective transporter ALMT1 (transports anions) (35% identical to 2.A.85.2.3) (Pineros et al., 2008)

3.A.1.204.23.description: Homo dimeric plasma membrane AbcG1 half ABC transporter of 633 aas and 6 TMSs. Actively exports volatile organic compounds (Benzenoids and phenylpropanoids such as methylbenzoate and benzyl alcohol, major VOC constituents emitted by flowers) from the flower cell cytoplasm to the external environment (Adebesin et al. 2017). May also export alcohol glycosides. Up regulated 100-fold in petunia…

3.A.1.204.24.name: Wax precursor (cuticular lipid) exporter of 678 aas and 6 TMSs, AbcG13.
3.A.1.204.24.description: Wax precursor (cuticular lipid) exporter of 678 aas and 6 TMSs, AbcG13 (Adebesin et al. 2017).

3.A.1.204.25.name: ABCG6 of 546 aas and 4 TMSs involved in phosholipid trafficing and drug export in Leishmania tarentolae.
3.A.1.204.25.description: ABCG6 of 546 aas and 4 TMSs involved in phosholipid trafficing and drug export in Leishmania tarentolae (Gonzalez-Lobato et al. 2016).

3.A.1.204.26.name: ABC transporter G family member 26, ABCG.26; AtABCG26 of 685 aas and 6 TMSs.
3.A.1.204.26.description: ABC transporter G family member 26, ABCG.26; AtABCG26 of 685 aas and 6 TMSs. Putative white-brown complex homolog protein 27. May function in vacuolar arsenic accumulation with potential for bioremediation (Potdukhe et al. 2018). Calcium-mediated mitigation strategies and novel approaches to alleviate arsenic induced plant stress have been reviewed (Faizan et al. 2025).

3.A.1.204.27.name: Multidrug resistancd protein, ABCG19 (Wbc19), of 725 aas and 6 TMSs with a domain order C-M. Confers resistance to kanamycin.
3.A.1.204.27.description: Multidrug resistancd protein, ABCG19 (Wbc19), of 725 aas and 6 TMSs with a domain order C-M. Confers resistance to kanamycin (Mentewab and Stewart 2005).

3.A.1.204.28.name: ABCG25 of 662 aas and 6 TMSs in a C-M domain arrangement.
3.A.1.204.28.description: ABCG25 of 662 aas and 6 TMSs in a C-M domain arrangement. Transports abscisic acid, ABA, a plant hormone that influences developmental processes, including seed and bud dormancy, the control of organ size and stomatal closure (Lefèvre and Boutry 2018). Strigolactones promote the localisation of the ABA exporter ABCG25 at the plasma membrane in root epidermal cells of Arabidopsis thaliana (Russo…

3.A.1.204.29.name: ABCG14 of 648 aas and 6 TMSs in a C + M domain arrangement.
3.A.1.204.29.description: ABCG14 of 648 aas and 6 TMSs in a C + M domain arrangement. May transport cytokinins (Lefèvre and Boutry 2018).

3.A.1.204.30.name: ABCG16 of 736 aas and 6 TMSs in a C-M domain arrangement.
3.A.1.204.30.description: ABCG16 of 736 aas and 6 TMSs in a C-M domain arrangement. Transports jasmonic acid (Lefèvre and Boutry 2018; An et al. 2026).

3.A.1.204.36.name: AbcG4 of 549 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs (domain order C-M).
3.A.1.204.36.description: AbcG4 of 549 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs (domain order C-M). Insecticides, including permethrin and other pyrethroids, are exported by ABCG4, which is also up-regulated in response to insecticide treatments (Negri et al. 2019).
3.A.1.204.36.proteins: AbcG4 of Anopheles stephensi (a mosquito malaria vector)

3.A.1.204.38.name: ABC transporter (exporter) of 1109 aas and 7 - 9 TMSs in a 1 + 1 or 2 + 5 or 6 TMS arrangement.
3.A.1.204.38.description: ABC transporter (exporter) of 1109 aas and 7 - 9 TMSs in a 1 + 1 or 2 + 5 or 6 TMS arrangement. It is a phytohormone transporter. Reduction of its gene expression level was linked to the dwarfing phenotype in apple rootstocks. MdABCG28 overexpression promoted shoot growth of atabcg14 mutants (Feng et al. 2019). It is upregulated by low temperature in the pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) (Niu et al…

3.A.1.204.4.name: The plant cuticular wax and/or lipid metabolite exporter, CER5; ABCG12; WBC12.
3.A.1.204.4.description: The plant cuticular wax and/or lipid metabolite exporter, CER5; ABCG12; WBC12 (in the plasma membrane of epidermal cells; secretes wax to the plant surface) (Pighin et al., 2004; Panikashvili and Aharoni 2008Panikashvili and Aharoni 2008).

3.A.1.204.42.name: ABC transporter G family member 10, ABCG10, of 590 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs.
3.A.1.204.42.description: ABC transporter G family member 10, ABCG10, of 590 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs. In Medicago truncatula, the ortholog transports 4-coumarate and liquiritigenin, representing key branching points in the phenylpropanoid pathway, and possibly other lignin-derived aromatic compounds such as the phenylpropanoid-derived phytoalexin (Biala et al. 2017).

3.A.1.204.43.name: ABCG! or ABCG2 of 660 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs (C-M domain order).
3.A.1.204.43.description: ABCG! or ABCG2 of 660 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs (C-M domain order). It may be a cell metabolite exporter (Wunderlich 2022).

3.A.1.204.44.name: Drug resistance ABC exporter, NpABC2, of 1092 aas and 8 - 10 TMSs in a 1 (N-terminus) + 1 + 6 - 8 TMS (C-terminus) arrangement.
3.A.1.204.44.description: Drug resistance ABC exporter, NpABC2, of 1092 aas and 8 - 10 TMSs in a 1 (N-terminus) + 1 + 6 - 8 TMS (C-terminus) arrangement. NpABC2 plays a role in the drug resistance of N. parvum and affects its virulence (Chen et al. 2022).
3.A.1.204.44.proteins: NpABC2 of Botryosphaeria parva (strain UCR-NP2) (Grapevine canker fungus) (Neofusicoccum parvum)

3.A.1.204.46.name: ABCG24 of 1109 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs.
3.A.1.204.46.description: ABCG24 of 1109 aas and 6 C-terminal TMSs. Exports absscisic acid (An et al. 2026).

3.A.1.204.5.name: The ABCG5 /ABCG8 heterodimeric neutral sterol exporter; present in the apical membranes of enterocytes and hepatocytes, the NBD-TMD interface, and…
3.A.1.204.5.description: The ABCG5 (sterolin-1)/ABCG8 (sterolin-2) heterodimeric neutral sterol (cholesterol and plant sterols) (e.g., sitosterol and lutein) (phosphoryl donors ATP > CTP > GTP > UTP) exporter; present in the apical membranes of enterocytes and hepatocytes ((Reboul 2013). Cholesteryl oleate, phosphatidyl choline and enantiomeric cholesterol are poorly transported (mutation of either ABCG5 or ABCG8 cause…
3.A.1.204.5.proteins: ABCG5/ABCG8 of Homo sapiens; ABCG5 (Q9H222); ABCG8 (Q9H221)

3.A.1.204.6.name: The efflux porter for phosphatidylcholine and its analogues as well as toxic alkyl phospholipids, ABCG4.
3.A.1.204.6.description: The efflux porter for phosphatidylcholine and its analogues as well as toxic alkyl phospholipids, ABCG4 (Castanys-Munoz et al., 2007). Also promotes cholesterol efflux to the mature forms of HDL (HDL2 and HDL3) (Voloshyna and Reiss, 2011).

3.A.1.204.7.name: Multidrug resistance efflux pump, AbcG6, causes camptothecin-resistant parasites
3.A.1.204.7.description: Multidrug resistance efflux pump, AbcG6, causes camptothecin-resistant parasites (Bosedasgupta et al., 2008)

3.A.1.204.8.name: The epidermal plasma membrane cuticular lipid exporters, ABCG11/ABCG11 and ABCG11/ABCG12; ABCG11 is also called Wbc11; Desperado (DSO); COF1; PEL1.
3.A.1.204.8.description: The epidermal plasma membrane cuticular lipid (wax) exporters, ABCG11/ABCG11 and ABCG11/ABCG12; ABCG11 is also called Wbc11; Desperado (DSO); COF1; PEL1. ABCG12 is also called CER5, WBC12 and D3 (Panikashvili and Aharoni 2008). Required for the cuticle and pollen coat development by controlling cutin and possibly wax transport to the extracellular matrix. Involved in developmental plasticity and…

3.A.1.204.9.name: The putative multidrug/pigment exporter, Adp1
3.A.1.204.9.description: The putative multidrug/pigment exporter, Adp1 (Lamping et al., 2010)

3.A.1.205.1.name: Pleiotropic drug resistance exporter; steroid exporter; sporidesmin toxicity suppressor; MDR; cyclic nucleotide exporter; amphipathic anion exporter.
3.A.1.205.1.description: Pleiotropic drug resistance (PDR; Pdr5) exporter; steroid exporter; sporidesmin toxicity suppressor (Sts1); MDR; cyclic nucleotide exporter; amphipathic anion exporter. Its ATPase activity is inhibited by its substrate, clotrimazole; can use ATP, GTP and maybe UTP to drive efflux (Golin et al., 2007). Molecular modeling revealed aspects of the binding pocket and mechanism of action (Rutledge et…

3.A.1.205.10.name: Pleiotropic drug resistance (PDR) exporter, named ABCG40, PDR9 or PDR12, 1423 aas with 12 - 14 TMSs.
3.A.1.205.10.description: Pleiotropic drug resistance (PDR) exporter, named ABCG40, PDR9 or PDR12, 1423 aas with 12 - 14 TMSs. It functions as a pump to exclude Pb2+ ions and/or Pb2+- containing toxin compounds) (Lee et al., 2005). It may also export abscisic acid (ABA) (Lefèvre and Boutry 2018).

3.A.1.205.11.name: The brefeldin resistance protein, Bfr1, (also exports actinomycin D, cerulenin, and cytochalasin B).
3.A.1.205.11.description: The brefeldin resistance protein, Bfr1, (also exports actinomycin D, cerulenin, and cytochalasin B) (Turi and Rose, 1995; Nagao et al., 1995).

3.A.1.205.13.name: The putative sterol uptake transporter, Aus1.
3.A.1.205.13.description: The putative sterol uptake transporter, Aus1. It also protects against antifungal azoles such as fluconazole and itraconazole (Nakayama et al. 2007).

3.A.1.205.15.name: Anaerobically-induced AusI.
3.A.1.205.15.description: Anaerobically-induced AusI. Specifically stimulated by phosphatidylserine in proteoliposomes. May translocate cholestrol and derivatives (Marek et al., 2011).

3.A.1.205.16.name: ABCG32/PEC1 transporter.
3.A.1.205.16.description: ABCG32/PEC1 transporter. Required for plant cuticle production (Bessire et al. 2011).

3.A.1.205.17.name: ABC transporter, PDR1 of 1452 aas and 12 or 14 TMSs in a repeated 6 or 7 TMS CMCM arrangement.
3.A.1.205.17.description: ABC transporter, PDR1 of 1452 aas and 12 or 14 TMSs in a repeated 6 or 7 TMS CMCM arrangement. Secretes phytohormones such as strigolactones that regulate plant shoot architecture and stimulate germination (Kretzschmar et al. 2012; Demurtas et al. 2020).

3.A.1.205.18.name: The monolignol (p-coumaryl alcohol) transporter, ABCG29 or PDR1.
3.A.1.205.18.description: The monolignol (p-coumaryl alcohol) transporter, ABCG29 or PDR1. In addition to this precursor of lignin biosynthesis, this transporter may transport various phenolic compounds and glucosinolates (Alejandro et al. 2012). Reported to be required for normal meiotic double strand DNA break formation resulting from interaction with SPO11-1 (De Muyt et al. 2007).

3.A.1.205.19.name: Small molecule transporter, ABCG10.
3.A.1.205.19.description: Small molecule transporter, ABCG10. Poorly expressed in an lrrB mutant (Sugden et al. 2010).

3.A.1.205.20.name: TUR2 transporter.
3.A.1.205.20.description: TUR2 transporter. May be a general defense protein. Involved in turion (dormant buds) formation. Confers resistance to the diterpenoid antifungal agent sclareol (van den Brûle et al. 2002). Induced by abiotic stresses such as cold-stress, cycloheximide and sodium chloride (NaCl). Induction by abscisic acid (ABA) is repressed by cytokinin such as kinetin (Crouzet et al. 2006).

3.A.1.205.21.name: ABC1 transporter.
3.A.1.205.21.description: ABC1 transporter. Excretes secondary metabolites such as terpenes. Involved in both constitutive and jasmonic acid-dependent induced defense. Secretes the terpenes, sclareol and sclareolide and thereby confers resistance to the fungus, B.cinerea (Stukkens et al. 2005). Induced by sclareolide and sclareol, and by some phytohormones such as jasmonic acid (JA) and ethylene. Strongly induced by…

3.A.1.205.22.name: Plasma membrane ABC family G member 39 (ABCG39; PDR11) paraquot uptake transporter of 1454 aas and 12 - 16 TMSs.
3.A.1.205.22.description: Plasma membrane ABC family G member 39 (ABCG39; PDR11) paraquot uptake transporter of 1454 aas and 12 - 16 TMSs. Also called pleiotropic drug resistance protein, PDR11 or PDR13 (Fujita and Shinozaki 2014). It may export a variety of xenobiotics (Lefèvre and Boutry 2018).

3.A.1.205.23.name: AbcG34 of 1453 aas and 12 TMSs.
3.A.1.205.23.description: AbcG34 of 1453 aas and 12 TMSs. Secretes a major phytoalexin, camalexin, which on the leaf surface protects the plant against necrotophic pathogens (Khare et al. 2017). Also protects against the antifungal agent, sclareol. AtABCG34 expression was induced by Abrassicicola inoculation as well as by methyl-jasmonate, a defense-related phytohormone, and AtABCG34 was polarly localized at the external…

3.A.1.205.24.name: Multidrug resistance (MDR) exporter, (Np)AbcG5/PDR5 of 1498 aas and 12 TMSs.
3.A.1.205.24.description: Multidrug resistance (MDR) exporter, (Np)AbcG5/PDR5 of 1498 aas and 12 TMSs. NpABCG5/NpPDR5 is barely expressed in leaf tissues under normal conditions, but its expression is induced by the biotic stress hormone methyl jasmonate, or when tissues are wounded or chewed by an insect. NpABCG5/NpPDR5 confers resistance to the herbivore Manduca sexta (Toussaint et al. 2017). The same system, ABCG5 of…
3.A.1.205.24.proteins: PDR5 of Nicotiana plumbaginifolia (Leadwort-leaved tobacco) (Tex-Mex tobacco)

3.A.1.205.25.name: Plasma membrane ABCG1 or PDR1a of 1434 aas and 12 TMSs.
3.A.1.205.25.description: Plasma membrane ABCG1 or PDR1a of 1434 aas and 12 TMSs. 85% identical to TC# 3.A.1.205.21. PDR1 secretes plastid-produced diterpene(s) that are the antimicrobial compounds active in preinvasion defense, as well as the sesquiterpenoid, capsidiol, the major phytoalexin produced by Nicotiana and Capsicum species. Capsidiol is produced in plant tissues attacked by pathogens and plays a major role in…

3.A.1.205.26.name: ABC transporter, AtrB or BcatrB, that catalyzes efflux of fungitoxic compounds including the phytoalexin, camalexin.
3.A.1.205.26.description: ABC transporter, AtrB or BcatrB, that catalyzes efflux of fungitoxic compounds including the phytoalexin, camalexin. Camalexin also induces its synthesis (Stefanato et al. 2009). Its fungicide export capacity has been confirmed and extended (Sofianos et al. 2024).
3.A.1.205.26.proteins: AtrB of Botryotinia fuckeliana (Noble rot fungus) (Botrytis cinerea)

3.A.1.205.27.name: Multidrug resistance efflux pump of 1567 aas and 12 TMSs.
3.A.1.205.27.description: Multidrug resistance efflux pump of 1567 aas and 12 TMSs. Probably exports many drugs including griseofulvin, itraconazole, terbinafine and amphotericin B (Martins et al. 2016) (Chen et al. 2023).
3.A.1.205.27.proteins: MDR of Trichophyton rubrum (Athlete's foot fungus)

3.A.1.205.28.name: ABCG30 or PDR2 of 1400 aas and 12 TMSs in a C-M-C-M domain arrangement.
3.A.1.205.28.description: ABCG30 or PDR2 of 1400 aas and 12 TMSs in a C-M-C-M domain arrangement. Responds to abiotic stresses such as heavy metals (Cd2+, Pb2+, etc), and is regulated by hormones related to pathogenic defenses (Crouzet et al. 2006). It may be a heavy metal efflux pump, but may also transport abscisic acid, influencing developmental processes, including seed and bud dormancy, the control of organ size and…

3.A.1.205.29.name: ABCG37 (PDR9; PDR12, ETA4, PIS1) of 1450 aas and 12 TMSs in a CMCM domain arrangement where each M domain contains 6 TMSs.
3.A.1.205.29.description: ABCG37 (PDR9; PDR12, ETA4, PIS1) of 1450 aas and 12 TMSs in a CMCM domain arrangement where each M domain contains 6 TMSs. It confers resistance to auxinic herbicides (Ito and Gray 2006) and contributes oxygenated coumarins to root exudates (Ziegler et al. 2017). It responds to abiotic stresses such as heavy metals (Cd2+ and lead) and is regulated by pathogenic defense hormones (Kim et al. 2007)…

3.A.1.205.3.name: Weak acid exporter, Pdr12p (exports preservative anions including propionate, sorbate and benzoate)
3.A.1.205.3.description: Weak acid exporter, Pdr12p (exports preservative anions including propionate, sorbate and benzoate) (Mollapour et al., 2008)

3.A.1.205.31.name: Pdr18 ABC pump of 1333 aas and 12 TMSs in a C-M-C-M domain arrangement.
3.A.1.205.31.description: Pdr18 ABC pump of 1333 aas and 12 TMSs in a C-M-C-M domain arrangement. It functions to insert sterols such as ergosterol into the membrane, and Pdr18-mediated multistress resistance is linked to the status of plasma membrane lipid environment related with ergosterol content and the associated plasma membrane properties (Godinho et al. 2018).

3.A.1.205.32.name: MDR exporter, TmrMDR3, of 1503 aas and 12 TMSs in a C-M-C-M domain arrangement.
3.A.1.205.32.description: MDR exporter, TmrMDR3, of 1503 aas and 12 TMSs in a C-M-C-M domain arrangement. Four ABC transporters (TruMDR1, TruMDR2, TruMDR3, and TruMDR5) and a second MFS transporter (TruMFS2) proved to be able to operate as azole efflux pumps. Milbemycin oxime inhibited only TruMDR3. TruMDR3 transports voriconazole (VRC) and itraconazole (ITC), while TruMDR2 transports only ITC. Disruption of TruMDR3…

3.A.1.205.33.name: Cordecepin/Pentostatin transmembrane transporter, Cns4, of 1364 aas and possibly 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 (or 5 + 5) TMS arrangement.
3.A.1.205.33.description: Cordecepin/Pentostatin transmembrane transporter, Cns4, of 1364 aas and possibly 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 (or 5 + 5) TMS arrangement. It is an ABC-type transporter; part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of cordycepin (COR) and pentostatin (PTN), two adenosine analogs with related bioactivity profiles as both mimic adenosine and can inhibit some of the processes that are adenosine…
3.A.1.205.33.proteins: Cns4 of Cordyceps militaris (strain CM01) (Caterpillar fungus)

3.A.1.205.34.name: ABCG39 K+ transporter, TPK1 or ABCG39 of 1423 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
3.A.1.205.34.description: ABCG39 K+ transporter, TPK1 or ABCG39 of 1423 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

3.A.1.205.4.name: Multidrug resistance protein, Cdr1 of 1501 aas and 14 TMSs in a CMCM arrangement with each M domain having 7 TMSs in a 6 + 1 TMS arrangement.
3.A.1.205.4.description: Multidrug resistance protein, Cdr1 (Candida drug resistance 1) of 1501 aas and 14 TMSs in a CMCM arrangement with each M domain having 7 TMSs in a 6 + 1 TMS arrangement. It confers resistance to cycloheximide, xenobiotics and antifungal agents such as azoles and terbinafine (Holmes et al., 2006; Schuetzer-Muehlbauer et al., 2003); also, transports phospholipids (Shukla et al., 2007). It is the…

3.A.1.205.5.name: Multidrug resistance protein, Cdr2.
3.A.1.205.5.description: Multidrug resistance protein, Cdr2 (confers resistance to azole and other antifungal agents/terbinafine, amorolfine, aspofungin, etc. as well as a variety of metabolic inhibitors) (Schuetzer-Muehlbauer et al., 2003; Basso et al., 2010). Chimeras between Cdr1 an Cdr2 revealed regions determining substrate specificity (Tanabe et al., 2011). Has an external binding site for an inhibiting octapeptide…

3.A.1.205.6.name: Multidrug resistance protein, Cn Afr1 (confers resistance to azole antifungal drugs including fluconazole)
3.A.1.205.6.description: Multidrug resistance protein, Cn Afr1 (confers resistance to azole antifungal drugs including fluconazole) (Posteraro et al., 2003)

3.A.1.205.7.name: The multidrug resistance protein, AtrB.
3.A.1.205.7.description: The multidrug resistance protein, AtrB (confers resistance to all major classes of fungicides as well as natural toxic compounds substrates include: anilinopyrimidine, benzimidazole, phenylpyrrole, phenylpyridylamine, strobirulin, azoles, dicarboximides, quintozene, acriflavin, and rhodamine 6G as well as natural toxins such as camptothecin (an alkaloid) and the stilbene phytoalexin, resveratrol)…

3.A.1.205.8.name: The multidrug resistance protein, Pdr11p, mediates sterol uptake by promoting movement of sterols from the plasma membrane to the endoplasmic…
3.A.1.205.8.description: The multidrug resistance protein, Pdr11p, mediates sterol uptake by promoting movement of sterols from the plasma membrane to the endoplasmic reticulum where esterification occurs (Li and Prinz, 2004).

3.A.1.205.9.name: The plasma membrane Cd2+/Pb2+ efflux pump, PDR8 ABCG36; PEN30, present in root hair and epidermal cells; it may export a broad range of substrates.
3.A.1.205.9.description: The plasma membrane Cd2+/Pb2+ efflux pump (heavy metal resistance pump), PDR8 (ABCG36; PEN30, present in root hair and epidermal cells; it may export a broad range of substrates (Kim et al., 2007). Also reported to transport flavonoid glycosides (phytoalexins) as well as quercitin, kaempeferol, 4-methoxy-indol-3-ylmethylglucosinolate and salicylate (Badri et al. 2012; Stein et al. 2006). Key…

3.A.1.206.name: The a-Factor Sex Pheromone Exporter (STE) Family (ABCB)

3.A.1.206.1.name: a-Factor sex pheromone (a hydrophobic isoprenylated (farnesylated) carboxymethylated peptide) exporter, Ste6.
3.A.1.206.1.description: a-Factor sex pheromone (a hydrophobic isoprenylated (farnesylated) carboxymethylated peptide) exporter, Ste6 (Michaelis and Barrowman 2012). It has been expressed in Pichia pastoris for structural studies by cryo-EM (Kalavacherla et al. 2023). The proteins in TC family 3.A.1.206 are closely related to those in family 3.A.1.201.

3.A.1.206.2.name: Mating factor M secretion protein, Mam1 of 1336 aas and 13 predicted TMSs.
3.A.1.206.2.description: Mating factor M secretion protein, Mam1 of 1336 aas and 13 predicted TMSs. Mam1 ABC protein is a promiscuous peptide transporter that can accommodate globular proteins of a relatively large size being capable of exporting a mating factor M- GFP fusion protein (Kjaerulff et al. 2005).

3.A.1.208.name: The Drug Conjugate Transporter (DCT) Family (ABCC) (Dębska et al., 2011)

3.A.1.208.1.name: Multi-drug resistance-associated protein, MRP1-like protein (MLP1 or MRP1).
3.A.1.208.1.description: Multi-drug resistance-associated protein, MRP1-like protein (MLP1 or MRP1) (Exporter of leukotrienes, glutathione, methotrexate and cysteinyl conjugates of organic anions, drugs, unmodified hydrophobic xenobiotics and hydrophilic conjugated endobiotics). Vincristine and glutathione are co-transported. MRP1 catalyzes export of glutathione during apoptosis (Hammond et al., 2007). Also transports…

3.A.1.208.11.name: Vacuolar metal resistance and drug detoxification protein, yeast cadmium factor, of 1515 aas and 15 or 16 TMSs in a 5 + 6 + 4 or 5 TMS arrangement…
3.A.1.208.11.description: Vacuolar metal resistance and drug detoxification protein, yeast cadmium factor (YCF1 or Ycf1p), of 1515 aas and 15 or 16 TMSs in a 5 + 6 + 4 or 5 TMS arrangement; it transports cadmium-glutathione conjugates, glutathione S-conjugated leukotriene C4, organic glutathione S-conjugates, selenodigluthatione, unconjugated bilirubin, reduced glutathione, and diazaborine (Lazard et al., 2011). It…

3.A.1.208.13.name: Cyclic nucleotide efflux pump, MRP8; also exports other nucleoside and nucleotide analogues, and confers resistance to fluoropyrimidines and the…
3.A.1.208.13.description: Cyclic nucleotide (cAMP and cGMP) efflux pump, MRP8 (ABCC11); also exports other nucleoside and nucleotide analogues, and confers resistance to fluoropyrimidines and the anti-AIDS drug, 2',3'-dideoxycytidine (Guo et al., 2003). Human earwax consists of wet and dry types. Dry earwax is frequent in East Asians, whereas wet earwax is common in other populations. A SNP, 538G --> A (rs17822931), in…

3.A.1.208.14.name: The vacuole (tonoplast) ZmMrp3 anthocyanin pigment transporter (ABCF)
3.A.1.208.14.description: The vacuole (tonoplast) ZmMrp3 anthocyanin pigment transporter (ABCF) (Goodman et al., 2004)

3.A.1.208.15.name: The general organic anion exporter, MRP5 (MOATC or ABCC5).
3.A.1.208.15.description: The general organic anion exporter, MRP5 (MOATC or ABCC5). It exports cyclic AMP, cyclic GMP, cyclic UMP, cyclicCMP, 5'-FUMP, glutathione and glutathione conjugates, and antimonial tartrate) (Schneider and Seifert 2017). It also transports reduced folates as well as mono-, di- and tri-glutamate derivatives of folic acid and methotrexate (Assaraf et al., 2006). When overexpressed, it can lower the…

3.A.1.208.16.name: The vacuolar Abc2p (SPAC3F10.11c) transporter for xenobiotics, glutathione S-conjugates and monochlorobimane
3.A.1.208.16.description: The vacuolar Abc2p (SPAC3F10.11c) transporter for xenobiotics, glutathione S-conjugates and monochlorobimane (Iwaki et al., 2006)

3.A.1.208.17.name: The vacuolar glutathione-conjugate and chlorophyll catabolite transporter, MRP3.
3.A.1.208.17.description: The vacuolar glutathione-conjugate and chlorophyll catabolite transporter, MRP3 (Tommasini et al., 1998). This protein appears to have an M-M-C-M-C domain order, possibly a characteristic of this ABC subfamily. 3.A.1.211.24.description: ABCF3 or ABC50 of 712 aas and 0 TMSs. ABC50 plays a key role in translation initiation and has functions that are distinct from those of other non-membrane ABC proteins (Paytubi et al. 2009).

3.A.1.211.3.name: Multidrug resistance pump, ABCA2 (ABC2).
3.A.1.211.3.description: Multidrug resistance pump, ABCA2 (ABC2). Mediates trafficking of LDL-derived free cholesterol (Voloshyna and Reiss, 2011). Transports endogenous lipids such as myelin (Soichi et al. 2007). It transports liipids (Wang et al. 2026).

3.A.1.211.4.name: The aced cell death 7 (ced-7) protein.
3.A.1.211.4.description: The aced cell death 7 (ced-7) protein (translocates molecules that mediate adhesion between dying and engulfing embryonic cells during programmed death).

3.A.1.211.5.description: The surfactant-secreting porter, ABCA3 (exports lipids and proteins into lamellar bodies). Fatal surfactant deficiency (FSD) can result from mutations in ABCA3, causing abnormal intracellular localization (type I) or decreased ATP hydrolysis (type II). Other mutations cause pediatric interstitial lung disease (pILD) (Matsumura et al. 2008). ABCA3 is found in lamellar bodies of lung alveolar type…

3.A.1.211.6.name: Xenobiotic transporter, ABCA8.
3.A.1.211.6.description: Xenobiotic transporter, ABCA8. It transports estradiol-β-glucuronide, taurocholate, LTC4, para-amino-hippurate, ochratoxin-A and hydrophilic drugs (Tsuruoka et al., 2002), (Sakamoto et al. 2019). A novel pathway in ABCA8-regulated inhibition of human hepatocellular carcinoma tumorigenesis and metastasis has been identified (Cui et al. 2020).

3.A.1.211.8.description: AbcA12 Keratinocyte lipid transporter. Transports lipids in lamellar granules to the apical surface of granular layer keratinocytes. Extracellular lipids, including ceramide, are thought to be essential for skin barrier function. ABCA12 mutations underlie the three main types of autosomal recessive congenital ichthyoses: harlequin ichthyosis, lamellar ichthyosis and congenital ichthyosiform…

3.A.1.211.9.name: ABCA5 of 1642 aas and 12 TMSs.
3.A.1.211.9.description: ABCA5 of 1642 aas and 12 TMSs. It is related to lysosomal diseases and plays important roles, especially in cardiomyocytes and follicular cells (Kubo et al. 2005). It mediates cholesterol efflux to HDL3 (Voloshyna and Reiss, 2011) and functions in autolysosomes (Sakamoto et al. 2019).

3.A.1.212.1.description: The mitochondrial peptide exporter, Mdl1p (exports peptides of 6-21 amino acyl residues from the mitochondrial matrix as well as degradation products of misassembled respiratory chain complexes) (Janas et al., 2003; van der Does et al., 2006; Gompf et al., 2007). A leaderless Mdl1p targets to the ER membrane instead of to the mitochondria (Gompf et al., 2007).

Genomic analyses of the euryhaline model ciliate Paramecium duboscqui reveal adaptations to environmental salinity via changes in transporter gene expression (Fu et al. 2024).

3.A.3.1.17.description: Na+/K+-ATPase of 1041 aas and 10 TMSs, SCN1A. Domain-specific mutations in the Na+/K+-ATPase α subunit differentially regulate sleep and circadian rhythms in Drosophila melanogaster.

This causes it to have a stoichiometry of 2 Na+ to 1 K+. It is a Na pump with reduced stoichiometry, up-regulated by brine shrimp in extreme salinities (Artigas et al. 2023). ().
